<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:coarse_rigidity_Introduction}
    Let $\mathsf{Q},\mathsf B\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ be inclusions of von Neumann algebras with expectation. We say that $\mathsf{Q}$ is {\em coarsely rigid in $\mathsf{M}$ relative to $\mathsf B$} if for every $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$ and for every  modular derivation $\delta\colon \operatorname{dom}(\delta)\subset L^2(\mathsf{M})\to \mathsf{H}$ with $\mathsf B\subseteq\operatorname{Null}(\bar\delta)$  and ${_\mathsf{M}}\mathsf{H}_\mathsf{M}\prec {_\mathsf{M}}L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes_\mathsf B\mathsf{K}\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M})_\mathsf{M}$ for some $\mathsf B$-$\mathsf B$-correspondence $\mathsf{K}$, we have that $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ converges strongly to the identity on $L^2(\mathsf{Q}^\omega
)$ as $\alpha
\to\infty$. We say that $\mathsf{M}$ is {\em coarsely rigid} if $\mathsf{M}$ is coarsely rigid in $\mathsf{M}$ relative to $\mathbb C$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{main_theorem_amenable_for introduction}
   If $\mathsf B,\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ are inclusions of $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebras with expectations such that $\mathsf B$ is amenable and $\mathsf{Q}$ does not have any non-zero amenable summand, then $\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}$ is coarsely rigid relative to $\mathsf B$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
If $\mathsf{M}$ is  a nonamenable  factor with separable predual which is not full, in particular,  if $\mathsf{M}$ is a type III$_0$ nonamenable factor, then $\mathsf{M}$ is  rigid with respect to modular derivations taking values in mixing weakly coarse correspondences.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:dichotomy result_Introduction}
     Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a diffuse von Neumann algebra with separable predual, and let $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$. Exactly one of the following holds true:
     \begin{enumerate}
         \item $\mathsf{M}$ has a non-zero amenable summand.
         \item For every modular derivation  $\delta:\operatorname{dom}(\delta)\subseteq L^2(\mathsf{M})\to \mathsf{H}$ with $\mathsf{H}\prec L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2(\mathsf{M})$, $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ converges strongly to the identity on $L^2(\mathsf{M}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega)$ as $\alpha\to\infty$.
     \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf A,\mathsf B\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ be  inclusions of $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebras such that   $\mathsf A$ is globally invariant under $\sigma^\varphi$ for some normal faithful state $\varphi$ on $\mathsf{M}$. Then $\mathsf A$ is amenable relative to $\mathsf B$ inside $\mathsf{M}$ if and only if there exists a  state $\psi:\langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle\to \mathbb  C$,  such that $\psi_{|_{\mathsf{M}}}\leq C\varphi$ for some $C>0$, $\psi_{|_{\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})}}$ is faithful and satisfies 
     $\psi(Ta)=\psi(\sigma_i^\varphi(a)T)$
            for $T\in \langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$ and $\sigma^\varphi$-analytic $a\in \mathsf A$.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
In the following examples, for any $\omega\in \beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$,     $\mathsf{M}$ is $\omega$-solid and stably solid relative to $\mathsf B$ along $\omega$.
\begin{itemize}
\item (Theorem \ref{thm:solidity for amalgamated free products}) $\mathsf{M}=\mathsf{M}_1\bar\ast_\mathsf B\mathsf{M}_2$,  where $\mathsf{M}_1,\mathsf{M}_2$ are $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebras with a common von Neumann subalgebra $\mathsf B$ with expectations such that $\mathrm{id}_{L^2(\mathsf{M}_j)}$ is compact relative to $\mathsf B$ for $j=1,2$. 
    \item (Theorem \ref{prop:omega solidity in crossed products}) $\mathsf{M}=\mathsf B\rtimes_{\alpha,\nu}\Gamma$, where $(\alpha,\nu)$ is a cocycle action of a discrete countable group $\Gamma$ on a von Neumann algebra $\mathsf B$  such that $\Gamma$ a proper 1-cocycle $c$ into a representation weakly contained in the left regular representation.
    \item (Corollary \ref{cor:solidity of free Araki-Woods with finitely generated bimodule}) $\mathsf{M}$ = $\Gamma(_\mathsf B\mathsf{H}_\mathsf B)$, the operator-valued free Araki–Woods von Neumann algebra , where $(\mathsf{H},\mathcal J,(\mathcal U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R})$ is a Tomita correspondence over a von Neumann algebra $\mathsf B$ with separable predual such that $\mathsf{H}$ is a countable direct sum of Tomita sub-correspondences which are  finitely-generated as right $\mathsf B$-modules.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
If $(\Phi_t)_{t\geq 0}$ is a quantum Markov semigroup on $\mathsf{M}$ that is GNS-symmetric with respect to $\varphi$ and $\psi$ is a faithful normal state on $\mathsf{M}$ that is invariant under $(\Phi_t)_{t\geq 0}$, then $\Phi_t^{(2)}(x\psi^{1/2})=\Phi_t(x)\psi^{1/2}$ for all $x\in\mathsf{M}$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
By \cite[Theorem A]{Wat79}, the fixed-point set $\mathsf B=\{x\in \mathsf{M}\mid \Phi_t(x)=x\text{ for all }t\geq 0\}$ is a von Neumann subalgebra of $\mathsf{M}$. For every $x\in\mathsf{M}$, the limit $E(x)=\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac 1 T\int_0^T \Phi_t(x)\,dt$ exists in the strong operator topology and $E$ is a faithful normal conditional expectation from $\mathsf{M}$ onto $\mathsf B$. Clearly, $\varphi\circ E=\varphi$ and $\psi\circ E=\psi$.

    Let $\varphi_\mathsf B$, $\psi_\mathsf B$ denote the restrictions of $\varphi$ and $\psi$ to $\mathsf B$. Since $\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}\in L^2(\mathsf B)$ is cyclic, there exists a sequence $(b_n)$ in $\mathsf B$ such that $b_n\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}\to \psi_\mathsf B^{1/2}$. If $\iota_\mathsf B\colon L^2(\mathsf B)\to L^2(\mathsf{M})$ denotes the isometry that maps $b\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}$ to $b\varphi^{1/2}$, then $\iota_\mathsf B^\ast(x\varphi^{1/2})=E(x)\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}$ and
    \begin{equation*}
        \langle \iota_\mathsf B \psi_\mathsf B^{1/2},x\iota_\mathsf B\psi_\mathsf B^{1/2}\rangle=\langle \psi^{1/2},E(x)\psi^{1/2}\rangle=\psi(x).
    \end{equation*}
    Thus $\psi^{1/2}=\iota_\mathsf B \psi_\mathsf B^{1/2}=\lim_{n\to\infty}b_n \varphi^{1/2}$ and
    \begin{equation*}
        \Phi_t^{(2)}(x\psi^{1/2})=\lim_{n\to\infty}\Phi_t(xb_n)\varphi^{1/2}=\lim_{n\to \infty}\Phi_t(x)b_n\varphi^{1/2}=\Phi_t(x)\psi^{1/2},
    \end{equation*}
    where we used that $\mathsf B$ is contained in the multiplicative domain of $\Phi_t$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
If $\delta\colon\operatorname{dom}(\delta)\subset L^2(\mathsf{M})\to\mathsf{H} $ is a densely defined closable $\varphi$-modular derivation with associated GNS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroup $(\Phi_t)_{t\geq 0}$ and $x\in \mathsf{M}$, then $\Phi_t(x)=x$ for all $t\geq 0$ if and only if $x\varphi^{1/2}\in \ker \delta$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
If $\Phi_t(x)=x$ for all $t\geq 0$, then $\Phi_t^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})=x\varphi^{1/2}$ for all $t\geq 0$ and thus $x\varphi^{1/2}\in \ker \mathcal L_2$. Hence $\lVert\bar\delta(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert^2=\langle x\varphi^{1/2},\mathcal L_2(x\varphi^{1/2})\rangle=0$.
    
    Conversely, if $x\varphi^{1/2}\in \ker \bar\delta\subset \ker \mathcal L_2$, then $\Phi_t(x)\varphi^{1/2}=\Phi_t^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})=x\varphi^{1/2}$, hence $\Phi_t(x)=x$ for all $t\geq 0$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- notation-1: body_md -->
If $\delta$ is a densely defined closable modular derivation, we write $\operatorname{Null}(\bar\delta)$ for $\{x\in \mathsf{M}\mid x\varphi^{1/2}\in \ker\bar\delta\}$.
<!-- end notation-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop: criteria for elements in the idealizer}
    Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a von Neumann algebra equipped with a normal faithful state $\varphi$, and let $\omega$ be a cofinal ultrafilter on a directed set $I$. For any net $(x_i)\in \ell^\infty(I,\mathsf{M})$, we have $(x_i)\in\mathcal{M}^\omega(\mathsf{M})$ if and only if for each $\varepsilon>0$, there is $c>0$ and $(y_i)\in\mathcal{M}^\omega(\mathsf{M})$ such that $\lim_{i\to\omega}\|x_i-y_i\|_\varphi^\sharp\leq \varepsilon$ and each $y_i\in \mathsf{M}(\sigma^\varphi, [-a,a])$.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:analytic_core_generator}
    If $(\Phi_t)$ is a GNS-symmetric QMS on $\mathsf{M}$ with $L^2$-generator $\mathcal L_2$, then $\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}\cap\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L_2)$ is dense in $\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L_2)$ with respect to the graph norm of $\mathcal L_2$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Since $\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}$ is  dense in $\mathfrak A_{\varphi}$, and is invariant under $(\Phi_t^{(2)})$, this follows from \cite[Lemma 3.7]{Wir22}.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:dom_L1_gen}
    Let $(\Phi_t)_{t\geq 0}$ be a GNS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroup with associated quantum Dirichlet form $\mathcal E$ and $L^1$-generator $\mathcal L_1$. If $a\in \operatorname{dom}(\mathcal E)$ and there exists $b\in L^1(\mathsf{M})$ such that
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathcal E(a,\varphi^{1/4}x\varphi^{1/4})=\operatorname{tr}(b^\ast x)
    \end{equation*}
    for all $x\in \mathsf{M}$ with $\varphi^{1/4}x\varphi^{1/4}\in \operatorname{dom}(\mathcal E)$, then $\varphi^{1/4}a\varphi^{1/4}\in \operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L_1)$ and $\mathcal L_1(\varphi^{1/4}a\varphi^{1/4})=b$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
If $y\in \mathsf{M}$, then $(\mathcal L+1)^{-1}(y)\in \operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L)$ and $\varphi^{1/4}(\mathcal L+1)^{-1}(y)\varphi^{1/4}=(\mathcal L_2+1)^{-1}(\varphi^{1/4}x \varphi^{1/4})\in \operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L_2)\subset \operatorname{dom}(\mathcal E)$. By assumption,
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathcal E(a,\varphi^{1/4}(\mathcal L+1)^{-1}(y)\varphi^{1/4})=\operatorname{tr}(b^\ast (\mathcal L+1)^{-1}(y))=\operatorname{tr}((\mathcal L_1+1)^{-1}(b)^\ast y).
    \end{equation*}
    On the other hand,
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal E(a,(\mathcal L_2+1)^{-1}(\varphi^{1/4}y\varphi^{1/4}))
        &=\langle a,(1-(\mathcal L_2+1)^{-1})(\varphi^{1/4}y\varphi^{1/4})\rangle_2\\
        &=\operatorname{tr}((1-(\mathcal L_1+1)^{-1})(\varphi^{1/4}a\varphi^{1/4})^\ast y)
    \end{align*}
    Thus $\varphi^{1/4}a\varphi^{1/4}=(\mathcal L_1+1)^{-1}(b+\varphi^{1/4}a\varphi^{1/4})\in \operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L_1)$ and $\mathcal L_1(\varphi^{1/4}a\varphi^{1/4})=b$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:char_Gamma_regular}
    Let $(\Phi_t)$ be a GNS-symmetric QMS on $M$ with $L^p$-generator $\mathcal L_p$ for $p\in \{1,2\}$. The quantum Dirichlet form $\mathcal E$ associated with $(\Phi_t)$ is $\Gamma$-regular if and only if $a,b\in \operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L_2)$ implies $ab\in\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L_1)$, and in this case
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathcal L_1(ab)=\mathcal L_2(a)b+a\mathcal L_2(b)-2\Gamma(a^\ast,b),
    \end{equation*}
    where the products are taken in the Haagerup $L^2$ space.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Assume that $\mathcal E$ is $\Gamma$-regular. We first consider the case $a,b\in\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}\cap\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L_2)$. In particular, there are $x,y\in\mathsf{M}$ such that $a=\varphi^{1/4}x\varphi^{1/4}$, $b=\varphi^{1/4}y\varphi^{1/4}$. If $x\in\mathsf{M}$ with $\varphi^{1/4}x\varphi^{1/4}\in\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}$, then it follows from \cite[Remark 7.1]{Wir22} that
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal E((x\varphi^{1/2}y)^\ast,\varphi^{1/4}z\varphi^{1/4})
        &=\mathcal E(\varphi^{1/4}z^\ast \varphi^{1/4},x\varphi^{1/2}y)\\
        &=\mathcal E(a^\ast,bz)+\mathcal E(a^\ast z^\ast, b)-2\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma(a^\ast,b)y)\\
        &=\operatorname{tr}((\mathcal L_2(a)b+a\mathcal L_2(b)-2\Gamma(a^\ast b))z)
    \end{align*}
    for all $z\in\mathsf{M}$ with $\varphi^{1/4}z\varphi^{1/4}\in \mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}$. If we only have $z\in\mathsf{M}$ with $\varphi^{1/4}z\varphi^{1/4}\in \operatorname{dom}(\mathcal E)$, then it follows analogous to \cite[Theorem 6.3]{Wir22} that there exists a bounded sequence $(d_n)$ in $\mathsf{M}$ with $\varphi^{1/4}d_n\varphi^{1/4}\in\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}$ such that $d_n\to z$ strongly and $\varphi^{1/4}d_n\varphi^{1/4}\to \varphi^{1/4}z\varphi^{1/4}$ with respect to the form norm of $\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal E)$. Hence $\mathcal E((x\varphi^{1/2}y)^\ast,\varphi^{1/4}z\varphi^{1/4})=\operatorname{tr}((\mathcal L_2(a)b+a\mathcal L_2(b)-2\Gamma(a^\ast b))z)$ remains valid. Now we deduce from Lemma \ref{lem:dom_L1_gen} that $ab=\varphi^{1/4}x\varphi^{1/2}y\varphi^{1/4}\in \operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L_1)$ and $\mathcal L_1(ab)=\mathcal L_2(a)b+a\mathcal L_2(b)-2\Gamma(a^\ast,b)$.

    In the general case $a,b\in \operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L_2)$, we can choose sequences $(a_n)$, $(b_n)$ in $\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}\cap \operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L_2)$ such that $a_n\to a$, $b_n\to b$ in the graph norm of $\mathcal L_2$ by Lemma \ref{lem:analytic_core_generator}. In particular, $a_n\to a$ and $b_n\to b$ in the form norm of $\mathcal E$, which implies $\Gamma(a_n^\ast,b_n)\to \Gamma(a^\ast,b)$ in $L^1(\mathsf{M})$. Since $\mathcal L_1$ is closed, we conclude $ab\in \operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L_1)$ and $\mathcal L_1(ab)=\mathcal L_2(a)b+a\mathcal L_2(b)-2\Gamma(a^\ast,b)$.

    Now assume conversely that $a,b\in\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L_2)$ implies $ab\in\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L_1)$. Let $a,b\in \mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}\cap\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L_2)$ and $y\in A_{\mathcal E}$. We have
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal E(\varphi^{1/2}y^\ast,\pi_l(a)^\ast b)
        &=\lim_{t\to 0}\frac 1 t\operatorname{tr}(y\varphi^{1/2}(\pi_l(a)^\ast b-P_t^{(2)}(\pi_l(a)^\ast b)))\\
        &=\lim_{t\to 0}\frac1 t \operatorname{tr}(y(a^\ast b-P_t^{(1)}(a^\ast b)))\\
        &=\operatorname{tr}(y\mathcal L_1(a^\ast b)).
    \end{align*}
    It follows from \cite[Remark 7.1]{Wir22} that 
    \begin{align*}
        \operatorname{tr}(\Gamma(a,b)y)&=\frac 1 2(\mathcal E(a,by)+\mathcal E(ay^\ast,b)-\mathcal E(\varphi^{1/2}y^\ast,\pi_l(a)^\ast b))\\
        &=\frac 1 2\operatorname{tr}((\mathcal L_2(a)^\ast b+a^\ast\mathcal L_2(b)-\mathcal L_1(a^\ast b))y).
    \end{align*}
    Therefore $\Gamma(a,b)=\frac1  2(\mathcal L_2(a)^\ast b+a^\ast\mathcal L_2(b)-\mathcal L_1(a^\ast b))\in L^1(\mathsf{M})$. If $a,b\in \operatorname{dom}(\mathcal E)$, then by Lemma \ref{lem:analytic_core_generator} and the density of $\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L_2)$ in $\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal E)$, there exist sequences $(a_n)$, $(b_n)$ in $\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}\cap \operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L_2)$ such that $a_n\to a$, $b_n\to b$ in the form norm. Since
    \begin{align*}
        \lVert\Gamma(a_m-a_n,b_m-b_n)\rVert_1&\leq \lVert\Gamma(a_m-a_n,b_m)\rVert_1+\lVert\Gamma(a_n,b_m-b_n)\rVert_1\\
        &\leq \mathcal E(a_m-a_n)^{1/2}\mathcal E(b_m)^{1/2}+\mathcal E(a_n)^{1/2}\mathcal E(b_m-b_n)^{1/2}
    \end{align*}
    there exists $h_{a,b}\in L^1(\mathsf{M})$ such that $\Gamma(a_n,b_n)\to h_{a,b}$ in $L^1(\mathsf{M})$. Thus
    \begin{align*}
        \langle \bar\delta(a),\bar\delta(b)y\rangle_\mathsf{H}=\lim_{n\to\infty}\langle \bar\delta(a_n),\bar\delta(b_n)y\rangle=\lim_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma(a_n,b_n)y)=\operatorname{tr}(h_{a,b}y)
    \end{align*}
    for all $y\in A_{\mathcal E}$, which implies $\Gamma(a,b)=h_{a,b}\in L^1(\mathsf{M})$.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
If $(\Phi_t)_{t\geq0}$ is a $\Gamma$-regular GNS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroup on $\mathsf{M}$ with $L^2$-generator $\mathcal L_2$ and $a,b\in\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal L_2)$, then
    \begin{equation*}
        \lVert\mathcal L_2(a)b+a\mathcal L_2(b)-\mathcal L_1(ab)\rVert_1\leq 2\lVert\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(a)\rVert_2\lVert\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(b)\rVert_2.
    \end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
By the previous lemma and the definition of the carré du champ,
    \begin{align*}
        \lVert\mathcal L_2(a)b+a\mathcal L_2(b)-\mathcal L_1(ab)\rVert_1&=2\sup_{\lVertz\rVert\leq 1}\lvert\Gamma(a^\ast b)(z)\rvert\\
        &=2\sup_{\lvertz\rvert\leq 1}\lvert\langle\delta(a^\ast),\delta(b)z\rangle\rvert\\
        &\leq 2\lVert\delta(a)\rVert_{\mathsf{H}}\lVert\delta(b)\rVert_{\mathsf{H}}\\
        &=2\lVert\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(a)\rVert_2\lVert\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(b)\rVert_2\qedhere
    \end{align*}
    as required.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:L2_L4_duality}
    If $b\in L^2(\mathsf{M})$, then
    \begin{equation*}
        \lVertb\rVert_2=\sup\{\lvert\operatorname{tr}(abc)\rvert:a,c\in L^4(M),\,\lVerta\rVert_4,\lVertc\rVert_4\leq 1\}.
    \end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
One inequality is a direct consequence of Hölder's inequality. To prove the reverse inequality, let $b=u\lvertb\rvert$ be the polar decomposition of $b$ with $u\in c_\varphi(\mathsf{M})$ and $\lvertb\rvert\in L^2(\mathsf{M})$. We can assume $b\neq 0$. Let $a=\lvertb\rvert^{1/2}u^\ast/\lVertb\rVert_2^{1/2}$, $c=\lvertb\rvert^{1/2}/\lVertb\rVert_2^{1/2}$. We have $\lVerta\rVert_4,\lVertc\rVert_4\leq 1$ and
    \begin{equation*}
        \lvert\operatorname{tr}(abc)\rvert=\frac 1{\lVertb\rVert_2}\lvert\operatorname{tr}(\lvertb\rvert^{1/2}u^\ast u\lvertb\rvert\lvertb\rvert^{1/2})\rvert=\frac 1{\lVertb\rVert_2}\operatorname{tr}(\lvertb\rvert^2)=\lVertb\rVert_2.\qedhere
    \end{equation*}
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:prod_rule}
    If $\delta\colon \operatorname{dom}(\delta)\subset L^2(M)\to \mathsf{H}$ is a densely defined closable $\varphi$-modular derivation, $a\in \operatorname{dom}(\bar\delta)\cap \mathsf{M}\varphi^{1/2}$ and $b\in \operatorname{dom}(\bar\delta)\cap \varphi^{1/2}\mathsf{M}$, then $\pi_l(a)b\in \operatorname{dom}(\bar\delta)$ and 
    \begin{equation*}
        \bar\delta(\pi_l(a)b)=\pi_l(a) \bar\delta(b)+\bar\delta(a)\cdot J\pi_r(b)^\ast J.
    \end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Since $a$ is left-bounded and $b$ is right-bounded, we have $a=x\varphi^{1/2}$ and $b=\varphi^{1/2}y$ with $x=\pi_l(a)$ and $y=J\pi_r(b)^\ast J$. Let $\mathcal E$ be  the quantum Dirichlet form associated with $\bar\delta$. By \cite[Theorem 6.3]{Wir22} there exist sequences $(a_n)$, $(b_n)$ in $\mathfrak A_\mathcal E$ such that $a_n\to a$, $b_n\to b$ in $(\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal E),\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\mathcal E})$ and $\pi_l(a_n)\to \pi_l(a)$, $\pi_r(b_n)\to \pi_r(b)$ in the strong operator topology.

    By \cite[Proposition 4.6]{Wir24}, one has
    \begin{equation*}
        \bar\delta(a_n b_n)=\pi_l(a_n)\bar\delta(b_n)+\bar\delta(a_n)\cdot J\pi_r(b_n)^\ast J.
    \end{equation*}
    Since $a_n b_n\to ab$ in $L^2(M)$ and the right side converges to $\pi_l(a)\bar\delta(b)+\bar\delta(a)\cdot J\pi_r(b)^\ast J$ in $\mathsf{H} $, the claim follows from the fact that $\bar\delta$ is closed.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:carre_du_champ_L2}
    If $\delta\colon \operatorname{dom}(\delta)\subset L^2(\mathsf{M})\to \mathsf{H} $ is a densely defined closable modular derivation and $\mathcal L_2=\delta^\ast\bar\delta$, then
    \begin{align*}
        &\lVertx\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(\varphi^{1/2}y)+\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(x\varphi^{1/2})y-\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(x\varphi^{1/2}y)\rVert_2\\
        &\quad\leq 4\lVertx\rVert^{1/2}\lVerty\rVert^{1/2}\lVert\bar\delta(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert^{1/2}\lVert\bar\delta(\varphi^{1/2}y)\rVert^{1/2}.
    \end{align*}
     for all $x,y\in \mathsf{M}$ with $x\varphi^{1/2}$, $\varphi^{1/2}y\in \operatorname{dom}(\bar\delta)$.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
If $x\varphi^{1/2},\varphi^{1/2}y\in \operatorname{dom}(\bar\delta)$, then $x\varphi^{1/2}y\in \operatorname{dom}(\bar\delta)$ by Lemma \ref{lem:prod_rule}, so that the expression in the lemma is well-defined.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal E$ be the quantum Dirichlet form associated with $\delta$. For $x,y\in\pi_l(\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E})$ define
    \begin{equation*}
        a_{x,y}=x^\ast\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(\varphi^{1/2}y)+\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(x^\ast\varphi^{1/2})y-\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(x^\ast\varphi^{1/2}y).
    \end{equation*}
   By Proposition  \ref{prop:char_Gamma_regular} we have
    \begin{align*}
        \varphi^{1/4}a_{x,y}\varphi^{1/4}&=\varphi^{1/4}x^\ast \varphi^{1/4}\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(\varphi^{1/4}y\varphi^{1/4})+\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(\varphi^{1/4}x^\ast \varphi^{1/4})\varphi^{1/4}y \varphi^{1/4}\\
        &\quad-\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(\varphi^{1/4}x^\ast\varphi^{1/2}y\varphi^{1/4})\\
        &=2\Gamma_{1/2}(\varphi^{1/4}x\varphi^{1/4},\varphi^{1/4}y\varphi^{1/4}),
    \end{align*}
    where $\Gamma_{1/2}$ is the carré du champ associated with $\mathcal L_2^{1/2}$.
    
    In particular, the sesquilinear form 
    \begin{align*}
        s\colon (\pi_l(\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E})\odot \mathsf{M})\times (\pi_l(\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E})\odot \mathsf{M})&\to \mathbb C,\\
        (x\otimes z_1,y\otimes z_2)&\mapsto \operatorname{tr}(z_1^\ast \varphi^{1/4}a_{x,y}\varphi^{1/4}z_2)
    \end{align*}
    is  positive semi-definite.
    
    By Cauchy--Schwarz and Lemma \ref{lem:L2_L4_duality}, we have
    \begin{align*}
        \lVerta_{x,y}\rVert_2&=\sup\{\lvert\operatorname{tr}(z_1^\ast \varphi^{1/4}a_{x,y}\varphi^{1/4}z_2): z_1,z_2\in\mathsf{M},\,\lVert\varphi^{1/4}z_j\rVert_4\leq 1\rvert\\
        &=\sup_{\lVert\varphi^{1/4} z_j\rVert_4\leq 1}\lverts(x\otimes z_1,y\otimes z_2)\rvert\\
        &\leq \sup_{\lVert\varphi^{1/4}z_1\rVert_4\leq 1}s(x\otimes z_1)^{1/2}\sup_{\lVert\varphi^{1/4}z_2\rVert\leq 1}s(y\otimes z_2)^{1/2}\\
        &=\lVerta_{x,x}\rVert_2^{1/2}\lVerta_{y,y}\rVert_2^{1/2}.
    \end{align*}
    Moreover,
    \begin{align*}
        \lVerta_{x,x}\rVert_2\leq 2\lVert\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(\varphi^{1/2}x)\rVert_2\lVertx\rVert+\lVert\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(x^\ast \varphi^{1/2}x)\rVert_2
    \end{align*}
    By definition, $\lVert\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(\varphi^{1/2}x)\rVert_2=\lVert\delta(\varphi^{1/2}x)\rVert^{1/2}$. Furthermore, by the product rule,
    \begin{align*}
        \lVert\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(x^\ast \varphi^{1/2}x)\rVert_2=\lVert\delta(x^\ast\varphi^{1/2})x+x^\ast \delta(\varphi^{1/2}x)\rVert\leq 4\lVert\delta(\varphi^{1/2}x)\rVert\lVertx\rVert,
    \end{align*}
    therefore,
    \begin{equation*}
        \lVerta_{x,x}\rVert_2\leq 2\lVertx\rVert\lVert\delta(\varphi^{1/2}x)\rVert.
    \end{equation*}
    If we combine this with the analogous bound for $\lVerta_{y,y}\rVert_2$, we arrive at the desired bound for $x,y\in\pi_l(\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E})$.

    In the general case, when we only assume $x\varphi^{1/2}$, $\varphi^{1/2}y\in \operatorname{dom}(\bar\delta)$, the result follows via approximation as in \cite[Theorem 6.3]{Wir22}.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:bound_Stinespring}
    If  a ucp map $\Phi\colon \mathsf{M}\to \mathsf{M}$ is GNS-symmetric with respect to $\varphi$  and $x,y\in \mathsf{M}$, then
    \begin{align*}
        \varphi(\lvert\Phi(xy)-\Phi(x)y\rvert^2)&\leq 2\lVertx\rVert^2\varphi(\lverty\rvert^2)^{1/2}\varphi(\lverty-\Phi(y)\rvert^2)^{1/2}
    \end{align*}
    and
    \begin{equation*}
        \lVerty\Phi^{(2)}(\varphi^{1/2}x)-\Phi^{(2)}(y\varphi^{1/2}x)\rVert^2\leq 2\lVertx\rVert^2\varphi(\lverty\rvert^2)^{1/2}\varphi(\lverty-\Phi(y)\rvert^2)^{1/2}.
    \end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
Let $\Phi=V^\ast\pi(\cdot)V$ be a Stinespring dilation of $\Phi$. We have
    \begin{align*}
        \varphi(\lvert\Phi(xy)-\Phi(x)y\rvert^2)&=\lVertV^\ast\pi(x)(\pi(y)V-V y)\varphi^{1/2}\rVert^2\\
        &\leq \lVertx\rVert^2\lVert(\pi(y)V-V y)\varphi^{1/2}\rVert^2\\
        &=\lVertx\rVert^2(\varphi(\Phi(y^\ast y))+\varphi(y^\ast y)-2\operatorname{Re}\varphi(\Phi(y)^\ast y)\\
        &=2\lVertx\rVert^2\varphi(y^\ast(y-\Phi(y))\\
        &\leq 2\lVertx\rVert^2\varphi(\lverty\rvert^2)^{1/2}\varphi(\lverty-\Phi(y)\rvert^2)^{1/2}.
    \end{align*}
    Thus, if $y\in \mathsf{M}_{\infty,\sigma^\varphi}$, then
    \begin{align*}
        &\lVert\Phi^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2}\sigma^\varphi_{i/2}(y))-\Phi^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})\sigma^\varphi_{i/2}(y)\rVert^2\\
        &\quad\leq 2\lVertx\rVert^2\varphi(\lvert\sigma^\varphi_{i/2}(y)^\ast\rvert^2)^{1/2}\lVert\varphi^{1/2}\sigma^\varphi_{i/2}(y)-\Phi^{(2)}(\varphi^{1/2}\sigma^\varphi_{i/2}(y))\rVert.
    \end{align*}
    Replacing $y$ by $\sigma^\varphi_{-i/2}(y)$, we get
    \begin{equation*}
        \lVert\Phi^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2}y)-\Phi^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})y\rVert^2
        \leq 2\lVertx\rVert^2\varphi(\lverty^\ast\rvert^2)^{1/2}\lVert\varphi^{1/2}y-\Phi^{(2)}(\varphi^{1/2}y)\rVert.
    \end{equation*}
    If we replace $x$ by $x^\ast$ and $y$ by $y^\ast$, we obtain the second inequality in the lemma. For general $y\in \mathsf{M}$, not necessarily analytic, the result follows by standard approximation arguments.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- notation-2: body_md -->
\label{notation}
    If $(\mathsf{H} ,\mathcal J,(\mathcal U_t))_{t\in\mathbb R})$ is a Tomita correspondence over $(\mathsf{M},\varphi)$, $\delta\colon \operatorname{dom}(\delta)\subset L^2(\mathsf{M})\to\mathsf{H} $ is a densely defined closable $\varphi$-modular derivation and $\alpha>0$, then we write $\zeta_\alpha$, $\theta_\alpha$ for the unique GNS-symmetric ucp maps on $\mathsf{M}$ such that
    \[\zeta_\alpha^{(2)}=\alpha^{1/2}(\mathcal L_2+\alpha)^{-1/2},\;\;\;\;\theta_\alpha^{(2)}=\alpha(\mathcal L_2+\alpha)^{-1} \;\; and \;\;\rho_\alpha=1-\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(\mathcal L_2+\alpha)^{-1/2}\]
    Moreover, we write
    \[\tilde\delta_\alpha =\bar\delta\circ(\mathcal L_2+\alpha)^{-1/2}=\alpha^{-1/2}\bar\delta\circ\zeta_\alpha^{(2)}.\]
<!-- end notation-2 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{rmk:ucp_families}
    Let $(\Phi_t)_{t\geq 0}$ be a GNS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroup on $\mathsf{M}$. As discussed in \ref{subsec:QMS}, one has
    \begin{equation*}
        (\mathcal L+\alpha)^{-1}=\int_0^\infty e^{-\alpha t}\Phi_t\,dt
    \end{equation*}
    as a weak$^\ast$ integral. 
    Thus $\theta_\alpha=\alpha(\mathcal L+\alpha)^{-1}$ is a GNS-symmetric ucp map.
    With the help of the spectral theorem, one can show that (cf. \cite[Lemma 3.2]{Pet09})
    \begin{align*}
        \alpha^{1/2}(\mathcal L_2+\alpha)^{-1/2}&=\frac 1 \pi\int_0^\infty \theta^{(2)}_{\alpha (1+t)/t}\frac{dt}{(1+t)\sqrt t},\\
        1-\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(\mathcal L_2+\alpha)^{-1/2}&=\frac 1 \pi \int_0^\infty \theta^{(2)}_{t\alpha/(1+t)}\frac{dt}{(1+t)\sqrt t}
    \end{align*}
    in the strong operator topology. It follows from Cipriani's correspondence \cite[Section 2]{Cip97} that the ucp maps $\zeta_\alpha$ and $\eta_\alpha$ exist.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem: the main technical lemma}
                                                                                          
    Let $(\mathsf{H} ,\mathcal J,(\mathcal U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R})$ be a Tomita correspondence over $(\mathsf{M},\varphi)$ and let $\delta\colon \operatorname{dom}(\delta)\subset L^2(\mathsf{M})\to \mathsf{H} $ be a densely defined closable $\varphi$-modular derivation. For $x,y\in \mathsf{M}$ and $\alpha>0$, one has
    \begin{align*}                      
        \lVert\zeta_\alpha(x)\tilde\delta_\alpha (\varphi^{1/2}y)-\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2}y)\rVert&\leq 10\lVertx\rVert^{1/2}\lVerty\rVert\lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert^{1/2},\\
        \lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\zeta_\alpha (y)-\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2}y)\rVert&\leq 10\lVerty\rVert^{1/2}\lVertx\rVert\lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(\varphi^{1/2}y)\rVert^{1/2}.
    \end{align*}
    In particular, 
    \begin{align*}
        \lim_{\alpha\to\infty} \lVert\zeta_\alpha(x)\tilde\delta_\alpha(a)-\tilde\delta_\alpha(xa)\rVert=0\\
        \lim_{\alpha\to\infty} \lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(a) \zeta_\alpha(x)-\tilde\delta_\alpha(a x)\rVert=0\\
    \end{align*}
    for all $x\in \mathsf{M}$, $a\in L^2(\mathsf{M})$.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
We may assume that $x$ and $y$ are analytic for $\sigma^\varphi$. By the product rule for $\bar\delta$ from Lemma \ref{lem:prod_rule} we have
    \begin{equation*}
        \zeta_\alpha(x)\tilde\delta_\alpha(\varphi^{1/2}y)=\alpha^{-1/2}\bar\delta(\zeta_\alpha(x)\varphi^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(y))-\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\zeta_\alpha(y).
    \end{equation*}
    Note that $\lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\zeta_\alpha(y)\rVert\leq \lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert\lVerty\rVert$ since $\zeta_\alpha$ is a ucp map.

    To bound $\alpha^{-1/2}\bar\delta(\zeta_\alpha(x)\varphi^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(y))$, let $\bar\delta=V\mathcal L_2^{1/2}$ be the polar decomposition of $\bar\delta$. As a consequence of Proposition \ref{prop:char_Gamma_regular} and Lemma \ref{lem:carre_du_champ_L2} we have
    \begin{align*}
        &V^\ast (\alpha^{-1/2}\bar\delta(\zeta_\alpha(x)\varphi^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(y)))\\
        &\quad=\alpha^{-1/2}\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(\zeta_\alpha(x)\varphi^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(y))\\
        &\quad=\underbrace{\alpha^{-1/2}\zeta_\alpha (x)\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(\varphi^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(y))}_{b_1}+\underbrace{\alpha^{-1/2}\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(\zeta_\alpha(x)\varphi^{1/2})\zeta_\alpha(y)}_{b_2}\\
        &\quad\quad-\underbrace{2\alpha^{-1/2}a_{\zeta_\alpha(x)^\ast,\zeta_\alpha(y)}}_{b_3},
    \end{align*}
    where $a_{\zeta_\alpha(x)^\ast,\zeta_\alpha(y)}\in L^2(\mathsf{M})$ with 
    \begin{align*}
        \lVerta_{\zeta_\alpha(x)^\ast,\zeta_\alpha(y)}\rVert_2
        &\leq 2\lVert\zeta_\alpha(x)\rVert^{1/2}\lVert\zeta_\alpha(y)\rVert^{1/2}\lVert\bar\delta(\varphi^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(x)^\ast)\rVert^{1/2}\lVert\bar\delta(\varphi^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(y)\rVert^{1/2}\\
        &\leq 2\alpha^{1/2}\lVertx\rVert^{1/2}\lVerty\rVert^{1/2}\lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(\varphi^{1/2}x)\rVert^{1/2}\lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(\varphi^{1/2}y)\rVert^{1/2}\\
        &\leq 2\alpha^{1/2}\lVertx\rVert^{1/2}\lVerty\rVert\lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(\varphi^{1/2}x)\rVert^{1/2}.
    \end{align*}

    We have $\lVertb_2\rVert\leq \lVert\alpha^{-1/2}\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(\zeta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2}))\rVert\lVerty\rVert=\lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert\lVerty\rVert$ and
    \begin{align*}
        b_1-V^\ast\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2}y)
        &=\alpha^{-1/2}(\zeta_\alpha(x)\mathcal L_2^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha^{(2)}(\varphi^{1/2}y)-\mathcal L_2^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2}y))\\
        &=(\zeta_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})y-x\varphi^{1/2}y)+(\rho_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2}y)-\zeta_\alpha(x)\rho_\alpha^{(2)}(\varphi^{1/2}y)).
    \end{align*}
    By the spectral theorem, if $E$ denotes the spectral measure of $\mathcal L_2$, then
    \begin{align*}
        \lVert(\zeta_\alpha^{(2)}-1)(a)\rVert^2
        &=\int_{[0,\infty)}(1-\alpha^{1/2}(\alpha+\lambda)^{-1/2})^2\,d\lVertE(\lambda)a\rVert^2\\
        &\leq \int_{[0,\infty)}\frac{\lambda}{\alpha+\lambda}\,d\lVertE(\lambda)a\rVert^2\\
        &=\alpha^{-1}\lVert\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(\zeta_\alpha^{(2)}(a))\rVert^2\\
        &=\lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(a)\rVert^2
    \end{align*}
    for all $a\in L^2(M)$. Thus
    \begin{equation*}
        \lVert\zeta_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})\varphi^{1/2}y-x\varphi^{1/2}y\rVert\leq \lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert\lVerty\rVert.
    \end{equation*}
    Moreover,
    \begin{align*}
        &\lVert\rho_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2}y)-\zeta_\alpha(x)\rho_\alpha^{(2)}(\varphi^{1/2}y)\rVert\\
        &\quad\leq \lVert\rho_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2}y)-\rho_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})\rho_\alpha(y)\rVert+\lVert\rho_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})-\zeta_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert\lVerty\rVert.
    \end{align*}
    For the first summand on the right side, we can use the bound from Lemma~\ref{lem:bound_Stinespring} to get
    \begin{align*}
        \lVert\rho_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2}y)-\rho_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})\rho_\alpha(y)\rVert
        &\leq \lVertx\rVert^{1/2}\lVert\varphi^{1/2}y\rVert\lVertx\varphi^{1/2}-\rho_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert^{1/2}\\
        &\leq \lVertx\rVert^{1/2}\lVerty\rVert\lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert^{1/2}.
    \end{align*}
    Furthermore,
    \begin{align*}
        \lVert\rho_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})-\zeta_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert
        &\leq \lVert\rho_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})-x\varphi^{1/2}\rVert+\lVertx\varphi^{1/2}-\zeta_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert\\
        &\leq 2\lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert.
    \end{align*}
    To conclude, we combine the bounds and note that $\lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert\leq \lVertx\varphi^{1/2}\rVert\leq \lVertx\rVert$ since $\varphi$ is a state.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor; corollary to the technical lemma in the ultrapower language}
    Let $\delta:\operatorname{dom}\delta\to\mathsf{H}$ be a densely defined closable modular derivation and let $\omega$ be a cofinal ultrafilter on  a directed set. We have
    \begin{align*}
        &\lim_{\alpha\to\infty}\|\zeta_{\alpha}(x)\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha}(\xi)-\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha}(x\xi)\|=0\\
        &\lim_{\alpha\to\infty}\|\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha}(\xi)\zeta_{\alpha}(x)-\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha}(\xi x)\|=0
    \end{align*}
    for all $x\in \mathsf{M}$ and $\xi\in L^2(\mathsf{M}^\omega)$, where $\mathsf{H}^\omega$ is treated as a possibly non-normal bimodule over $\mathsf{M}$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
We shall prove the first equality.   Let $x\in \mathsf{M}$ with $\|x\|_\infty\leq  1$  and let $\xi\in L^2(\mathsf{M}^\omega)$. Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and choose $y\in\mathsf{M}^\omega$ such that $\|\xi-(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2} y\|\leq \varepsilon$. Let  $(y_n)\in \mathcal{M}^\omega(\mathsf{M})$ be  representatives of $y$, and let $C>0$ be a constant such that $C>\sup_n  \|y_n\|_\infty$. By Lemma \ref{lem: the main technical lemma}, we have
    \begin{align*}
     \|\zeta_{\alpha }(x)\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha }(\xi)-\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha }(x\xi)\|
     &\leq 2\varepsilon \|x\|_\infty+ \|\zeta_{\alpha }(x)\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha }((\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}y)-\tilde\delta_{\alpha }(x(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}y)\|\\
&=2\varepsilon+\lim_{n\to\omega}\|\zeta_\alpha(x)\tilde\delta_\alpha(\varphi^{1/2}y_n)-\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2}y_n)\|\\
     &\leq 2\varepsilon +10 C\|\tilde\delta_{\alpha }( x\varphi^{1/2})\|^{1/2}
    \end{align*}
 Because $\varepsilon>0$ is arbitrary and $\tilde\delta_\alpha$ converges strongly to $0$ on $L^2(\mathsf{M})$, the required assertion follows.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lemma:estimates on the values in derivation}
  Let $\delta:\operatorname{dom}\delta\subseteq L^2(\mathsf{M})\to\mathsf{H}$ be a densely defined closable $\varphi$-modular derivation.   There exists $C>0$ such that for $\alpha\geq 1$ and $x,y\in \mathsf{M}$ with $x\varphi^{1/2}\in \operatorname{dom}(\overline\delta)$ one has
    \begin{equation*}
        \lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2}y)-x\tilde\delta_\alpha(\varphi^{1/2}y)\rVert\leq C\alpha^{-1/4}(\lVertx\rVert^{1/2}+\lVert\overline\delta(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert^{1/2})\lVert\overline\delta(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert^{1/2}\lVerty\rVert.
    \end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
By the product rule,
    \begin{equation*}
        x\tilde\delta_\alpha(\varphi^{1/2}y)=\alpha^{-1/2}x\overline\delta(\varphi^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(y))=\alpha^{-1/2}\overline\delta(x\varphi^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(y))-\alpha^{-1/2}\overline{\delta}(x\varphi^{1/2})\zeta_\alpha(y).
    \end{equation*}
    Thus
    \begin{align*}
        &\lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2}y)-x\tilde\delta_\alpha(\varphi^{1/2}y)\rVert\\
        &\quad\leq \alpha^{-1/2}\lVert\bar\delta(\zeta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2}y)-x\varphi^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(y))\rVert+\alpha^{-1/2}\lVert\bar\delta(x\varphi^{1/2})\zeta_\alpha(y)\rVert\\
        &\quad\leq \alpha^{-1/2}\lVert\bar\delta(\zeta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2}y)-x\varphi^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(y))\rVert+\alpha^{-1/2}\lVert\bar\delta(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert\lVerty\rVert.
    \end{align*}
    We have
    \begin{align*}
        &\lVert\bar\delta(\zeta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2}y)-x\varphi^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(y))\rVert\\
        &\quad=\lVert\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(\zeta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2}y)-x\varphi^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(y))\rVert\\
        &\quad\leq \lVert\mathcal L_2^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2}y)-x\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(\varphi^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(y))\rVert\\
        &\qquad+\lVertx\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(\varphi^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(y))+\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(x\varphi^{1/2})\zeta_\alpha(y)-\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(x\varphi^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(y))\rVert\\
        &\qquad +\lVert\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(x\varphi^{1/2})\zeta_\alpha(y)\rVert.
    \end{align*}
   By Lemma \ref{lem:carre_du_champ_L2},  the second summand on the right side is bounded above by
    \begin{align*}
        4\lVertx\rVert^{1/2}\lVerty\rVert^{1/2}\lVert\bar\delta(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert^{1/2}\lVert\bar\delta(\varphi^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(y)\rVert^{1/2}\leq 4\alpha^{1/4}\lVertx\rVert^{1/2}\lVert\bar\delta(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert^{1/2}\lVerty\rVert.
    \end{align*}
 For the third summand, we have
    \begin{align*}
        \lVert\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(x\varphi^{1/2})\zeta_\alpha(y)\rVert\leq \lVert\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert\lVerty\rVert=\lVert\bar\delta(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert\lVerty\rVert.
    \end{align*}
    It remains to bound the first summand. We have
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal L_2^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2}y)-x\mathcal L_2^{1/2}(\varphi^{1/2}\zeta_\alpha(y))&=\alpha^{1/2}x\rho_\alpha^{(2)}(\varphi^{1/2}y)-\alpha^{1/2}\rho_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2} y).
    \end{align*}
    By Lemma \ref{lem:bound_Stinespring} we have
    \begin{align*}
        \lVertx\rho_\alpha^{(2)}(\varphi^{1/2}y)-\rho_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2} y)\rVert&\leq \sqrt 2\lVerty\rVert\lVertx\rVert^{1/2}\lVert\rho_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})-x\varphi^{1/2}\rVert^{1/2}\\
        &=\sqrt 2 \lVerty\rVert\lVertx\rVert^{1/2}\lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert^{1/2}\\
        &\leq \alpha^{-1/4}\sqrt 2\lVerty\rVert\lVertx\rVert^{1/2}\lVert\bar\delta(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert^{1/2}.
    \end{align*}
    Altogether, we have shown that
    \begin{align*}
        &\lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2}y)-x\tilde\delta_\alpha(\varphi^{1/2}y)\rVert\\
        &\quad\leq (2\alpha^{-1/2}\lVert\bar\delta(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert^{1/2}+(4+\sqrt 2)\alpha^{-1/4}\lVertx\rVert^{1/2})\lVert\bar\delta(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert^{1/2}\lVerty\rVert.\qedhere
    \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{lem: density of analytic unitaries}
    If $\mathsf{M}$ is a von Neumann algebra and $\alpha\colon \mathbb R\curvearrowright \mathsf{M}$ is a point-weak$^\ast$ continuous action by $\ast$-isomorphisms, then the set of $\alpha$-analytic unitaries is strongly dense in $\mathcal U(\mathsf{M})$.
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
If $u\in \mathcal U(\mathsf{M})$, then there exists $x\in \mathsf{M}$ self-adjoint with spectrum contained in $[0,2\pi]$ such that $u=e^{ix}$. By standard approximation arguments, there is a sequence $(x_n)$ of self-adjoint elements in $M$ that are analytic for $\alpha$, satisfy $0\leq x_n\leq 2\pi$ for all $n\in\mathbb N$ and converge to $x$ strongly. For example, one can take $x_n=\sqrt{\frac n \pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-nt^2}\alpha_t(x)\,dt$. If we let $u_n=e^{ix_n}$, then $u_n$ is unitary, analytic for $\alpha$ since $\exp$ is entire and $u_n\to u$ strongly by the strong continuity of functional calculus.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:ext_bimodule_action}
    Let $\mathsf B\subset \mathsf{M}$ be an inclusion of von Neumann algebras with expectation and let $\mathsf P=\langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$. If $\mathsf{H}$ is an $\mathsf{M}$-$\mathsf B$ correspondence, then there exists a normal $\ast$-homomorphism $\rho\colon \mathsf P\to \pi_r^\mathsf{H}(\mathsf B)^\prime$ that extends $\pi_l^\mathsf{H}$ if and only if there exists a $\mathsf B$-$\mathsf B$ correspondence $\mathsf{K}$ such that ${_\mathsf{M}\mathsf{H}_\mathsf B}\cong {_\mathsf{M} L^2(\mathsf{M})}\otimes_\mathsf B \mathsf{K}_\mathsf B$.

    Moreover, if $\mathsf{H}$ is an $\mathsf{M}$-$\mathsf{M}$ correspondence, then there exist normal $\ast$-homo\-morphisms $\rho_l\colon \mathsf P\to B(\mathsf{H})$, $\rho_r\colon \mathsf P^{\mathrm{op}}\to B(\mathsf{H})$ with commuting images that extend $\pi_l^\mathsf{H}$ and $\pi_r^\mathsf{H}$, respectively, if and only if there exists a $\mathsf B$-$\mathsf B$ correspondence $\mathsf{K}$ such that $_\mathsf{M} \mathsf{H}_\mathsf{M}\cong {_\mathsf{M} L^2(\mathsf{M})}\otimes_\mathsf B \mathsf{K}\otimes_\mathsf B {L^2(\mathsf{M})_\mathsf{M}}$.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
We prove only the second part; the first is similar. 
Fix a faithful normal state $\omega$ on $\mathsf B$. If $_\mathsf{M}\mathsf{H}_\mathsf{M}={_\mathsf{M} L^2(\mathsf{M})}\otimes_\omega \mathsf{K}\otimes_\omega {L^2(\mathsf{M})_\mathsf{M}}$, one can define $\rho_l(S)=S\otimes_\omega 1_\mathsf{K}\otimes_\omega 1_{L^2(\mathsf{M})}$ and $\rho_r(T^{\mathrm{op}})=1_{L^2(\mathsf{M})}\otimes_\omega 1_\mathsf{K}\otimes_\omega J_\mathsf{M} T^\ast J_\mathsf{M}$.

    Conversely, let $_{\mathsf P}\mathsf{H}_{\mathsf P}$ be the $\mathsf P$-$\mathsf P$ correspondence defined by $\rho_l$ and $\rho_r$ and let $_\mathsf B \mathsf{K}_\mathsf B={_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M})}\otimes_{\mathsf P}\mathsf{H}\otimes_{\mathsf P} L^2(\mathsf{M})_\mathsf B$. We have
    \begin{align*}
        {_\mathsf P}L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes_\mathsf B \mathsf{K}\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M})_{\mathsf P}&\cong {_\mathsf P}L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes_{\mathsf P}\mathsf{H}\otimes_{\mathsf P}L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M})_{\mathsf P}\\
        &\cong{_\mathsf P}L^2(\mathsf P)\otimes_{\mathsf P}\mathsf{H}\otimes_{\mathsf P} L^2(\mathsf P)_{\mathsf P}\\
        &\cong{_\mathsf P}\mathsf{H}_{\mathsf P},
    \end{align*}
    where we used the isomorphism ${_\mathsf P}L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M})_{\mathsf P}\cong {_\mathsf P}L^2(\mathsf P)_{\mathsf P}$ from \cite[Proposition 3.1]{Sau83}.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{Prop:Equivalent conditions on relative amenability in terms of states with extra assumption on summand}
    Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a  von Neumann algebra equipped with a normal faithful state $\varphi$, and let $\mathsf A$ be a subalgebra of $\mathsf{M}$  with $\varphi$-preserving expectation $E_\mathsf A$. Denote by $\mathsf{M}_\infty$ the algebra of $\sigma^\varphi$-analytic vectors of $\mathsf{M}$. Assume that $\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M}$ has no summand that is both semifinite and properly infinite. For a   $C^\ast$-algebra $\mathcal{B}$ containing $\mathsf{M}$ as a unital subalgebra, the following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
     \item There exists a norm-one projection $\Phi$ from $\mathcal{B}$ onto $\mathsf A$ such that $\Phi_{|_{\mathsf{M}}}=E_\mathsf A$.\label{existence of a conditional expectation}
      \item There exists a state $\psi:\mathcal{B}\to\mathbb C$ and a constant $C>0$ such that $\psi_{|_{\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})}}$ is faithful and   
        \[\psi_{|_{\mathsf{M}}}\leq C\varphi, \;\;\;\;\psi(Tb)=\psi(\sigma_i^\varphi (b)T)\]
        for $T\in \mathcal{B}$ and $b\in \mathsf A\cap \mathsf{M}_\infty$. \label{existence of a state dominated by phi}
        \item There exists a state $\psi:\mathcal{B}\to\mathbb C$ and a positive element  $z\in \mathcal{Z}(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})$ with full support  such that  
       \[\psi(x)=\varphi(xz),\;\;\;\;\;\psi(Tb)=\psi(\sigma_i^\varphi(b)T)\]
        for  all $x\in \mathsf{M}$, $T\in \mathcal{B}$ and $b\in \mathsf A\cap \mathsf{M}_\infty$. \label{existence of a state conjugated by a centralizer element}
     \item There exists a  state $\psi:\mathcal{B}\to \mathbb  C$ such that $\psi_{|_{\mathsf{M}}}=\varphi$ and satisfies 
     \[\psi(Tb)=\psi(\sigma_i^\varphi(b)T)\]
            for $T\in \mathcal{B}$ and $b\in \mathsf A\cap \mathsf{M}_\infty$.\label{existence of a state whose restriction is phi}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
(\ref{existence of a conditional expectation})$\implies$(\ref{existence of a state dominated by phi}) Take $\psi=\varphi\circ \Phi$.
    
    (\ref{existence of a state dominated by phi})$\implies$(\ref{existence of a state conjugated by a centralizer element}).  The condition $\psi_{|_\mathsf{M}}\leq C \varphi$ implies that there exists $a\in \mathsf{M}_+$ with    $0\leq a\leq C$ such that   $\psi(x)=\langle \varphi^{1/2},x\varphi^{1/2}a\rangle$  for $x\in \mathsf{M}$ (\cite[Proposition 2.3]{Str20}).
    We claim that $a\in \mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M}$. Indeed, if $b\in \mathsf A,y\in \mathsf{M}$ and $b$ is analytic, then
    \begin{align*}
    \langle \varphi^{1/2}, y\varphi^{1/2}\sigma_{i/2}^\varphi(b)a\rangle&= \langle \varphi^{1/2}, yb\varphi^{1/2}a\rangle=\psi( yb)
    =\psi(\sigma_i^\varphi(b) y)\\
    &=\langle \sigma_{-i}^\varphi(b^\ast)\varphi^{1/2}, y\varphi^{1/2}a\rangle=\langle\varphi^{1/2},y \varphi^{1/2}a\sigma_{i/2}^\varphi(b)\rangle
    \end{align*}
    and since $y\in \mathsf{M}$  is arbitrary, it follows that $a\sigma_{i/2}^\varphi(b)=\sigma_{i/2}^\varphi(b)a$ for all $b\in \mathsf A\cap\mathsf{M}_\infty$. Since $\mathsf A\cap\mathsf{M}_\infty$ is globally invariant under $\sigma_z^\varphi, z\in \mathbb C$ and since $\mathsf A\cap\mathsf{M}_\infty$ is weakly dense in $\mathsf A$, our claim follows.

Now  denote by $G$ the subgroup of $\mathcal{U}(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})$ consisting of $\sigma^\varphi$-analytic unitaries. Since $\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M}$ is globally invariant under $\sigma^\varphi$, it follows from Lemma \ref{lem: density of analytic unitaries} that $G$ is $\sigma$-weak dense in $\mathcal{U}(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})$.
                   
                                                                                         
                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                   
By weak Dixmier property (\cite[Theorem 2.2]{Iso25}, \cite[Theorem 5.2]{Mar25}), there is a normal faithful conditional expectation $F:\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M}\to\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})$ such that 
\begin{align*}
 F(a)\in \overline{\text{co}}^{\text{wk}}\{uau^\ast; u\in G\},
\end{align*}
where $\overline{\text{co}}^{\text{wk}}$ denotes the weak closure of the convex hull of a set. This is where we needed the fact that $\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M}$ contains no semifinite and properly infinite summand, otherwise $F$ need not be faithful.
Set
\[z=F(a).\]
Since $a\neq0$ is positive,  the faithfulness of $F$ yields $z\neq 0$; hence $\varphi(z)\neq0$. We will define a new positive functional $\tilde\psi$ on $\mathcal{B}$ which will satisfy $\tilde\psi(x)=\varphi(zx)$ for $x\in \mathsf{M}$ and  the remaining
conditions in the statement. By normalizing $\tilde\psi$ by $\varphi(z)$, we will get the required state.

 Let $\{a_j\}_{j\in \Lambda}$ be a net in $\text{co}\{uau^\ast; u\in G\}$ such that $z=\text{wk}-\lim_j a_j$ for some directed set $\Lambda$. Write  $a_j=\sum_{u\in F_j}\lambda_u uau^\ast$ for some finite subset $F_j$ of $G$ and nonnegative scalars $\{\lambda_u; u\in F_j\}$ with $\sum_{u\in F_j}\;\lambda
_u=1.$ For each $j\in \Lambda$, consider the positive linear functional $\psi_j$ on $\mathcal{B}$ defined by
\begin{align*}
    \psi_j(T)=\sum_{u\in F_j}\lambda_u\psi(\sigma_{-i/2}^\varphi(u)^\ast T\sigma_{-i/2}^\varphi(u)),\;\;T\in \mathcal{B}.
\end{align*}
For $x\in \mathsf{M}$, we have
\begin{align*}
    \psi_j(x)&=\sum_{u\in F_j}\lambda_u\psi(\sigma_{-i/2}^\varphi(u)^\ast x\sigma_{-i/2}^\varphi(u))=\sum_{u\in F_j}\lambda_u\langle\varphi^{1/2}, \sigma_{-i/2}(u)^\ast x\sigma_{-i/2}^\varphi(u)\varphi^{1/2}a\rangle\\
    &=\sum_{u\in F_j}\lambda_u\langle  \sigma_{-i/2}^\varphi(u)\varphi^{1/2}, x\sigma_{-i/2}^\varphi(u)\varphi^{1/2}a\rangle=\sum_{u\in F_j}\lambda_u\langle  \varphi^{1/2}u, x\varphi^{1/2}ua\rangle\\
    &=\sum_{u\in F_j}\lambda_u\langle\varphi^{1/2}, x\varphi^{1/2}uau^\ast\rangle=\langle\varphi^{1/2}, x\varphi^{1/2}a_j\rangle.
\end{align*}
Since $\|a_j\|\leq \|a\|\leq C$, we get ${\psi_j}_{|_\mathsf{M}}\leq C\varphi$; in particular, $\|\psi_j\|=\psi_j(1)\leq C$. Let $\tilde\psi$ be a weak$^\ast$ limit point of the net $\{\psi_j\}_{j\in \Lambda}$, which exists because the net $\psi_j$ is uniformly bounded. Since $\{a_j\}_{j\in \Lambda}$ converges to $z$ and since $z\in \mathcal{Z}(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})\subseteq\mathsf{M}^\varphi$,  it follows for all $x\in \mathsf{M}$ that
\begin{align*}
    \tilde\psi(x)&=\operatorname{Lim}_j\psi_j(x)\\
    &=\operatorname{Lim}_j\langle\varphi^{1/2},x\varphi^{1/2}a_j\rangle\\
    &=\langle\varphi^{1/2}, x\varphi^{1/2}z\rangle\\
    &=\varphi(xz)\\
    &=\varphi(z^{1/2}xz^{1/2}).
\end{align*}
Moreover, for all $T\in \mathcal{B}$ and $b\in \mathsf A\cap\mathsf{M}_\infty$, since $\sigma_{i/2}^\varphi(u)$ commutes with $b$ for all $u\in G$, we obtain
\begin{align*}
  \psi(\sigma_{-i/2}^\varphi(u)^\ast Tb\sigma_{-i/2}^\varphi(u))&=\psi(\sigma_{-i/2}^\varphi(u)^\ast T\sigma_{-i/2}^\varphi(u)b)\\
  &=\psi(\sigma_i^\varphi(b)\sigma_{-i/2}^\varphi(u)^\ast T\sigma_{-i/2}^\varphi(u))\\
  &=\psi(\sigma_{-i/2}^\varphi(u)^\ast \sigma_i^\varphi(b)T\sigma_{-i/2}^\varphi(u))
\end{align*}
so that $\psi_j(Tb)=\psi_j(\sigma_i^\varphi(b)T)$ and thus $\tilde\psi(Tb)=\tilde\psi(\sigma_i^\varphi(b)T)$. Finally, if $p$ is the kernel projection of $z$ then $p\in \mathcal{Z}(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})\subseteq\mathsf{M}^\varphi$ and we have
\begin{align*}
    \psi(p)&=\langle\varphi^{1/2}, p\varphi^{1/2}a\rangle\\
    &=\langle\varphi^{1/2}, \varphi^{1/2}pa\rangle\\
    &=\varphi(pa).
\end{align*}
However, by bimodularity of $F$, we have $F(pap)=pF(a)p=pzp=0$. Since $pap\geq0$, by faithfulness of $F$, we have $pap=0$; hence $pa=0$. Thus we get $\psi(p)=0$,
and since $\psi$ is faithful on $\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})$, it follows that $p=0$  proving that $z$ has full support. 

(\ref{existence of a state conjugated by a centralizer element})$\implies$(\ref{existence of a state whose restriction is phi}) Let $\psi$ and $z$ be as in the statement of (\ref{existence of a state conjugated by a centralizer element}). Set $z_\varepsilon=\chi_{(\varepsilon,\infty)}z^{-1/2}$ and define the positive functional $\psi_\varepsilon$ on $\mathcal{B}$ by $\psi_\varepsilon(T)=\psi(z_\varepsilon Tz_\varepsilon)$, $T\in\mathcal{B}$. Since
\[\psi_\varepsilon(1)=\psi(z_\varepsilon^{2})=\varphi(z_\varepsilon^2z)=\varphi(\chi_{(\varepsilon,\infty)}(z))\leq \varphi(1)\] it follows that $\psi_\varepsilon$ is a uniformly bounded net. Let $\tilde\psi=\operatorname{Lim}_{\varepsilon\to 0}\psi_\varepsilon$ be a weak$^\ast$ limit of $\psi_\varepsilon$. Since $z$ has full support, $\chi_{(\varepsilon,\infty)}(z)\to 1$ $\sigma$-weakly as $\varepsilon\to0$ which further yields 
\begin{align*}
    \tilde\psi(x)=\operatorname{Lim}_{\varepsilon\to0}\varphi(z_\varepsilon xz_\varepsilon z)=\operatorname{Lim}_{\varepsilon\to0}\varphi(\chi_{(\varepsilon,\infty)}(z)x)=\varphi(x),\;\;\forall x\in \mathsf{M}.
\end{align*}Moreover, if $b\in\mathsf A\cap\mathsf{M}_\infty$  and $T\in \mathcal{B}$, then since $z$ commutes with $\mathsf A$, it follows that
    \begin{align*}
        \psi_\varepsilon(Tb)&=\psi(z_\varepsilon Tbz_\varepsilon)\\
        &=\psi(z_\varepsilon Tz_\varepsilon b)\\
        &=\psi(\sigma^\varphi_i(b)z_\varepsilon Tz_\varepsilon)\\
        &=\psi(z_\varepsilon\sigma^\varphi_i(b)Tz_\varepsilon)\\
        &=\psi_\varepsilon(\sigma^\varphi_i(b)T),
    \end{align*}
    and this property is clearly preserved in the weak$^\ast$ limit.


$(\ref{existence of a state whose restriction is phi})\implies(\ref{existence of a conditional expectation})$                                                                                                    
Denote by $\xi_\varphi$ the cyclic and separating  vector in $L^2(\mathsf A,\varphi_{|_\mathsf A})$ such that $\varphi(b)=\langle\xi_\varphi,b\xi_\varphi\rangle$ for $b\in \mathsf A$.
For every $T\in \mathcal{B}$, consider the sesquilinear form on $\mathsf A\xi_\varphi\times \mathsf A\xi_\varphi$ given by
    \[(x\xi_\varphi, y\xi_\varphi)\mapsto \psi(x^*Ty),\;\;\;x,y\in \mathsf A.\]
    This form is bounded because
    \begin{align*}
        |\psi(x^*Ty)|^2\leq \|T\|^2\psi(x^*x)\psi(y^*y)= \|T\|^2\varphi(x^*x)\varphi(y^*y)=\|T\|^2\|x\xi_\varphi\|^2\|y\xi_\varphi\|^2.
    \end{align*}
    Hence there exists an operator $\Phi(T)\in B(L^2(\mathsf A,\varphi))$ with $\lVert\Phi(T)\rVert\leq \lVertT\rVert$ such that 
    \[\langle x\xi_\varphi, \Phi(T)y\xi_\varphi\rangle=\psi(x^*Ty),\;\;\;x,y\in \mathsf A.\]
    We identify $L^2(\mathsf A,\varphi_{|_\mathsf A})$ as a subspace of $L^2(\mathsf{M},\varphi)$ via the inclusion $b\xi_\varphi\mapsto b\varphi^{1/2}$ and write $J_\varphi$ for the modular conjugation operator  in  $L^2(\mathsf A,\varphi_{|_\mathsf A})$.
   To show that $\Phi(T)\in \mathsf A$, one calculates the following  for all $x,y,z\in \mathsf A$ with $y\in\mathsf A\cap\mathsf{M}_\infty$:
    \begin{align*}
        \langle x\xi_\varphi, \Phi(T)J_\varphi yJ_\varphi z\xi_\varphi\rangle&=\langle x\xi_\varphi, \Phi(T)z\sigma_{-i/2}^\varphi(y^*)\xi_\varphi\rangle\\
        &=\psi(x^*Tz\sigma_{-i/2}^\varphi(y^*))\\
        &=\psi(\sigma_{i/2}^\varphi(y^*)x^*Tz)\;\;\;\;(\text{by hypothesis})\\
                                               
        &=\langle x\sigma_{-i/2}^\varphi(y)\xi_\varphi, \Phi(T)z\xi_\varphi\rangle\\
                                                                                            
        &=\langle J_\varphi y^*J_\varphi x\xi_\varphi, \Phi(T)z\xi_\varphi\rangle\\
        &=\langle x\xi_\varphi, J_\varphi yJ_\varphi \Phi(T)z\xi_\varphi\rangle
    \end{align*}
    which shows that $\Phi(T)J_\varphi yJ_\varphi=J_\varphi yJ_\varphi \Phi(T)$. Since $\mathsf A\cap\mathsf{M}_\infty$ is weakly dense in $
\mathsf A$, it follows that $\Phi(T)\in (J_\varphi\mathsf A J_\varphi)'\cap B(L^2(\mathsf A,\varphi_{|_\mathsf A}))= \mathsf A$. For $a\in \mathsf{M}$, we moreover have
    \begin{align*}
        \langle x\xi_\varphi,\Phi(a)z\xi_\varphi\rangle&=\psi(x^*az)\\
        &=\varphi(x^\ast a z)\\
        &=\langle x\varphi^{1/2},az\varphi^{1/2}\rangle\\
        &=\langle x\varphi^{1/2}, E_\mathsf A(a)z\varphi^{1/2}\rangle\\
        &
        =\langle x\xi_\varphi, E_\mathsf A(a)z\xi_\varphi\rangle
    \end{align*}
    proving that $\Phi(a)=E_\mathsf A(a)$. Therefore, $\Phi\colon \mathcal{B}\to \mathsf A$ is a norm-one projection such that $\Phi_{|_\mathsf{M}}=E_\mathsf A$.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:conditions for relative amenability}
  Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a  von Neumann algebra equipped with a normal faithful state $\varphi$, and let $\mathsf A$ be a subalgebra of $\mathsf{M}$  with $\varphi$-preserving expectation $E_\mathsf A$. Denote by $\mathsf{M}_\infty$ the algebra of $\sigma^\varphi$-analytic vectors of $\mathsf{M}$.  For a   $C^\ast$-algebra $\mathcal{B}$ containing $\mathsf{M}$ as a unital subalgebra, the following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
     \item There exists a norm-one projection $\Phi$ from $\mathcal{B}$ onto $\mathsf A$ such that $\Phi_{|_{\mathsf{M}}}=E_\mathsf A$.\label{cor:existence of a conditional expectation1}
      \item There exists a state $\psi:\mathcal{B}\to\mathbb C$ and a constant $C>0$ such that $\psi_{|_{\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})}}$ is faithful and   
        \[\psi_{|_{\mathsf{M}}}\leq C\varphi, \;\;\;\;\psi(Tb)=\psi(\sigma_i^\varphi (b)T)\]
        for $T\in \mathcal{B}$ and $b\in \mathsf A\cap \mathsf{M}_\infty$. \label{cor:existence of a state dominated by phi}
     \item There exists a  state $\psi:\mathcal{B}\to \mathbb  C$ such that $\psi_{|_{\mathsf{M}}}=\varphi$ and satisfies 
     \[\psi(Tb)=\psi(\sigma_i^\varphi(b)T)\]
            for $T\in \mathcal{B}$ and $b\in \mathsf A\cap \mathsf{M}_\infty$.\label{cor:existence of a state whose restriction is phi}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
We only need to prove (\ref{cor:existence of a state dominated by phi})$\implies$(\ref{cor:existence of a state whose restriction is phi}) because the other implications  follow the same procedure as in Proposition \ref{Prop:Equivalent conditions on relative amenability in terms of states with extra assumption on summand}. 
    Let $\psi:\mathcal{B}\to\mathbb C$ be a given state on $\mathcal{B}$ satisfying the hypotheses of (\ref{existence of a state dominated by phi}).
    
    Let $q\in \mathcal{Z}(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})$ be  the maximal projection such that $q(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})$ is semifinite and properly infinite so that $(1-q)(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})$ contains no semifinite properly infinite summand. If $q=0$,  the conclusion follows from Proposition \ref{Prop:Equivalent conditions on relative amenability in terms of states with extra assumption on summand}; so assume that $q\neq 0$.  We emphasize that $q\in \mathsf{M}^\varphi$ and we will repeatedly use the fact $\sigma_z^\varphi(q)=q$ for $z\in\mathbb C$.  Denote by \[\varphi_q:=\varphi(q\cdot q)/\varphi(q)\] the state on $q\mathsf{M} q$. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
By Lemma \ref{lem:existence of certain finite projections} below, there is a sequence of  projections in  the centralizer $q_n\in q(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})^{\varphi_{q}}=q(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M}^\varphi)$ such that $q_n\to q$ $\sigma$-strongly, each $q_nq(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})q_n$ is a finite von Neumann algebra and $\psi(q_n\cdot q_n)_{|_{q_n\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})}}$ is faithful.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        

Consider the  states $\psi_n$ and $\varphi_n$ on the compression algebras $q_n\mathcal{B} q_n$ and $q_n\mathsf{M} q_n$ respectively given  by  \[\psi_n(\cdot)=\psi(q_n\cdot q_n)/\psi(q_n) \qquad\mbox{ and }\qquad \varphi_n:=\varphi(q_n\cdot q_n)/\varphi(q_n).\]
  By virtue of $q_n$ being in  $\mathsf{M}^\varphi$ and commuting with $\mathsf A$,   each $\psi_n$ satisfies 
   \[{\psi_n}_{|_{q_n\mathsf{M} q_n}}\leq C\frac{\varphi(q_n)}{\psi(q_n)}\varphi_{n}\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad\psi_n(Tb)=\psi_n(\sigma_i^{\varphi_n}(b)T)\] for all $T\in q_n\mathcal{B} q_n$ and $\sigma^{\varphi_n}$-analytic $b\in q_n\mathsf A$. Since each
   $q_n(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})q_n=(q_n\mathsf A)'\cap q_n\mathsf{M} q_n$ is finite and  ${\psi_n}_{|_{q_n\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})}}$ is faithful, Proposition \ref{Prop:Equivalent conditions on relative amenability in terms of states with extra assumption on summand} yields a new state, say $\zeta_n$ on $q_n\mathcal{B}  q_n$, such
   that
   \[{{\zeta}_n}_{|_{q_n\mathsf{M} q_n}}=\varphi_n\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad \zeta_n(Tb)=\zeta_n(\sigma_i^{\varphi_n}(b)T)\]
   for all $T\in q_n\mathcal{B} q_n$ and $\sigma^{\varphi_n}$-analytic $b\in q_n\mathsf A$.
   Let $\omega$ be a free ultrafilter on $\mathbb N$ and define the state $\zeta:q\mathcal{B} q\to\mathbb C$ by
   \[\zeta(T)=\lim_{n\to\omega}\zeta_n(q_n Tq_n),\;\;T\in q\mathcal{B} q.\]
Since $q_n\to q$ $\sigma$-strongly,  \[\zeta(x)=\lim_{n\to\omega}\varphi_n(q_n xq_n)=\varphi(qxq)/\varphi(q)=\varphi_q(x)\] for all $x\in q\mathsf{M} q.$ Since  $q_n\in q(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M}^\varphi)$, we note that if   $b\in q\mathsf A q$ is $\sigma^{\varphi_q}$-analytic,  each $q_nbq_n$ is $\sigma^{\varphi_n}$ - analytic such that $\sigma_i^{\varphi_n}(q_n bq_n)=q_n\sigma_i^{\varphi_q}(b)q_n$, and since $q_n$ commutes with $\mathsf A$, the KMS condition of each $\zeta_n$  yields the following
\begin{align*}
    \zeta(Tb)=\zeta(\sigma_i^{\varphi_q}(b)T),\;\;\;\forall  T\in q\mathcal{B} q.
\end{align*}
If $q=1$, we are done. Otherwise, let $p:=1-q\neq 0$ and consider the state $\varphi_p:=\varphi(p\cdot p)/\varphi(p)$ on $p\mathsf{M} p$. Since $p\mathsf A'\cap p\mathsf{M} p=p(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf{M})$ contains no semifinite properly infinite summand by the maximality of $q$, we are now again in the position to invoke Proposition \ref{Prop:Equivalent conditions on relative amenability in terms of states with extra assumption on summand} for the unital inclusion $p\mathsf{M} p\subseteq p\mathcal{B} p$ to obtain a state $\eta$ on $p\mathcal{B} p$  satisfying 
\[\eta_{|_{p\mathsf{M} p}}=\varphi_{p}\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad\eta(Tb)=\eta(\sigma_i^{\varphi_p}(b)T)\] for all $T\in p\mathcal{B} p$ and $\sigma^{\varphi_p}$ - analytic $b\in p\mathsf A p$. This finishes the proof because the state $\tilde\psi:\mathcal{B}\to\mathbb C$ by
\[\tilde\psi(T)=\varphi(q)\zeta(qT q)+\varphi(p)\eta(pTp), \;\;T\in \mathcal{B}\] satisfies the required conditions.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:existence of certain finite projections}
  Let $\varphi, \psi$ be normal positive functionals on a $\sigma$-finite semifinite von Neumann algebra $\mathsf{N}$ satisfying $\psi\leq \varphi$ and such that $\varphi$ and the restriction $\psi_{|_{\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{N})}}$ are faithful. There exists a sequence $\{q_n\}_{n\geq1}$ of projections in the centralizer $\mathsf{N}^\varphi$ such that $q_n\to 1$ $\sigma$-strongly,  $q_n\mathsf{N} q_n$ is finite and $\psi(q_n\cdot q_n)$ is faithful on $\mathcal{Z}(q_n\mathsf{N} q_n)$ for each $n\geq 1$.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Let $\tau$ be a normal faithful semifinite weight on $\mathsf{N}$, and let $a$ be the positive operator affiliated to $\mathsf{N}$ such that $\varphi(x)=\tau(ax),\;\;x\in \mathsf{N}.$   
   For each $n\geq 1$, set $e_n={1}_{(1/n,\infty)}(a)\in \mathsf{N}$ and define the positive functionals $\mu_n$ on $\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{N})$ by 
   \begin{align*}
       \mu_n(z)=\psi(ze_n),\;\;z\in\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{N}).
   \end{align*}
   Since $\varphi$ is faithful, $a$ has full support; hence $e_n\to 1$ $\sigma$-strongly as $n\to\infty$. Moreover, $\psi(e_n)\uparrow\psi(1)$, so $\psi(e_n)\neq0$ for large enough $n$. We will therefore assume that $\psi(e_n)\neq0$ for all $n\geq1$, so that each $\mu_n$ is a non-zero functional. 
   Let $f_n$ be the support of $\mu_n$ in $\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{N})$ and set 
   \[q_n=e_nf_n.\]
   We show that $q_n$ satisfies the required assertion. Clearly, $e_n\in \mathsf{N}^\varphi$ as $e_na=ae_n$, and since $f_n\in \mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{N})\subseteq\mathsf{N}^\varphi$, it follows that $q_n\in\mathsf{N}^\varphi$.
   
  Write $b_n=g_n(a)$, where $g_n$ is the function on $[0,\infty)$ given by
  $g_n(t)=\frac{1}{t}1_{(1/n,\infty)}(t)$, $ t\geq 0$.
  Then $\tau(e_n)=\tau(ab_n)=\psi(b_n)<\infty$, which means each $e_n$ is a finite projection. Hence each $q_n$ is a finite projection so that $q_n\mathsf{N} q_n$ is a finite von Neumann algebra. 
  
  Clearly,  $\psi(q_n\cdot q_n)_{|_{\mathcal{Z}(q_n\mathsf{N} q_n)}}$ is faithful. Indeed, we have $\mathcal{Z}(q_n\mathsf{N} q_n)=q_n\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{N})$ and  if  $z\in\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{N})$ is a positive element such that $\psi(q_nz)=0$, then
  \begin{align*}
      \mu_n(z)=\mu_n(zf_n)=\psi(zf_ne_n)=\psi(zq_n)=0,
  \end{align*}
  showing that $zf_n=0$ as $f_n$ is the support of $\mu_n$; hence $zq_n=0$. 

 Finally we show that $f_n\to1$ $\sigma$-strongly. Since $e_n\leq e_{n+1}$, we have $\mu_n\leq \mu_{n+1}$ as positive functionals. This implies $f_n\leq f_{n+1}$ as well as $q_n\leq q_{n+1}$. Let $f_n\to f$ $\sigma$-strongly which exists by the monotonicity of $f_n$. Using $\psi(e_nf_n)=\mu_n(f_n)=\mu_n(1)=\psi(e_n)$ and the inequality $f_n\geq e_nf_n$, we obtain
 \begin{align*}
     \psi(1-f)&=\psi(1)-\lim_{n\to\infty}\psi(f_n)\\
     &\leq \psi(1)-\lim_{n\to\infty}\psi(e_nf_n)\\
&     =\psi(1)-\lim_{n\to\infty}\psi(e_n)\\
&=0.
 \end{align*}
 Since $f\in \mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{N})$ and $\psi_{|_{\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{N})}}$ is faithful, we infer $f=1$. Also since $e_n\uparrow1$ $\sigma$-strongly,  we conclude that $q_n=e_nf_n\uparrow1$ $\sigma$-strongly.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
If we take $\mathcal{B}=\langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$ in Theorem \ref{thm:conditions for relative amenability},  we get the equivalent conditions of relative amenability in terms of certain states satisfying KMS type conditions.

Note that $\mathsf B$ is amenable if and only if the basic construction $\langle \mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$ is amenable. Indeed, amenability of $\mathsf B$ is equivalent to amenability of $J\mathsf B J$, and hence to amenability of its commutant
$(J\mathsf B J)'=\langle \mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle.
$

Now suppose  that $\mathsf B$ is amenable. Then there exists a conditional expectation
\[
F:\mathbb B(L^2(\mathsf{M}))\longrightarrow \langle \mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle.
\]If $\mathsf A$ is amenable relative to $\mathsf B$ inside $\mathsf{M}$, there is a conditional expectation
$E:\langle \mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle\to \mathsf A$
whose restriction to $\mathsf{M}$ is $E_{\mathsf A}$. Consequently,
$E\circ F:\mathbb B(L^2(\mathsf{M}))\longrightarrow \mathsf A $ is a conditional expectation, showing that $\mathsf A$ is amenable.
Conversely,  if $\mathsf A$ is amenable, then by the injectivity of $\mathsf A$, the conditional expectation $E_{\mathsf A}:\mathsf{M}\to\mathsf A$ extends to a conditional expectation
$\widetilde E:\langle \mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle\longrightarrow\mathsf A$, which shows that $\mathsf A$ is amenable relative to $\mathsf B$ inside $\mathsf{M}$.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf{M}\subset \mathbb B(\mathsf{H})$ be a $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebra with faithful normal state $\varphi$. The von Neumann algebra $\mathsf{M}$ is amenable if and only if there exists a state $\psi\colon \mathbb B(\mathsf{H})\to\mathbb C$ such that $\psi|_\mathsf{M}=\varphi$ and
    \begin{equation*}
        \psi(Tx)=\psi(\sigma^\varphi_i(x)T)
    \end{equation*}
    for $T\in\mathbb B(\mathsf{H})$ and $x\in \mathsf{M}_{\infty,\sigma^\varphi}$.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
The same argument shows the following result: Let $(A,\alpha)$ be a $C^\ast$-dynamical system. For a $\beta$-KMS state $\varphi$ of $\alpha$ ($\beta\in \mathbb R$), the following properties are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item For every faithful representation $\pi:A\to  B(H)$, there exists a state $\psi\colon B(H)\to \mathbb C$ such that $\psi\circ\pi=\varphi$ and
    \begin{equation*}
        \psi(aT)=\psi(T\alpha_{i\beta}(a))
    \end{equation*}
    for all $T\in B(H)$ and $\alpha$-analytic $a\in A$.
    \item For every faithful representation $A\subset B(H)$, there exists a ucp map $\Phi\colon B(H)\to \pi_\varphi(A)^{\prime\prime}$ such that $\Phi|_A=\pi_\varphi$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop: uniform convergence of GNS-symmetric maps}
    Let $(\Psi_i)$ be a net of GNS-symmetric ucp maps on a $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebra $\mathsf{M}$ and let $\omega$ be a cofinal ultrafilter on a directed set. For every inclusion $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ and every  normal faithful state $\varphi$ on $\mathsf{M}$,  the following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\sup_{x\in\mathsf{Q}_1}{\|\Psi_i^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})-x\varphi^{1/2}}\|\to^i 0$,
        \item  $\sup_{x\in(\mathsf{Q}^\omega)_1}{\|(\Psi_i^{(2)})^\omega(x\psi^{1/2})-x\psi^{1/2}}\|\to^i 0$, where $\psi=\varphi^\omega$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Since $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{Q}^\omega$ and $(x\varphi^{1/2})^\omega=x\psi^{1/2}$ for $x\in \mathsf{Q}$, $(2)\implies(1)$ is obvious. Conversely,  if $a\in \mathsf{Q}^\omega$ with $\|a\|_\infty\leq 1$, then there exists $(x_n)\in\mathcal{M}^\omega(\mathsf{Q})$  such that $a=(x_n)_n^\omega $ and $\sup_n\lVertx_n\rVert\leq 2$.
So we have
    \begin{align*}
        \lVert(\Psi_i^{(2)})^\omega(a\psi^{1/2})-a\psi^{1/2}\rVert_2&=\lim_{n\to\omega}\lVert\Psi_i^{(2)}(x_n\varphi^{1/2})-x_n\varphi^{1/2}\rVert\\
        &\leq \sup_{y\in\mathsf{Q}, \lVerty\rVert\leq 2}\lVert\Psi_i^{(2)}(y\varphi^{1/2})-y\varphi^{1/2}\rVert.
    \end{align*}
    The right side is independent of $a\in (\mathsf{Q}^\omega)_1$ and converges to zero along $i$.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
Let $(\Psi_i)$ be a net of GNS-symmetric ucp maps on a $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebra $\mathsf{M}$ and let $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$. For every inclusion $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ and a normal faithful state $\varphi$ on $\mathsf{Q}$ such that $\mathsf{Q}$ is globally invariant under $\sigma^\varphi$,  the following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\sup\{\|\Psi_i^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})-x\varphi^{1/2}\|; x\in \mathsf{Q}(\sigma^\varphi, [-c,c]), \|x\|\leq 1\}\to^i 0$ for every $c>0$,
        \item  $\sup\{\|(\Psi_i^{(2)})^\omega(y\varphi^{1/2})-y\psi^{1/2}\|; y\in \mathsf{Q}^\omega(\sigma^\psi, [-c,c]),\|x\|\leq 1\}\to^i 0$ for every $c>0$, where $\psi=\varphi^\omega$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Since $\mathsf{Q}_{\infty,\sigma^\varphi}\subseteq\mathsf{Q}^\omega_{\infty,\sigma^\psi}$, $(2)\implies(1)$ is obvious.  For the converse, let $y\in \mathsf{Q}^\omega(\sigma^\psi, [-c,c])$, then by \cite[Proposition 2.3]{HI17} there is a sequence $y_n\in \mathsf{Q}(\sigma^\varphi, [-4c, 4c])$ such that $(y_n)\in \mathcal{M}^\omega(\mathsf{Q})$ and $y=(y_n)^\omega$. Therefore, 
        \begin{align*}
            \|(\Psi_i^{(2)})^\omega(y\psi^{1/2})-y\psi^{1/2}\|&=\lim_{n\to\omega}\|\Psi_i^{(2)}(y_n\varphi^{1/2})-y_n\varphi^{y_n\varphi^{1/2}}\|\\
            &\leq \sup\{\|\Psi_i^{(2)}(z\varphi^{1/2})-z\psi^{1/2}\|; z\in \mathsf{Q}^\omega(\sigma^\psi, [-4c,4c])\}
        \end{align*}
        and the right hand side is independent of $y$ and goes to $0$ along $i$.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:uniform convergence gives ultrapower pointwise convergence}
    Let $\omega$ be a cofinal ultrafilter on a directed set $\Lambda$, let $(\Psi_k)$ be a net of GNS-symmetric ucp maps on $\mathsf{M}$, let $\varphi$ be a normal faithful state on $\mathsf{M}$ and let $\mathsf{Q}$ be a subalgebra of $\mathsf{M}$ globally invariant under $\sigma^\varphi$.  If
    \begin{equation*}
        \lim_{k}\sup\{\lVert\Psi_k^{(2)}(a\varphi^{1/2})-a\varphi^{1/2}\rVert: a\in \operatorname{dom}(\sigma_{\pm i/2}^\varphi)\cap\mathsf{Q}, \|\sigma_{\pm i/2}^\varphi(a)\|\leq 1\}= 0,
    \end{equation*}
    then $(\Psi_k^{(2)})^\omega$ converges strongly on $L^2(\mathsf{Q}^\omega)$.
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Write $\psi=\varphi^\omega$ and note that $\mathsf{Q}^\omega$ is globally invariant under $\sigma^\psi$.  Fix
        $x=(x_n)\in\mathsf{Q}^\omega$. Since $\mathsf{Q}^\omega\psi^{1/2}$ is norm dense in $L^2(\mathsf{Q}^\omega)$, it suffices to show that $(\Psi_k^{(2)})^\omega(x\psi^{1/2})$ converges to $x\psi^{1/2}$. For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exist $y=(y_n)^\omega\in \mathsf{Q}^\omega$ such that each $y_n$ is $\sigma^\varphi$-analytic, $y$ is $\sigma^\psi$-analytic, $\|x\psi^{1/2}-y\psi^{1/2}\|\leq \varepsilon$ and $\sup_n\|\sigma^\varphi_{\pm i/2}(y_n)\|_\infty<\infty$. Thus we have
    \begin{align*}
       \lim_{k}\|(\Psi_k^{(2)})^\omega(y\psi^{1/2})-y\psi^{1/2}\|&=\lim_{k}\lim_{n\to\omega}\|\Psi_k^{(2)}(y_n\varphi^{1/2})-y_n\varphi^{1/2}\|\\
       &\leq \lim_{k}\sup_n\|\Psi_k^{(2)}(y_n\varphi^{1/2})-y_n\varphi^{1/2}\|\\
       &=0 
    \end{align*}
where the last equality is by the hypothesis.  By the contractiveness of $\Psi_k^{(2)}$, this implies that 
   \begin{align*}
            \lim_{k} \|(\Psi_k^{(2)})^\omega(x\psi^{1/2})-x\psi^{1/2}\|\leq 2\varepsilon+ \lim_{k}\|(\Psi_k^{(2)})^\omega(y\psi^{1/2})-y\psi^{1/2}\|=2\varepsilon
   \end{align*}
   and we get our required assertion as $\varepsilon>0$ is arbitrary.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:equivalent conditions for L2-rigidity}
 Let $\delta:\operatorname{dom}\delta\subseteq L^2(\mathsf{M})\to\mathsf{H}$ be a modular derivation, and let $\theta_\alpha$ be the associated deformation. For an inclusion $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ with expectation, the following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
    \item For any normal faithful state $\varphi$ on $\mathsf{M}$ such that $\mathsf{Q}$ is globally invariant under $\sigma^\varphi$, we have
    \begin{align*}
        \lim_{\alpha\to\infty}\|\theta_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})-x\varphi^{1/2}\|; x\in\operatorname{dom}(\sigma_{\pm i/2}^\varphi)\cap\mathsf{Q}, \|\sigma^\varphi_{\pm i/2}(x)\|_\infty\leq 1\}=0.
    \end{align*}\label{st:for any faithful state}
    \item For some normal faithful state $\varphi$ on $\mathsf{M}$ such that $\mathsf{Q}$ is globally invariant under $\sigma^\varphi$, we have
    \begin{align*}
        \lim_{\alpha\to\infty}\|\theta_\alpha^{(2)}(x\varphi^{1/2})-x\varphi^{1/2}\|; x\in\operatorname{dom}(\sigma_{\pm i/2}^\varphi)\cap\mathsf{Q}, \|\sigma^\varphi_{\pm i/2}(x)\|_\infty\leq 1\}=0.
    \end{align*}\label{st:for some faithful state}
        \item $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ converges strongly on the set $L^2(\mathsf{Q}^\omega)$ as $\alpha\to\infty$, for every cofinal ultrafilter $\omega$ on a directed set.\label{st: for any ultrafilter}
        \item $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ converges strongly on the set $L^2(\mathsf{Q}^\omega)$ as $\alpha\to\infty$, for some $\omega\in \beta \mathbb N\setminus \mathbb N$.\label{st:for some ultrafilter}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
$(\ref{st:for any faithful state})\implies(\ref{st:for some faithful state})$ is obvious.
        
        $(\ref{st:for some faithful state})\implies(\ref{st: for any ultrafilter})$ follows from Lemma \ref{lem:uniform convergence gives ultrapower pointwise convergence}.
        
   $(\ref{st: for any ultrafilter})\implies(\ref{st:for some ultrafilter})$ is obvious.

  $(\ref{st:for some ultrafilter})\implies(\ref{st:for any faithful state})$  Suppose that $(\ref{st:for any faithful state})$ fails for some normal faithful state $\varphi$ on $\mathsf{M}$ for which $\mathsf{Q}$ is globally invariant under $\sigma^\varphi$, so  there exist $\delta>0$,  a sequence  $(\alpha_n)$ in $\mathbb N$ and a sequence $x_{n}\in\operatorname{dom}(\sigma^\varphi_{i/2})\cap \operatorname{dom}(\sigma^\varphi_{-i/2})\cap\mathsf{Q}$ with $\lVert\sigma^\varphi_{\pm i/2}(x_n)\rVert\leq 1$  such that $\|\theta_{\alpha_n}^{(2)}(x_{n}\varphi^{1/2})-x_n\varphi^{1/2}\|\geq \delta$.
  
We show that $(x_n)\in\mathcal{M}^\omega(\mathsf{Q})$. First note that by the maximum principle for analytic functions, $\lVertx_n\rVert\leq \max\{\lVert\sigma^\varphi_{-i/2}(x_n)\rVert,\lVert\sigma^\varphi_{i/2}(x_n)\rVert\}\leq 1$. Now, if $(y_n)\in\mathsf{Q}$ is a net such that $\|y_n\|_\varphi^\sharp\to0$ as $n\to\omega$, then we have
    \begin{align*}
        \varphi(y_n^\ast x_n^\ast x_n y_n+x_n y_n y_n^\ast x_n^\ast)
        &\leq \lVertx_n\rVert^2\varphi(y_n^\ast y_n)+\lVert\sigma^\varphi_{-i/2}(x_n)\rVert^2\varphi(y_n y_n^\ast)\\
        &\leq \varphi(y_n^\ast y_n+y_n y_n^\ast)\\
        &\to 0
    \end{align*}
    and
    \begin{align*}
        \varphi(x_n^\ast y_n^\ast y_n x_n+y_n x_n x_n^\ast y_n^\ast)
        &\leq \lVert\sigma^\varphi_{i/2}(x_n)\rVert^2\varphi(y_n^\ast y_n)+\lVertx_n\rVert^2\varphi(y_n y_n^\ast)\\
        &\leq \varphi(y_n^\ast y_n+y_n y_n^\ast)\\
        &\to 0.
    \end{align*}
  Set $x=(x_n)^\omega\in\mathsf{Q}^\omega$. By assumption, $(\theta_{\alpha}^{(2)})^\omega(x(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2})$  converges to $x(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}$ as $\alpha\to\infty$, so there is some $\alpha>0$ such that
    \begin{equation*}
\lim_{n\to\omega}\|{\theta_{\alpha}^{(2)}(x_n\varphi^{1/2})-x_n\varphi^{1/2}}\|=  \|(\theta_{\alpha}^{(2)})^\omega  (x(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2})-x(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}\|\leq  \delta/2.
    \end{equation*}
However, for $\alpha_n\geq\alpha$, we have
\begin{align*}
  \|\theta^{(2)}_{\alpha}(x_n\varphi^{1/2})-x_n\varphi^{1/2}\|\geq  \|\theta^{(2)}_{\alpha_n}(x_n\varphi^{1/2})-x_n\varphi^{1/2}\|\geq\delta
\end{align*}
leading to a contradiction, where the last inequality follows because $(\theta_\beta^{(2)}-id)^2$ is decreasing; that is,  for any
$\beta\geq\alpha$ and $\xi\in L^2(\mathsf{M})$, if $E$ denotes the spectral projection of $\mathcal{L}_2$, then
    \begin{align*}
       \|\theta_{\alpha}^{(2)}(\xi)-\xi\|^2
        &=\int_{[0,\infty)}\left\lvert1-\frac{\alpha}{\lambda+\alpha}\right\rvert^2\,d\lVertE(\lambda)\xi\rVert^2\\
        &=\int_{[0,\infty)}\frac{\lambda^2}{(\lambda+\alpha)^2}\,d\lVertE(\lambda)\xi\rVert^2\\
        &\geq \int_{[0,\infty)}\frac{\lambda^2}{(\lambda+\beta)^2}\,d\lVertE(\lambda)\xi\rVert^2\\
        &=\|\theta_\beta^{(2)}(\xi)-\xi\|^2.
    \end{align*}    
This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\label{def: L2 rigidity}
Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebra and let $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq 1_\mathsf{Q}\mathsf{M} 1_\mathsf{Q}$, $\mathsf B\subseteq \mathsf{M}$   be inclusions of von Neumann algebras with expectations. We say that $\mathsf{Q}$ is {\em coarsely rigid relative to $\mathsf B$ inside $\mathsf{M}$} if for every modular derivation $\delta\colon \operatorname{dom}(\delta)\subset L^2(\mathsf{M})\to \mathsf{H}$  with $\mathsf B\subseteq\operatorname{Null}(\bar\delta)$ and ${_\mathsf{M}}\mathsf{H}_\mathsf{M}\prec {_\mathsf{M}}L^2(\mathsf{M} )\otimes_\mathsf B\mathsf{K}\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M})_\mathsf{M}$ for some $\mathsf B$-$\mathsf B$ correspondence $\mathsf{K}$, the associated deformation $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ converges strongly on $L^2(\mathsf{Q}^\omega)$  to the identity as $\alpha\to\infty$   for some  free ultrafilter $\omega$ on $\mathbb N$. We call a von Neumann algebra $\mathsf{M}$  {\em coarsely rigid} if $\mathsf{M}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ is coarsely rigid relative to $\mathbb C$.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
\label{ex:comparision of different rigidity notion}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item  If $\mathsf{M}$ is a tracial von Neumann algebra with Property (T), then $\mathsf{M}$ is coarsely rigid.
