More generally, if $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ is an inclusion of tracial von Neumann algebras with relative Property (T) (see \cite{Pop06}), then the inclusion $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ is  coarsely rigid relative to $\mathsf B$ for every subalgebra $\mathsf B$ of $\mathsf{M}$.
    
  However, Property (T) is a stronger notion  than coarse rigidity.  For example,  take $\mathsf{M}=L\mathbb F_2\bar\otimes L\mathbb F_2$, where $\mathbb F_2$ is the free group of 2 symbols. Then $\mathsf{M}$  does not have Property (T). Indeed this is because $L\mathbb F_2$ does not have Property (T), e.g. the trace preserving ucp map determined by the assignment $u_g\otimes u_h\mapsto e^{-t|g|}u_g\otimes u_h$, $g,h\in \mathbb F_2$ does not converge uniformly on the unit ball of $L\mathbb F_2\bar\otimes 1$ in $L^2$-norm as $t\to0$. 
    
    On the other hand, $\mathsf{M}$ is coarsely rigid by Corollary \ref{cor: tensor product of nonamenable factors are coarse rigid} below.
  \item   If $\mathsf{M}$ is a coarsely rigid tracial von Neumann algebra, then $\mathsf{M}$ is $L^2$-rigid in the sense of \cite{Pet09}. However, coarse rigidity is a strictly stronger notion than $L^2$-rigidity.
  
  For example, take $\mathsf{M}=L\mathbb F_2\bar\otimes\mathcal{R}$, where  $\mathcal{R}$ is the separable hyperfinite II$_1$ factor. Since $\mathsf{M}$ is a nonamenable nonprime factor, it follows from \cite[Corollary 4.6]{Pet09} that  $\mathsf{M}$ is $L^2$-rigid. 
  
  On the other hand, $\mathsf{M}$ is not coarsely rigid. Indeed, since  $L\mathbb F_2$ is not $L^2$-rigid (\cite[Remark 3.2]{Pet09}), there is a trace-symmetric derivation 
$\delta:\operatorname{dom}(\delta)\subseteq \ell^2(\mathbb F_2)\to \left(\ell^2(\mathbb F_2)\otimes \ell^2(\mathbb F_2)\right)^{\oplus \infty}$ such that the associated deformation $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ does not converge strongly to the identity on $L^2((L\mathbb F_2)^\omega)$, as $\alpha\to\infty$, for any $\omega\in \beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$ (in fact, one can take the derivation associated to the length function). Now consider  the modular derivation $\partial:=\delta\otimes 1$ on $L^2(\mathsf{M})$ which takes values in $\left(\ell^2(\mathbb F_2)\otimes \ell^2(\mathbb F_2)\right)^{\oplus \infty}\otimes L^2(\mathcal{R})$ and whose associated deformation is $\eta_\alpha:=\theta_\alpha\otimes \operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{R}}$. Clearly, $(\eta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ does not converge strongly to the identity on $L^2(\mathsf{M}^\omega)$,  even if $\left(\ell^2(\mathbb F_2)\otimes \ell^2(\mathbb F_2)\right)^{\oplus \infty}\otimes L^2(\mathcal{R})$ is weakly contained in $L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2(\mathsf{M})$ as $\mathsf{M}$-correspondence because $\mathcal{R}$ is amenable.
 \label{ex:L2 rigid bur not coarse rigid}

 \item More generally, for any $L^2$-rigid tracial von Neumann algebra $\mathsf{N}$ and any  hyperfinite factor $\mathsf{Q}$ (of type II$_\infty$ or of type III) the algebra $\mathsf{M}=\mathsf{N}\bar\otimes \mathsf{Q}$ is not coarsely rigid by the same argument as above.
 \item If a diffuse von Neumann algebra $\mathsf{M}$ admits a modular derivation  whose associated deformations $\theta_\alpha^{(2)}$ are compact for each $\alpha>0$, then $\mathsf{M}$ is not coarsely rigid by Proposition \ref{prop:convergence of deformation with compact resolvent gives atomicity}. For example, $\mathsf{M}=\Gamma(U_t, \mathsf{H}_{\mathbb R})$ if the free Araki-Woods factors for $\dim\mathsf{H}_{\mathbb R}<\infty$ (see Sec \ref{sec:Examples} for the construction.)

 \item By the same argument as in \cite[Remark 4.2]{Pet09}, one shows that $\mathsf{M}_1\bar\ast\mathsf{M}_2$ is not coarsely rigid for any diffuse von Neumann algebras $\mathsf{M}_1,\mathsf{M}_2$ (see Sec \ref{sec:Examples} for construction of a derivation in the coarse bimodule).
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{An inequality on the norm of certain operator}
 If $\pi_\ell$ and $\pi_r$ are (not necessarily normal)  $\ast$-homomorphisms of $\mathsf{M}$ and $\mathsf{M}^\mathrm{op}$ respectively with commuting ranges, then $\lVert\sum_i\pi_\ell(x_i)\pi_r(x_i^\ast)\rVert\leq \|\sum_ixJx_iJ\|$  for any $x_i, 1\leq i\leq n$. In particular, if  $\mathsf{H}$ is a Hilbert $\mathsf{M}$-correspondence, then we have $\lVert\sum_i\pi_\mathsf{H}(x_i^\ast\otimes x_i^{\operatorname{op}})\rVert\leq \lVert\sum_i x_i^\ast Jx_i^\ast J\rVert$.
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{Norm estimate of involving certain ucp maps}
    Let $\mathsf B\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ be a unital inclusion of von Neumann algebras. For $i\in \{1,2\}$ let $\mathsf{H}_i$ be an $\mathsf{M}$-$\mathsf B$ correspondence, let $\mathsf{K}_i$ be a $\mathsf B$-$\mathsf B$ correspondence such that $_\mathsf{M}(\mathsf{H}_i)_\mathsf B\prec {_\mathsf{M} L^2(\mathsf{M})}\otimes_\mathsf B (\mathsf{K}_i)_\mathsf B$ and let $V_i:L^2(\mathsf{M})\to\mathsf{H}_i$ be  right $\mathsf B$-linear contractions. If $\theta_i:\mathsf{M}\to \langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$ is the completely positive map given by $\theta_i(x)=V_i^\ast\pi_l^{\mathsf{H}_i}(x) V_i$, $x\in\mathsf{M}$, then we have
    \begin{align*}
        \left\lVert\sum_{j=1}^n\theta_1(x_j^\ast)\otimes_\mathsf B\theta_2(x_j)^{\operatorname{op}}\right\rVert\leq \left\lVert\sum_{j=1}^n x_j^\ast\otimes_\mathsf B x_j^{\operatorname{op}}\right\rVert
    \end{align*}
 for $x_i\in\mathsf{M}, 1\leq i\leq n$,   where $x\otimes_\mathsf B y^{\operatorname{op}}$ is the operator on $L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M})$ as defined before.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Since $V_i$ is right $\mathsf B$-linear, it is clear that $\theta_i(x)\in \langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$. By definition,
    \begin{equation*}
        \theta_1(x)\otimes_\mathsf B \theta_2(y)^{\mathrm{op}}=(V_1^\ast\otimes_\mathsf B V_2^\ast)(\pi_l^{\mathsf{H}_1}(x)\otimes_\mathsf B \pi_r^{\bar\mathsf{H}_2}(y^{\operatorname{op}}))(V_1\otimes_\mathsf B V_2)
    \end{equation*}
    for all $x,y\in \mathsf{M}$.

    Since $\lVertV_1^\ast\otimes_\mathsf B V_2^\ast\rVert=\lVertV_1\otimes_\mathsf B V_2\rVert\leq \lVertV_1\rVert\lVertV_2\rVert\leq 1$, we get
    \begin{equation*}
        \left\lVert \sum_{j=1}^n \theta_1(x_j)^\ast\otimes_\mathsf B \theta_2(x_j)^\mathrm{op}\right\rVert\leq \left\lVert\sum_{j=1}^n \pi_l^{\mathsf{H}_1}(x_j)^\ast\otimes_\mathsf B \pi_r^{{\bar \mathsf{H}_2}}(x_j^\mathrm{op}) \right\rVert.
    \end{equation*}
    Since ${_\mathsf{M} (\mathsf{H}_1)}\otimes_\mathsf B (\overline{H_2})_\mathsf{M}\prec _\mathsf{M} L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes_\mathsf B \mathsf{K}_1\otimes_\mathsf B \overline{\mathsf{K}_2}\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M})_\mathsf{M}$ by \cite[Lemma 1.7]{AD95}, we obtain
    \begin{equation*}
        \left\lVert\sum_{j=1}^n \pi_l^{\mathsf{H}_1}(x_j)^\ast\otimes_\mathsf B \pi_r^{{\bar \mathsf{H}_2}}(x_j^\mathrm{op}) \right\rVert\leq \left\lVert\sum_{j=1}^n \pi_l^{L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes_\mathsf B \mathsf{K}_1}(x_j)^\ast\otimes_\mathsf B \pi_r^{{\bar\mathsf{K}_2\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M})}}(x_j^\mathrm{op}) \right\rVert.
    \end{equation*}
    Finally, as the left action of $\mathsf{M}$ on $_\mathsf{M} L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes_\mathsf B \mathsf{K}_1$ and the right action on $\bar\mathsf{K}_2\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M})_\mathsf{M}$ can be extended to actions of $\langle \mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$ and ${_{\langle M,B\rangle}L^2(\mathsf{M})}\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M})_{\langle M,B\rangle}\cong {_{\langle M,B\rangle}L^2(\langle \mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle)_{\langle M,B\rangle}}$ by \cite[Proposition 3.1]{Sau83}, the claim follows from Lemma \ref{An inequality on the norm of certain operator}.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
\label{rmk:weak_containment_deformations}
    Let $\Phi\colon \mathsf{M}\to \mathsf{M}$ be a normal ucp map and $(\pi,\mathsf{H},V)$ a minimal Stinespring triple for $\theta$, that is, $\mathsf{H}$ is a Hilbert space, $\pi\colon \mathsf{M}\to \mathbb B(\mathsf{H})$ is a normal unital $\ast$-homomorphism and $V\colon L^2(\mathsf{M})\to \mathsf{H}$ is an isometry such that $\text{span}\{\pi(x)V\eta\mid x\in \mathsf{M},\eta\in L^2(\mathsf{M})\}$ is dense in $\mathsf{H}$ and $\Phi=V^\ast\pi(\cdot)V$. One can turn $\mathsf{H}$ into an $\mathsf{M}$-$\mathsf{M}$ correspondence by defining $\pi_l^\mathsf{H}=\pi$ and
    \begin{equation*}
        \pi_r^\mathsf{H}(y^\mathrm{op})\pi(x)V\eta=\pi(x)V(\eta y)
    \end{equation*}
    for $x,y\in \mathsf{M}$ and $\eta\in L^2(\mathsf{M})$. We call $\mathsf{H}$ with these bimodule actions the {\em minimal Stinespring correspondence} and denote it by $\mathsf{H}_\Phi$.

    Now let $(\Phi_t)_{t\geq 0}$ be a GNS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroup and recall the definitions of the families of ucp maps  $(\zeta_\alpha)_{\alpha>0}$, $(\theta_\alpha)_{\alpha>0}$ and $(\rho_\alpha)_{\alpha>0}$ from Remark~\ref{rmk:ucp_families}. It follows easily from the integral formulas given there that
    \begin{align*}
        {_\mathsf{M}(\mathsf{H}_{\theta_\alpha})_\mathsf{M}}&\subset \int_{\mathbb R_+} ^\oplus {_\mathsf{M} (\mathsf{H}_{\Phi_t})_\mathsf{M}}\,\alpha e^{-\alpha t}dt,\\
        {_\mathsf{M}(\mathsf{H}_{\zeta_\alpha})_\mathsf{M}}&\subset \int_{\mathbb{R}_+}^\oplus {_\mathsf{M}(\mathsf{H}_{\theta_{\alpha(1+t)/t}})_\mathsf{M}}\frac{dt}{\pi(1+t)\sqrt t},\\
        {_\mathsf{M}(\mathsf{H}_{\rho_\alpha})_\mathsf{M}}&\subset \int_{\mathbb R_+}^\oplus {_\mathsf{M}(\mathsf{H}_{\theta_{t\alpha/(1+t)}})_\mathsf{M}}\frac{dt}{\pi(1+t)\sqrt t}.
    \end{align*}
    In particular, if there exists a $\mathsf B$-$\mathsf B$ correspondence $\mathsf{K}_t$ such that ${_\mathsf{M} (\mathsf{H}_{\Phi_t})_\mathsf B}\prec _\mathsf{M} L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes_\mathsf B (\mathsf{K}_t)_\mathsf B$ for all $t\geq 0$, then the same is true for $\mathsf{H}_{\eta_\alpha}$, $\mathsf{H}_{\zeta_\alpha}$ and $\mathsf{H}_{\theta_\alpha}$.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- example-2: body_md -->
\label{ex:weak_containment_amenable}
    If $\mathsf B$ is amenable, then $ {_\mathsf B}L^2(\mathsf B)_\mathsf B\prec  {_\mathsf B}L^2(\mathsf B)\otimes L^2(\mathsf B)_\mathsf B$, so for any $\mathsf{M}$-$\mathsf B$ correspondence $\mathsf{H}$ we have \begin{align*}
        {_\mathsf{M}}\mathsf{H}_{\mathsf B}&\cong  {_\mathsf{M}}\mathsf{H}\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf B)_\mathsf B\prec  {_\mathsf{M}}\mathsf{H}\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf B)\otimes L^2(\mathsf B)_\mathsf B\\
        &\cong {_\mathsf{M}}\mathsf{H}\otimes L^2(\mathsf B)_\mathsf B\prec  {_\mathsf{M}}L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2(\mathsf B)_\mathsf B\\
        &\prec  {_\mathsf{M} L^2(\mathsf{M})}\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf B)\otimes L^2(\mathsf B)_\mathsf B
    \end{align*}
    where we  used the fact that ${_\mathsf{M}\mathsf{H}_{\mathbb C}}\subset {_\mathsf{M} (L^2(\mathsf{M})}\otimes \ell^2(S))_{\mathbb C}\prec  {_\mathsf{M} L^2(\mathsf{M})}_{\mathbb C}$  by the representation theory of von Neumann algebras, where $S$ is a possibly uncountable set.
<!-- end example-2 -->
<!-- example-3: body_md -->
Let $G$ be a discrete group, $H$ a subgroup of $G$ and $\pi\colon G\to \mathcal U(\tilde\mathsf{H})$ a unitary representation. If we let $\mathsf{M}=L(G)$, $\mathsf B=L(H)$, then $\mathsf{H}=\tilde\mathsf{H}\otimes\ell^2(G)$ becomes an $\mathsf{M}$-$\mathsf{M}$ correspondence when endowed with the bimodule actions given by $\pi_l^\mathsf{H}(\lambda(g))=\pi(g)\otimes\lambda(g)$ and $\pi_r^\mathsf{H}(\lambda(g)^{\mathrm{op}})=1\otimes \rho(g^{-1})$. With the unitary $U\colon \mathsf{H}\to \mathsf{H}$, $\eta\otimes 1_g\mapsto \pi(g^{-1})\eta\otimes 1_g$ we get $U\pi_l^\mathsf{H}(x)U^\ast=1\otimes x$ and $U\pi_r^\mathsf{H}(\lambda(g)^{\mathrm{op}})U^\ast=\pi(g^{-1})\otimes \rho(g^{-1})$. It follows that $U^\ast(1\otimes T)U\in \pi_r^\mathsf{H}(\mathsf B^{\mathrm{op}})^\prime$ for $T\in \langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$. Thus there exists a $\mathsf B$-$\mathsf B$ correspondence $\mathsf{K}$ such that ${_\mathsf{M}\mathsf{H}}_\mathsf B\cong {_\mathsf{M} L^2(\mathsf{M})}\otimes_\mathsf B \mathsf{K}_\mathsf B$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:ext_bimodule_action}.
<!-- end example-3 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{A result of Woronowicz on self-polar forms}
    Let $\mathsf{M}$  be a von Neumann algebra with a normal faithful state $\varphi$. Let $s:\mathsf{M}\times\mathsf{M}\to\mathbb C$ be a bipositive positive-definite sesquilinear form such that $s(x,1)=\varphi(x),  x\in \mathsf{M}$. Then $s(x,x)\leq s_\varphi(x,x)$ for all $x\in \mathsf{M}$.
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{A Hahn-Banach type theorem}
    Let $C$ be a convex cone of a real vector space $V$, and let $p,q:V\to\mathbb R$ be maps such that $p,-q$  are sublinear  satisfying $q(c)\leq p(c)$ for $c\in C.$  Then there is a linear functional $\psi$ on $V$ such that $\psi(x)\leq p(x)$ and $q(c)\leq \psi(c)$ for all $x\in V,c\in C.$
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{main_theorem}
    Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebra,  let $\delta\colon \operatorname{dom}(\delta)\subset L^2(\mathsf{M})\to \mathsf{H}$ be a densely defined closable  modular derivation with associated quantum Markov semigroup $(\Phi_t)_{t\geq 0}$ and let $\mathsf B\subseteq\operatorname{Null}(\bar\delta)$. Assume that there exists an $\langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$-$\langle \mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$ correspondence $\mathsf{K}$ and $\langle \mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$-$\mathsf B$ correspondences $\mathsf{K}_t$ for $t\geq 0$ such that $_\mathsf{M}\mathsf{H}_\mathsf{M}\prec {_\mathsf{M}\mathsf{K}}_\mathsf{M}$ and $_\mathsf{M}(\mathsf{H}_{\Phi_t})_\mathsf B\prec {_\mathsf{M}(\mathsf{K}_t)}_\mathsf B$.
    
   For an inclusion $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq 1_\mathsf{Q}\mathsf{M} 1_\mathsf{Q}$ of von Neumann algebras  with expectation, at least one of the following holds:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item There is a non-zero projection $p\in {\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{Q}'\cap1_\mathsf{Q} \mathsf{M}1_\mathsf{Q})}$ such that $p\mathsf{Q}$ is amenable relative to $\mathsf B$.
        \item $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ strongly  converges to the identity on $L^2(\mathsf{Q}'\cap 1_\mathsf{Q}\mathsf{M}^\omega1_\mathsf{Q})$ as $\alpha\to\infty$ for every cofinal ultrafilter $\omega$ on a directed set.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
We shall prove the result when $1_\mathsf{Q}=1_\mathsf{M}$ just to avoid notational complications. The general case will follow from the same argument (see Remark \ref{rem:proof of the main theorem:general case} below).

 Therefore, for the remainder of the proof, we assume that $1_\mathsf{Q}=1_\mathsf{M}$ and $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ does not converge to the identity on $L^2(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega)$ as $\alpha\to\infty$ for some cofinal ultrafilter $\omega$.
 Let $\varphi$ be a normal faithful state on $\mathsf{M}$ such that $\mathsf{Q}$  is globally invariant under $\sigma^\varphi$. We emphasize here that the derivation $\delta$ need not be modular with respect to $\varphi$, and in particular, $\sigma^\varphi_t$ need not commute with $\theta_\alpha$, $t\in\mathbb R, \alpha>0$. Nevertheless, the following computations go through smoothly without any trouble. Our goal is to construct a state $\psi$ on $\langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$ and a nonzero projection $p\in\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M})$  such that $\psi_{|_{\mathcal{Z}(p(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}))}}$ is faithful and satisfies the KMS conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:conditions for relative amenability}.
 
Clearly, the algebra $\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega$ is globally invariant under $\sigma^{\varphi^\omega},$ which means that
  the  algebra $\mathcal{A}$ consisting of $\sigma^{\varphi^\omega}$-analytic elements of $\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega$ is strongly dense in $\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega$; hence $\mathcal{A}(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}$ is norm dense in $L^2(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega)$. Therefore, there is some $d\in \mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega$ which is $\sigma^{\varphi^\omega}$-analytic such that $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega(d(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2})$ does not converge to $d(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}$. Here $(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}$ denotes the unique vector in  the positive cone $L^2(\mathsf{M}^\omega)_+$ associated to the state $\varphi^\omega$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                   
                 
                                                            
   Since
   \[\|\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha}(d(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2})\|\geq \|(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega(d(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2})-d(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}\|,\] it follows that  $\|\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha}(d(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2})\|$ does not converge to $0$. Choose $C>0$ and  an increasing sequence $\alpha_n$ of positive numbers converging to $\infty$ such that $\|\delta_{\alpha_n}(d(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2})\|\geq C$ for all $n\geq1$. Set 
    \begin{align*}
     d_n=\frac{d}{\|\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(d(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2})\|} \in \mathsf{M}^\omega,\;\;\;\;   \xi_n:= d_n(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}\in L^2(\mathsf{M}^\omega)^\omega
    \end{align*}
    so that each ${\tilde\delta^\omega
     _{\alpha_n}(\xi_n)}$ is a unit vector and $\|d_n\|_\infty\leq \frac{\|d\|_\infty}{C}$.
Now we consider the following spaces:
\begin{align*}
    &\mathcal{V}:=\text{span}\{x\otimes y^{\operatorname{op}}; x,y\in \mathsf{M}\}\subseteq \langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle\otimes_{\min,\mathsf B}\langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle^{\operatorname{op}},\\
    &\mathcal{C}:=\{\sum_jx_j^\ast \otimes x_j^{\operatorname{op}}; x_j \in \mathsf{M}\}.
\end{align*}
Then $\mathcal{C}$ is a cone in the  vector space $\mathcal{V}$.  Now consider the following maps on $\mathcal{V}$ given by 
\begin{align*}
&f(T):=\|\sum_ix_i\otimes_\mathsf B y_i^{\operatorname{op}}\|\\
&g(T)=\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Lim}_n\langle\tilde\delta_{\alpha_n}^\omega(\xi_n), \sum_i\pi_{\mathsf{H}^\omega}(\zeta_{\alpha_n}(x_i)\otimes\zeta_{\alpha_n}(y_i)^{\operatorname{op}})\tilde\delta_{\alpha_n}^\omega(\xi_n)\rangle\\
&\qquad=\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Lim}_n\sum_i\langle\tilde\delta_{\alpha_n}^\omega(\xi_n),\zeta_{\alpha_n}(x_i)\tilde\delta_{\alpha_n}^\omega(\xi_n) \zeta_{\alpha_n}(y_i)\rangle\end{align*}
for $T=\sum_ix_i\otimes y_i^{\operatorname{op}}\in \mathcal{V}$, where $\operatorname{Lim}_n$ is a Banach limit on $\ell^\infty(\mathbb N)$. By Corollary \ref{cor; corollary to the technical lemma in the ultrapower language},  we have
for all $x,y\in \mathsf{M}$ that
\begin{align*}
    \operatorname{Lim}_n\|\zeta_{\alpha_n}(x)\tilde\delta_{\alpha_n}^\omega(d(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2})\zeta_{\alpha_n}(y)-\tilde\delta_{\alpha_n}^\omega(xd(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}y)\|=0,
\end{align*}
and since $\|\tilde\delta_{\alpha_n}^\omega(d(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2})\|\geq C$ for all $n\geq 1$, it follows that
\begin{align}\label{eq:a consequence of technical lemma}
  \operatorname{Lim}_n\|\zeta_{\alpha_n}(a)&\tilde\delta_{\alpha_n}^\omega(\xi_n)\zeta_{\alpha_n}(b)-\tilde\delta_{\alpha_n}^\omega(a\xi_nb)\|\\
  &\leq \frac{1}{C}   \operatorname{Lim}_n\|\zeta_{\alpha_n}(a)\tilde\delta_{\alpha_n}^\omega(d(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2})\zeta_{\alpha_n}(b)-\tilde\delta_{\alpha_n}^\omega(ad(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}b)\|=0\nonumber,
\end{align}
which can then be used to rewrite the expression for $g$ as follows:
\begin{align*}
 g(x\otimes y^{\operatorname{op}})=\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Lim}_n\langle\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(\xi_n), \tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(x \xi_n y)\rangle,\quad x,y\in\mathsf{M}.
   
                                                  
                                        
\end{align*}
We shall repeatedly use the expression \eqref{eq:a consequence of technical lemma} in the sequel without always referring to it. Since $\mathsf{K}$ is a $\langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$-$\langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$ correspondence, and since ${_\mathsf{M}}{\mathsf{H}^\omega}_\mathsf{M}\prec{_\mathsf{M}}{\mathsf{H}}_\mathsf{M}\prec {_\mathsf{M}}\mathsf{K}_\mathsf{M}$ and $_\mathsf{M}(\mathsf{H}_{\zeta_\alpha})_\mathsf B\prec {_\mathsf{M} L^2(\mathsf{M})}\otimes_\mathsf B (\mathsf{K}_\alpha)_\mathsf B$ for some $\mathsf B$-$\mathsf B$ correspondence $\mathsf{K}_\alpha$ as discussed in Remark~\ref{rmk:weak_containment_deformations}, it follows from Lemma \ref{Norm estimate of involving certain ucp maps} that 
\begin{align*}
    \lVert\pi_{\mathsf{H}^\omega}(\sum_i\zeta_{\alpha_n}(x_i^\ast)\otimes\zeta_{\alpha_n}(x_i)^{\mathrm{op}})\rVert&\leq \lVert\pi_\mathsf{K}(\sum_i\zeta_{\alpha_n}(x_i^\ast)\otimes\zeta_{\alpha_n}(x_i)^{\mathrm{op}})\rVert\\
    &\leq \|\sum_i\zeta_{\alpha_n}(x_i^\ast)\otimes_\mathsf B\zeta_{\alpha_n}(x_i)^{\mathrm{op}}\|\\
    &\leq \|\sum_ix_i^\ast\otimes_\mathsf B {x_i}^{\mathrm{op}}\|
\end{align*}
for all $n\in\mathbb N$; hence we have
$g\leq f$ on $\mathcal{C}.$  Moreover, $f,-g$ are sublinear (in fact, $g$ is linear). We use Lemma \ref{A Hahn-Banach type theorem} by considering $\mathcal{V}$ as a real vector space, so  that  there exists a complex  linear map $\psi$ on $\mathcal{V}$ such that 
\[\operatorname{Re}\psi\leq f\;\;\mbox{on }\mathcal{V} \mbox{ and }g\leq \operatorname{Re}\psi\;\;\mbox{on }\mathcal{C}.\]
This implies   that $\|\psi(T)\|\leq \|T\|$ for $T\in \mathcal{V}$, so  $\psi$ extends to a bounded linear map, still denoted by $\psi$ on $\langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle\otimes_{\min,\mathsf B}\langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle^{\operatorname{op}}$ such that $\|\psi\|\leq 1$. Moreover, since $\zeta_{\alpha_n}$ is unital, it follows that $1=g(1\otimes_\mathsf B 1)\leq \psi(1\otimes_\mathsf B 1)$; hence $\psi$ is a state on $\langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle\otimes_{\min,\mathsf B}\langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle^{\operatorname{op}}$.  Define the state $\tilde\psi:\langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle\to \mathbb{C} $ by 
  \[\tilde\psi(T)=\frac{1}{2}\psi(T\otimes_\mathsf B1+1\otimes_\mathsf B T^{\operatorname{op}}),\;\;T\in \langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle.\]
  We choose to work with the above symmetrization  rather than $\psi(T\otimes 1)$ in order to consider certain bi-positive and positive-definite sesquilinear forms in the sequel.
We make the following two claims:
\\
\\
{\em Claim 1}: $\tilde\psi_{|_\mathsf{M}}\leq   C_1\varphi$ for some constant $C_1>0$, and
\\
  {\em Claim 2:} There is a projection $p\in\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{Q})$ such that $\tilde\psi(Ta)=\tilde\psi(\sigma^\varphi_i(a)T)$ for $T\in\langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$ and $a\in p\mathsf{Q}_\infty$.
  \\
  \\
 For this purpose,
 consider the sesquilinear forms $s,t$ on $\mathsf{M}\times\mathsf{M}$ given by 
\begin{align*}
&t(x,y)=\frac{1}{2}\psi(x\otimes_\mathsf B{y^\ast}^{\operatorname{op}}+y^\ast \otimes_\mathsf B x^{\operatorname{op}}),\\
& s(x,y)=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{Lim}_n\left(\langle\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n),\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(x \xi_n y^\ast)\rangle+\langle\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n), \tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(y^\ast \xi_n x)\rangle\right)
\end{align*}
for $x,y\in \mathsf{M}$. For all $x\in \mathsf{M}$, note that $t(x,x),s(x,x)\in \mathbb R$; indeed  $t(x,x)\in\mathbb R$ follows because $\psi$ is a state, while $s(x,x)\in\mathbb R$ follows from observing that 
\begin{align*}
 \operatorname{Lim}_n\langle\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n),\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(x \xi_n x^\ast)\rangle&=\operatorname{Lim}_n\langle\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n),\zeta_{\alpha_n}(x)\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n)\zeta_{\alpha_n}(x^\ast)\rangle\\
 &=\operatorname{Lim}_n\langle \zeta_{\alpha_n}(x^\ast)\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n)\zeta_{\alpha_n}(x),\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n)\rangle\\
 &=\operatorname{Lim}_n\langle\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(x^\ast \xi_n x),\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n)\rangle
\end{align*}
that is $s(x,x)=g(x\otimes {x^\ast}^{\operatorname{op}})$.
Moreover,  
\begin{align*}
    t(x,x)=\operatorname{Re}\psi(x\otimes {x^\ast}^{\operatorname{op}})\geq g(x\otimes {x^{\ast}}^{\operatorname{op}})=s(x,x).
\end{align*}
Now let $y\in \mathsf{M}$ be a self-adjoint element and $\lambda\in\mathbb R$. Since $t(y,1)=t(1,y), s(y,1)=s(1,y)$ and since $ t(1,1)=1=s(1,1)$,
we obtain
 \begin{align*}
     1+2\lambda t( y,1)+\lambda^2t(y,y)&=t(1+\lambda y, 1+\lambda y)\\
     &\geq s(1+\lambda y,1+\lambda y)\\
     &= 1+2\lambda s( y,1)+\lambda^2s(y,y),
 \end{align*}
that is
 \[      2\lambda (t( y,1)-s(y,1))+\lambda^2(t(y,y)-s(y,y))\geq 0.\]
 Since $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ is arbitrary, and since $t(y,y)-s(y,y)\geq0$, it follows that 
 $t( y,1)= s(y,1)$; hence 
 $t(x,1)=s(x,1),\;\forall x\in \mathsf{M}$ 
and thus the state $\tilde\psi$ can be written as
  \begin{align*}
      \tilde\psi(x)=t(x,1)=s(x,1),\;\;x\in\mathsf{M}.
  \end{align*}
  {\em Proof of Claim 1.}
For all $a\in \mathsf{M}$, we have
  \begin{align*}
     \operatorname{Lim}_n\langle{\tilde\delta}^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n),{\tilde\delta}^\omega_{\alpha_n}(a^\ast a \xi_n)\rangle
                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                         
      &=\operatorname{Lim}_n\langle{\tilde\delta}^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n), \zeta_{\alpha_n}(a^\ast){\tilde\delta}^\omega_{\alpha_n}(a \xi_n)\rangle\\
      &=\operatorname{Lim}_n\langle\zeta_{\alpha_n}(a){\tilde\delta}^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n), {\tilde\delta}^\omega_{\alpha_n}(a \xi_n)\rangle\\
      &=\operatorname{Lim}_n\langle{\tilde\delta}^\omega_{\alpha_n}(a \xi_n), {\tilde\delta}^\omega_{\alpha_n}(a \xi_n)\rangle\\
    &\leq \operatorname{Lim}_n\|\tilde{\delta}^\omega_\alpha\|^2\|a \xi_n\|^2\\
    &\leq \|a(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}\sigma_{i/2}^{\varphi^\omega}(d_n)\|^2\\
    &\leq \|a(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}\|^2\|\sigma_{i/2}^{\varphi^\omega}(d_n)\|^2\\
    &\leq  C_1 \varphi(a^\ast a)
  \end{align*}
  where $C_1= \max \{\frac{1}{C^2}\|\sigma_{i/2}^{\varphi^\omega}(d)\|^2_\infty, \frac{1}{C^2}\|d\|^2_\infty\}$, so that  $C_1\geq  \sup_n\|\sigma_{i/2}^{\varphi^\omega}(d_n)\|_\infty^2$ as well as $C_1\geq \sup_n\|d_n\|^2_\infty$.
  Similarly, we have
  \begin{align*}
       \operatorname{Lim}_n\langle{\tilde\delta}^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n),{\tilde\delta}^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n a^\ast a)\rangle\leq\sup_n\|d_n\|^2 \|(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}a^\ast\|^2\leq C_1\varphi(a^\ast a)
  \end{align*}
yielding the following:
\begin{align*}
    \tilde\psi(a^\ast a)=s(a^\ast a,1)\leq   C_1\varphi(a^\ast a).
\end{align*}
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
 {\em Proof of Claim 2.}  To prove this claim,  we consider the restrictions of the forms $s,t$ to $\mathsf{Q}\times\mathsf{Q}$, and consider  the positive functional $\varphi_1$ on $\mathsf{Q}$ defined by 
\[\varphi_1(a)=\operatorname{Lim}_n\langle\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n), \tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(a \xi_n)\rangle=\operatorname{Lim}_n\langle\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n), \zeta_{\alpha_n}(a)\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n)\rangle,\;\;a\in \mathsf{Q}.\]
By a calculation similar to the
one above,  we have that $\varphi_1\leq   C_1\varphi_{|_\mathsf{Q}}$ so that $\varphi_1$ is a normal state on $\mathsf{Q}$.
By noting that $\sigma_t^{\varphi_{|_\mathsf{Q}}}={\sigma^\varphi_t}_{|_\mathsf{Q}}$, we get that $\mathsf{Q}\cap\mathsf{M}_{\infty,\sigma^\varphi}=\mathsf{Q}_{\infty,\sigma^{\varphi_{|_\mathsf{Q}}}}:=\mathsf{Q}_\infty$; so we identify $\sigma_\lambda^\varphi(a)$ and $\sigma_\lambda^{\varphi_{|_\mathsf{Q}}}(a)$, $a\in \mathsf{Q}_{\infty},\lambda\in\mathbb C$ and write them as $\sigma_\lambda(a)$. If $c\in \mathsf{Q}_{\infty,\sigma^\varphi}$, then $c$ is $\sigma^{\varphi^\omega}$-analytic as an element in $\mathsf{M}^\omega$ and $\sigma^{\varphi^\omega}_\lambda(c)=\sigma_\lambda^\varphi(c)$ for $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ \cite[Theorem 4.1]{AH14}, so that $c(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}=(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}\sigma_{i/2}^\varphi(c)$, and since $d_n\in \mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega$, we have $cd_n(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}=d_nc(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}=d_n(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}\sigma_{i/2}(c)$ which finally yields
\begin{align*}
    c\xi_n=\xi_n\sigma_{i/2}(c).
\end{align*}
Thus for all $a\in \mathsf{Q}$ we obtain
\begin{align*}
\varphi_1(ac)&=\operatorname{Lim}_n\langle\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n), \tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(ac \xi_n)\rangle\\
&=\operatorname{Lim}_n\langle\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n), \tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(a\xi_n\sigma_{i/2}(c))\rangle\\
&=\operatorname{Lim}_n\langle\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n), \tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(a \xi_n)\zeta_{\alpha_n}(\sigma_{i/2}(c))\rangle\\
&=\operatorname{Lim}_n\langle\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n)\zeta_{\alpha_n}(\sigma_{-i/2}(c^\ast)), \tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(a \xi_n)\rangle\\
&=\operatorname{Lim}_n\langle\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n \sigma_{-i/2}(c^\ast)), \tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(a \xi_n)\rangle\\
&=\operatorname{Lim}_n\langle\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(\sigma_{-i}(c^\ast) \xi_n ), \tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(a \xi_n)\rangle\\
&=\operatorname{Lim}_n\langle\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n ), \tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(\sigma_i(c)a \xi_n)\rangle\\
&=\varphi_1(\sigma_i(c)a).
\end{align*}
Arguing as in the proof of Proposition \ref{Prop:Equivalent conditions on relative amenability in terms of states with extra assumption on summand}, we get in particular $\varphi_1\circ\sigma_t=\varphi_1$ on $\mathsf{Q}$. Combining this with the fact that $\varphi_1\leq   C_1\varphi_{|_\mathsf{Q}}$ yields  a non-zero positive operator $z\in \mathsf{Q}^{\varphi_{|_\mathsf{Q}}}=\mathsf{M}^\varphi\cap\mathsf{Q}$, the centralizer, such that 
\[\varphi_1(a)=\varphi(za)=\varphi(z^{1/2}az^{1/2}),\] for $a\in \mathsf{Q}.$ Let $\xi_\varphi$ denote the cyclic and separating vector in $L^2(\mathsf{Q},\varphi_{|_\mathsf{Q}})$ such that $\varphi_{|_\mathsf{Q}}(a)=\langle\xi_\varphi,a\xi_\varphi\rangle,a\in\mathsf{Q}$. We identify $L^2(\mathsf{Q},\varphi_{|_\mathsf{Q}})$ as a subspace of $L^2(\mathsf{M},\varphi)$ via the map $a\xi_\varphi\mapsto a\varphi^{1/2}$ for $a\in\mathsf{Q}$.
Under this identification,   for all $a\in\mathsf{Q},c\in\mathsf{Q}_\infty$ we have
\begin{align*}
    \langle a^\ast\xi_\varphi,zc\xi_\varphi\rangle=\varphi(azc)=\varphi(\sigma_i(c)az)=\varphi_1(\sigma_i(c)a)=\varphi_1(ac)=\varphi(acz)=\langle a^\ast\xi_\varphi, cz\xi_\varphi\rangle
\end{align*}
implying that $zc=cz$; hence $z\in\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{Q})$. In particular, $z^{1/2}\xi_\varphi\in L^2(\mathsf{Q},\varphi_{|_\mathsf{Q}})_+,$ the positive cone of $L^2(\mathsf{Q})$.  Note also that if $p=s(z)$ is the support of $z$ in $\mathsf{Q}$, then $p$ is also the support of $\varphi_1$ (since $\varphi_1(a)=0$ if and only if $za=0$ for any $a\in \mathsf{Q}_+$); in particular $p\in \mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{Q})\subseteq\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M})$.
By working and proving the following results with $p\mathsf{Q}$, we may and we will as well assume that $p=1$, that is, $\varphi_1$ is faithful.
                                                                                                       

We now consider the self-polar form $r$ on $\mathsf{Q}\times\mathsf{Q}$ associated to the normal faithful  state $\varphi_1$, that is, $r(a,c)=\langle\varphi_1^{1/2}, a\varphi_1^{1/2}c^\ast\rangle$ for $a,c\in Q$, where $\varphi_1^{1/2}=z^{1/2}\xi_\varphi\in L^2(\mathsf{Q})$.   We have
 \begin{align*}r(a,c)=\langle z^{1/2}\xi_\varphi,az^{1/2} \xi_\varphi c^\ast\rangle=\langle \xi_\varphi,az \xi_\varphi c^\ast\rangle=\langle \varphi^{1/2},a z\varphi^{1/2}  c^\ast\rangle,
 \end{align*}
 for $a,c\in\mathsf{Q}$. Since $d_n\in\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega$, we next observe the following  for $a\in\mathsf{Q},c\in\mathsf{Q}_\infty$:   
 \begin{align*}
     2s(a,c)&=\operatorname{Lim}_n\left(\langle\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n), \tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(a \xi_n c^\ast)\rangle+\langle\tilde\delta_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n), \tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(c^\ast \xi_n a)\rangle\right)\\
     &=\operatorname{Lim}_n\left(\langle\tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n), \tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(a\sigma_{-i/2}(c^\ast) \xi_n)\rangle+\langle\tilde\delta_{\alpha_n}( \xi_n), \tilde\delta^\omega_{\alpha_n}(c^\ast\sigma_{-i/2}(a) \xi_n)\rangle\right)\\
     &=\varphi_1(a\sigma_{-i/2}(c^\ast)+c^\ast\sigma_{-i/2}(a))\\
     &=\langle \varphi^{1/2}, a\sigma_{-i/2}(c^\ast)z\varphi^{1/2}\rangle+\langle\varphi^{1/2}, c^\ast\sigma_{-i/2}(a) z\varphi^{1/2} \rangle\\
     &=\langle\varphi^{1/2}, az\varphi^{1/2} c^\ast\rangle+\langle\varphi^{1/2}, c^\ast z\varphi^{1/2} a\rangle\\
     &=r(a,c)+r(c^\ast,a^\ast),
 \end{align*}
 and since both $s,r$ are weak$^\ast$-continuous separately in each coordinate and since $\mathsf{Q}_\infty$ is weak$^\ast$-dense in $\mathsf{Q}$, it follows that $r(a,b)+r(b^\ast,a^\ast)=2s(a,b)$ for all $a,b\in\mathsf{Q}.$ Since  $r(a,a)\geq 0$, we have 
 \[r(a,a)=\overline{r(a,a)}={r(a^\ast,a^\ast)}\] which implies that
 \begin{align*}
     s(a,a)=r(a,a),\;\;a\in\mathsf{Q}.
 \end{align*}
Positive definiteness of $r$ also yields positive definiteness of $t_{|_{\mathsf{Q}\times\mathsf{Q}}}$, as
$t(a,a)\geq s(a,a)\geq 0$ for all $a\in\mathsf{Q}$. Since $\psi$ is a positive functional,
$t(a,b)=\frac{1}{2}\psi(a\otimes b^{\operatorname{op}}+b\otimes a^{\operatorname{op}})\geq 0$ for all $a,b\in\mathsf{Q}$ positive. Moreover,  we have \[t(a,1)=s(a,1)=\frac{1}{2}(r(a,1)+r(1,a^\ast))=\varphi_1(a),\;\; a\in\mathsf{Q}.\]
We can then invoke Theorem \ref{A result of Woronowicz on self-polar forms} to conclude that  $t(a,a)\leq r(a,a)$ for all $a\in\mathsf{Q}$, and the reverse inequality being also true from above yields
 $t(a,a)=r(a,a)$. By polarization, we arrive at the following:
\begin{align*}
    r(a,b)=t(a,b)=s(a,b),\;\;\forall a,b\in\mathsf{Q}.
\end{align*}
Thus for $a,b\in\mathsf{Q}_\infty$, we infer
\begin{align*}
    t(a,b^\ast)=\varphi_1(a\sigma_{-i/2}(b)).
\end{align*}
Returning to the state  $\psi$ on $\mathsf{M}\otimes_{\mathsf B,\min}\mathsf{M}^{\operatorname{op}}$, for $a\in\mathsf{Q}_\infty$, put 
\begin{align*}
&A=a\otimes_\mathsf B1-1\otimes_\mathsf B \sigma_{i/2}(a)^{\text{op}}\\
&B=\sigma_{i/2}(a)\otimes_\mathsf B1-1\otimes_\mathsf B a^{\text{op}}
\end{align*}
 and compute
\begin{align*}
  &\psi(A^\ast A)=  
                                                                                                                            
      \psi(a^\ast a\otimes_\mathsf B1)+\psi(1\otimes_\mathsf B (\sigma_{i/2}(a)\sigma_{-i/2}(a^\ast))^{\operatorname{op}})-2 \operatorname{Re}\psi(a^\ast\otimes_\mathsf B \sigma_{i/2}(a)^{\text{op}})\\
      &\psi(BB^\ast)=\psi(\sigma_{i/2}(a)\sigma_{-i/2}(a^\ast) \otimes_\mathsf B1)+\psi(1\otimes_\mathsf B (a^\ast a)^{\mathrm{op}})-2 \operatorname{Re}\psi(\sigma_{i/2}(a)\otimes_\mathsf B {a^\ast}^{\text{op}}).
\end{align*}
    
               
                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                  
             
Adding the  respective sides of the above equalities as well as using the fact that $s(a,b^\ast)=\varphi_1(a\sigma_{-i/2}(b)+b\sigma_{-i/2}(a))$ for all $a,b\in\mathsf{Q}_\infty$  conclude the following:
\begin{align*}
\psi(A^\ast A+BB^\ast)
  &=2t(a^\ast a,1)+2t(\sigma_{i/2}(a)\sigma_{-i/2}(a^\ast),1)-4\operatorname{Re} t(\sigma_{i/2}(a),a)\\
                                                                                          
  &=2\varphi_1(a^\ast a)+2\varphi_1(\sigma_{i/2}(a)\sigma_{-i/2}(a^\ast))-4\operatorname{Re}\varphi_1({\sigma_{i/2}(a)\sigma_{-i/2}(a^\ast)})\\
  &=0.
\end{align*}
This proves that
\begin{align*}
  \psi(A^\ast A)=0=\psi(BB^\ast)
\end{align*}
and hence for all $T\in \langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$, we have
  \begin{align*}
    &\psi(Ta\otimes _\mathsf B1)=\psi(T\otimes_\mathsf B \sigma_{i/2}(a)^{\mathrm{op}}),\\
   & \psi(a\otimes T^{\mathrm{op}})=\psi(1\otimes_\mathsf B T^{\mathrm{op}}\sigma_{i/2}(a)^{\mathrm{op}})=\psi(1\otimes_\mathsf B (\sigma_{i/2}(a)T)^{\mathrm{op}}),\\
   & \psi(\sigma_{i/2}(a)T\otimes_\mathsf B1)=\psi(T\otimes_\mathsf B a^{\mathrm{op}}),\\
    &\psi(\sigma_{i/2}(a)\otimes T^{\mathrm{op}})=\psi(1\otimes a^{\mathrm{op}}T^{\mathrm{op}})=\psi(1\otimes_\mathsf B(Ta)^{\mathrm{op}}),
    \end{align*}
   which finally yields the following:
   \begin{align*}
       \psi(Ta\otimes_\mathsf B1)=\psi(\sigma_i(a)T\otimes_\mathsf B1),\;\;\;\psi(1\otimes (Ta)^{\mathrm{op}})=\psi(1\otimes (\sigma_i(a)T)^{\mathrm{op}}).
   \end{align*}
   Thus we have shown that 
  \begin{align*}
     \tilde \psi(Ta)&=\frac{1}{2}\psi(Ta\otimes_\mathsf B1)+\frac{1}{2}\psi(1\otimes(Ta)^{\mathrm{op}})\\
     &=\frac{1}{2}\psi(\sigma_i(a)T\otimes_\mathsf B1)+\frac{1}{2}\psi(1\otimes(\sigma_i(a)T)^{\mathrm{op}})\\
     &=\tilde\psi(\sigma_i(a)T)
  \end{align*}
  for all $a\in \mathsf{Q}_\infty,$ $T\in \langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$, which concludes  the proof of Claim 2.
  
 To finish the proof, let
 $p\in \mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M})$ be the smallest non-zero projection such that $\tilde\psi(1-p)=0$, that is, $p$ is the support of $\tilde\psi_{|_{\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M})}}$. Clearly, $p\neq 0$.  By definition of $p$,  $\tilde\psi_{|_{p\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{Q}'\cap \mathsf{M})}}$ is faithful. Clearly, the condition $\tilde\psi_{|_{p\mathsf{M} p}}\leq C_1 \varphi(p\cdot p)$ remains valid. Moreover,  if $\varphi_p:=\varphi(p\cdot p)/\varphi(p)$ is the state on $p\mathsf{M} p$, then the condition $p\in \mathsf{M}^\varphi$ implies that
 \[\sigma_t^{\varphi_p}(x)=\sigma_t^\varphi(x)=p\sigma_t^\varphi(x)p,\;\;\forall t\in\mathbb R, x\in p\mathsf{M} p\] and that the $\sigma^{\varphi_p}$-analytic elements of $\mathsf{M}$ (resp. $p\mathsf{Q}$) are precisely $p\mathsf{M}_{\infty,\sigma^{\varphi}}p$ (resp. $p\mathsf{Q}_\infty$). Therefore the equality  \[\tilde\psi(Tx)=\tilde\psi(\sigma_i^{\varphi_p}(x)T),\;\; T\in p\langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle p, x\in p\mathsf{Q}\] remains valid as well. After normalizing the functional $\tilde\psi_{|_{p\langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle p}}$  by $\tilde\psi(p)$, we have thus shown that $p\mathsf{Q}$ is amenable relative to $\mathsf B$ inside $\mathsf{M}$ in view of Theorem~\ref{thm:conditions for relative amenability}.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
\label{rem:proof of the main theorem:general case}
 We assumed $1_\mathsf{Q}=1_\mathsf{M}$   in the proof of Theorem \ref{main_theorem}. The general case will follow from the same argument as follows: Choose a normal faithful state $\varphi$ on $\mathsf{M}$ such that $1_\mathsf{Q}$ lies in the centralizer $\mathsf{M}^\varphi$ and $\mathsf{Q}$ is globally invariant under $\sigma^\varphi$. Indeed, take any normal faithful state $\psi$ on $1_\mathsf{Q}\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf{Q}$ such that $\mathsf{Q}$ is globally invariant under $\sigma^\psi$, let $\nu$ be a normal faithful state on $(1_\mathsf{M}-1_\mathsf{Q})\mathsf{M}(1_\mathsf{M}-1_\mathsf{Q})$ and set
 \[\varphi(x)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\psi(1_\mathsf{Q} x1_\mathsf{Q})+\nu((1_\mathsf{M}-1_\mathsf{Q})x(1_\mathsf{M}-1_\mathsf{Q}))\right),\;\;\;x\in \mathsf{M}.\]
  Then if (2) in Theorem \ref{main_theorem} is not true, one will find $d\in \mathsf{Q}'\cap 1_\mathsf{Q}\mathsf{M}^\omega 1_\mathsf{Q}$ such that $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega(d(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2})$ does not converge to $d(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}$. Since $1_\mathsf{Q}\varphi^\omega=\varphi^\omega 1_\mathsf{Q}$, the  same argument will yield a state $\psi$ on $1_\mathsf{Q}\langle\mathsf{M},B\rangle1_\mathsf{Q}$ satisfying the KMS condition.
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
We say that an expected inclusion $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq1_\mathsf{Q}\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf{Q}$ is {\em completely nonamenable relative to $\mathsf B$} if $p\mathsf{Q}$ is not amenable relative to $\mathsf B$ for every non-zero projection $p\in\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{Q}'\cap1_\mathsf{Q}\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf{Q})$.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:dichotomy result in amenable case}
    Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebra and $\delta\colon \operatorname{dom}(\delta)\subset L^2(\mathsf{M})\to \mathsf{H}$ a densely defined closable modular derivation with $\mathsf{H}\prec L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2(\mathsf{M})$. If $\mathsf{Q}\subset 1_\mathsf{Q}\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf{Q} $ is a von Neumann subalgebra with expectation, at least one of the following is true:
    \begin{enumerate}[1.]
        \item  There is a non-zero projection $p\in {\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{Q}'\cap1_\mathsf{Q} \mathsf{M}1_\mathsf{Q})}$ such that $p\mathsf{Q}$ is amenable.
        \item $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ converges strongly to the identity on $L^2(\mathsf{Q}^\prime\cap \mathsf{M}^\omega)$ as $\alpha\to \infty$ for every cofinal ultrafilter $\omega$ on a directed set.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:dichotomy result, unform convergence at the centralizer level version}
Under the same hypotheses
as  in Theorem \ref{main_theorem},   at least one of the following is true:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item There is a non-zero projection $p\in {\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{Q}'\cap1_\mathsf{Q} \mathsf{M}1_\mathsf{Q})}$ such that $p\mathsf{Q}$ is amenable relative to $\mathsf B$.
        \item For every cofinal ultrafilter $\omega$ on a directed set and for every  state $\varphi$ on $\mathsf{M}$ with $\varphi=\varphi\circ E_\mathsf{Q}$, $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$   converges uniformly to the identity in $\|\cdot\|_{\varphi^\omega}$-norm on the unit ball of $\mathsf{Q}'\cap(\mathsf{M}^{\omega})^{\varphi^\omega}$. 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
If $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ does not converge uniformly on $\mathsf{Q}'\cap(\mathsf{M}^\omega)^{\varphi^\omega}$ for some cofinal ultrafilter $\omega$ and a state $\varphi$ with $\varphi\circ E_\mathsf{Q}=\varphi$, then by Lemma \ref{lem:pointwise convergece gives uniform convergence at the level of centralizer} below $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ does not converge strongly on $L^2(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^{\omega'})$ for some cofinal ultrafilter $\omega'$ on a directed set, and so we are in the situation of Theorem \ref{main_theorem} to  conclude the first statement.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{lem:pointwise convergece gives uniform convergence at the level of centralizer}
 Let $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ be an inclusion of $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebras,  and let $\varphi$ be a normal faithful state on $\mathsf{M}$ such
that $\mathsf{Q}$ is globally invariant under $\sigma^\varphi$.   Let $(\Psi_\alpha)_{\alpha\in \Lambda}$ be a net of GNS-symmetric ucp maps such that $\lVert\xi-\Psi_\alpha^{(2)}\xi\rVert\leq \lVert\xi-\Psi_\beta^{(2)}\rVert$ if $\alpha\geq \beta$ for all $\xi\in L^2(\mathsf{M})$. Suppose that $(\Psi_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ does not converge uniformly in $\|\cdot\|_{\varphi^\omega}$ norm on  $(\mathsf{Q}'\cap(\mathsf{M}^\omega)^{\varphi^{\omega}})_1$ for some cofinal ultrafilter $\omega$ on a directed set $J$. Then there exists a cofinal ultrafilter $\omega_1$ on a directed set such that $(\Psi_\alpha^{(2)})^{\omega_1}$ does not converge strongly  on $L^2(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^{\omega_1})$.
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
Put $T_\alpha=\Psi_\alpha^{(2)}$. Since   $T_\alpha^{\omega}$ does not converge uniformly in $\|\cdot\|_{\varphi^\omega}$ on the unit ball of $\mathsf{Q}'\cap(\mathsf{M}^\omega)^{\varphi^{\omega}}$, after passing to a subnet if necessary,  there is $C>0$ such that for all $\alpha\in \Lambda$, there is some $x_\alpha\in \mathsf{Q}'\cap(\mathsf{M}^{\omega})^{\varphi^{\omega}}$ satisfying $\|x_\alpha\|< 1$ and $\|T_\alpha^{\omega}(x_\alpha(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2})-x_\alpha(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2}\|\geq C$. For each $\alpha\in\Lambda$, let $(x_{\alpha,j})_{j\in J}\in \mathcal{M}^{\omega}(\mathsf{M})$ be such that $\sup_{j\in J}\|x_{\alpha,j}\|\leq 1$ and $x_\alpha=((x_{\alpha,j})_{j\in J})^{\omega}$. Consider the directed set
 \[I:=\{(\alpha, F, n); \alpha\in \Lambda, F\subseteq(\mathsf{Q})_1 \mbox{ finite},n\in\mathbb N\}\] 
 with the order $(\alpha, F,n)\leq (\alpha', F',n')$ if and only if $\alpha\leq\alpha', F\subseteq F'$ and $n\leq n'$. For each $i=(\alpha,F,n)\in I$, there is a $j_i\in J$ such that, putting $y_i=x_{\alpha,{j_i}}$, we have
  \begin{align*}
      &\|T_\alpha(y_i\varphi^{1/2})-y_i\varphi^{1/2}\|\geq C,\\
      &\|y_i\varphi^{1/2}-\varphi^{1/2}y_i\|\leq \frac{1}{n}\\
      &\|(y_i q-qy_i)\varphi^{1/2}\|\leq\frac{1}{n},\;\;\forall q\in F.
  \end{align*}
Let $\omega_1$ be a cofinal ultrafilter on the directed set $I$ and consider the element $(y_i)_{i\in I}\in \ell^\infty(I, \mathsf{M})$. Since $\lim_{i}\|y_i\varphi^{1/2}-\varphi^{1/2}y_i\|=0$, with a similar proof as in \cite[Proposition 2.2]{HR15}, it follows  that $(y_i)_{i\in I}\in \mathcal{M}^{\omega_1}(\mathsf{M})$. Set $x=(y_i)^{\omega_1}\in \mathsf{M}^{\omega_1}$. Thus we have
\begin{align*}
 \|T_\alpha^{\omega_1}(x(\varphi^{\omega_1})^{1/2})-x(\varphi^{\omega_1})^{1/2}\| \geq C\;\;\;\mbox{and }\;\;\;x\in \mathsf{Q}'\cap(\mathsf{M}^{\omega_1})^{\varphi^{\omega_1}}.  
\end{align*}
 So we have shown that $T_\alpha^{\omega_1}$ does not converge strongly along $\alpha$ to the identity  on $L^2(\mathsf{Q}'\cap(\mathsf{M}^{\omega_1})^{\varphi^{\omega_1}})$ and hence does not converge strongly on $L^2(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^{\omega_1})$.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ be an inclusion of $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebras with expectation such that $\mathsf{Q}_\ast$ is separable,  let $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$ and    let $(\Psi_n)_{n\geq1}$ be a sequence of GNS-symmetric ucp maps on $\mathsf{M}$ such that $\lVert\xi-\Psi_{n+1}^{(2)}\xi\rVert\leq\lVert\xi- \Psi_{n}^{(2)}\xi\rVert$ for all $\xi\in L^2(\mathsf{M}),n\in\mathbb N$. If $(\Psi_n^{(2)})^{\omega}$ converges strongly to the identity  on $L^2(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^{\omega})$, then $(\Psi_n^{(2)})^\omega$  converges uniformly in $\|\cdot\|_{\varphi^\omega}$-norm on  $(\mathsf{Q}'\cap(\mathsf{M}^\omega)^{\varphi^{\omega}})_1$ for every normal faithful state $\varphi$ on $\mathsf{M}$ such that $\mathsf{Q}$ is globally invariant under $\sigma^\varphi$.
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{thm:dichotomy result for subalgebras}
     Let $\mathsf{M}$ be diffuse a von Neumann algebras with  separable predual, and let $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$. Exactly one of the following holds true:
     \begin{enumerate}
         \item $\mathsf{M}$ has a non-zero amenable summand.
         \item For every modular derivation  $\delta:\operatorname{dom}(\delta)\subseteq L^2(\mathsf{M})\to \mathsf{H}$ with $\mathsf{H}\prec L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2(\mathsf{M})$, we have that $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ converges strongly to the identity on $L^2(\mathsf{M}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega)$, as $\alpha\to\infty$.
     \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{lem: a criteria for existence of certain derivation}
    Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebra, let $\varphi$ be a normal faithful state on $\mathsf{M}$, and let $\alpha:\mathbb R\curvearrowright \mathsf{M}$ be a $\varphi$-preserving action  such that $\alpha$ commutes with $\sigma^\varphi$. Write $\alpha^{(2)}_t=e^{itD}, t\in \mathbb R$ for a  self-adjoint operator $D$ on $L^2(\mathsf{M})$. Let $\omega$ be a cofinal ultrafilter on a directed set $I$. If there are a  uniformly bounded net  $\{x_n\}_{n\in I}\in \mathsf{M}$ and $\{\lambda_n\}_{n\in I}$ in $ (0,\infty)$ with $\lambda_n\to\infty$ such that   $D^2(x_n\varphi^{1/2})=\lambda_nx_n\varphi^{1/2}$ and $x:=(x_n)^\omega$ is a well-defined non-zero element in $\mathsf{M}^\omega$ then there is a $\varphi$-modular derivation $\delta:\operatorname{dom}\delta\subseteq L^2(\mathsf{M})\to L^2(\mathsf{M})$ such that $\theta_\alpha^\omega(x)$ does not converge strongly to $x$ as $\alpha\to\infty$.
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal{A}_\alpha$ and $\mathcal{A}_\varphi$ be the algebra of $\alpha$ and $\sigma^\varphi$-analytic vectors of $\mathsf{M}$, respectively, and set $\mathcal{A}=\mathcal{A}_\alpha\cap\mathcal{A}_\varphi$. Since $\alpha$ and $\sigma^\varphi$ commute, $\mathcal{A}$ is a strongly dense unital $\ast$-subalgebra of $\mathsf{M}$; indeed if $x\in \mathsf{M}$ then $x_n:=\frac{n}{\pi}\int_{\mathbb R\times\mathbb R}e^{-nt^2-ns^2}\alpha_t(\sigma_s^\varphi(x))dtds$ belongs to $\mathcal{A}$ such that $x_n\to x$ strongly as $n\to\infty$.
    
    Set $\operatorname{dom}(\delta)=\mathcal{A}\varphi^{1/2}\subseteq L^2(\mathsf{M},\varphi)$ and define $\delta:\operatorname{dom}(\delta)\to L^2(\mathsf{M})$ by $\delta=iD_{|_{\operatorname{dom}(\delta)}}$, that is,
\[ \delta(x\varphi^{1/2})=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0}
    \alpha_t(x)\varphi^{1/2} =iD(x\varphi^{1/2}),\quad x\in\mathcal A.\]
 The formula
 $ \alpha_t(xy)=\alpha_t(x)\alpha_t(y)$ for $ x, y\in \mathsf{M}$ implies the derivation rule for $\delta$.  Since $\alpha$ commutes with $\sigma^\varphi$, the operators $D$ and  $\Delta_\varphi^{it}$  strongly commute for all $t\in\mathbb R$. It is also easy to see that $J_\varphi D=-DJ_\varphi$. Hence $\delta$ has the required modular property. Since $D$ is a closed unbounded operator, $\delta$ is closable with the closure being $iD$. Moreover, we have $\mathcal{L}_2=\delta^\ast\bar\delta=D^2$.

 Next, we note that
 \[\theta_\alpha^{(2)}(x_n\varphi^{1/2})=\frac{\alpha}{\alpha+\lambda_n}x_n\varphi^{1/2},\;\;n\geq1, \alpha>0.\]
Since $\lambda_n\to\infty$ and $\{x_n\}_{n\in I}$ is uniformly bounded, it follows  for all $\alpha>0$ that  $\theta_\alpha^{(2)}(x_n\varphi^{1/2})\to 0$ along $n$. 
Thus $ (\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega(x(\varphi^\omega)^{1/2})=0$ for all $\alpha>0$, which proves that
$(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega(x)$ does not converge strongly to $x$, as $\alpha\to\infty$.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{lem: a derivation on the hyperfinite}
There exists a trace-symmetric derivation $\delta:\operatorname{dom}\delta\subseteq L^2(\mathcal{R})\to L^2(\mathcal{R})$ such that $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ does not converge strongly on $L^2(\mathcal{R}'\cap\mathcal{R}^\omega)$ as $\alpha\to\infty$ for any $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$.
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
Take the infinite tensor product decomposition 
\[\mathcal{R}
  =\overline{\bigotimes_{n=1}^\infty}
   (\mathbb M_2, {\operatorname{tr}}_2)\]
of the hyperfinite $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor, with its trace denoted by $\tau$. Here $\operatorname{tr}_2$ denotes the normalized trace on the complex matrix algebra $\mathbb M_2$.
Choose a sequence $\lambda_n\to\infty$, for example $\lambda_n=n$, and set
\[
  h_n
  =\frac{\lambda_n}{2}
   \begin{pmatrix}
     1&0\\
     0&-1
   \end{pmatrix}\in \mathbb M_2.
\]
There is a unique strongly continuous  action $\alpha$ of $\mathbb R$ on $\mathcal{R}$ such that 
\[
  \alpha_t
  =\bigotimes_{n=1}^\infty\mathrm{Ad}(e^{ith_n}),\;\;t\in\mathbb R.
\]
Clearly, $\alpha$ is $\tau$-preserving.  
For each $n\geq1$, let
\[
  u_n=1\otimes\cdots\otimes
   \begin{pmatrix}
     0&1\\
     1&0
   \end{pmatrix}
   \otimes\cdots,
\]
where the nontrivial matrix occurs in the $n$-th tensor factor.  Each $u_n$
is a self-adjoint unitary.  Moreover, $\|u_nx-xu_n\|_2\to0,$as $n\to\infty,$ for all $x\in\mathcal{R},$
because this is immediate for simple tensors and then follows for arbitrary
$x\in\mathcal{R}$ by approximation. 
Hence $u=(u_n)^\omega\in\mathcal{R}'\cap\mathcal{R}^\omega.$

Let $D$ be the self-adjoint operator on $L^2(\mathcal{R},\tau)$ such that $\alpha_t^{(2)}=e^{-itD}.$ For any $y\in \mathbb M_2$, if we set $x=1\otimes\cdots y\otimes\cdots$, where $y$ is in the $n$-th tensor factor, then one verifies
\begin{align*}
    D(x\tau^{1/2})=(yh_n-h_ny)\tau^{1/2}.
\end{align*}
In particular, if $e_{ij}^{(n)}$ for $1\leq i,j\leq 2$ denotes
matrix units in the $n$-th tensor factor, then 
\[
  D(e_{12}^{(n)}\tau^{1/2})=\lambda_ne_{12}^{(n)}\tau^{1/2},
  \qquad
  D(e_{21}^{(n)}\tau^{1/2})=-\lambda_ne_{21}^{(n)}\tau^{1/2}.
\]
Since $u_n=e_{12}^{(n)}+e_{21}^{(n)},$ we obtain
 $ D^2(u_n\tau^{1/2})=\lambda_n^2u_n\tau^{1/2}.$ 
Thus $(u_n)_{n\geq1}$ satisfies the hypothesis of Lemma \ref{lem: a criteria for existence of certain derivation}; hence $\theta_\alpha^\omega(u)$ does not converge strongly to $u$ as $\alpha\to\infty$.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{lem: a derivation on diffuse abelian}
If $\mathsf A$ is the unique separable diffuse abelian von Neumann algebra $\mathsf A$, then there exists a trace-symmetric derivation $\delta:\operatorname{dom}(\delta)\subseteq L^2(\mathsf A)\to L^2(\mathsf A)$  such that $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ does not converge strongly on $L^2(\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf A^\omega)$ for any $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$.
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Let $(X,\mu)$ be a non-atomic probability measure space such that $\mathsf A=L^\infty(X,\mu)$.    By uniqueness,   we may identify $  (X,\mu)\cong(\mathbb T^{\mathbb N},m^{\mathbb N})$, where $m$ is the one-dimensional Lebesgue measure on the unit circle $\mathbb T$.
Choose $\lambda_n\to\infty$, and define a measure-preserving flow on $\mathbb T^{\mathbb N}$ by
\[
  T_t((z_n)_n)
  =(e^{i\lambda_n t}z_n)_n,\;\;\;\;(z_n)_n\in\mathbb T^{\mathbb N},\;\;t\in\mathbb R.
\]
Set $\alpha_t(f)=f\circ T_t $ for $f\in L^\infty(\mathbb T^{\mathbb N}, m^{\mathbb N})$, which induces a $\tau$-preserving action of $\mathbb R$ on $L^\infty(\mathbb T^{\mathbb N}, m^{\mathbb N})$, where $\tau$ is the integration with respect to $m^{\mathbb N}$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
For $n\geq1$, consider the unitaries $v_n\in L^\infty(\mathbb T^{\mathbb N}, m^{\mathbb N})$ defined by 
\[
  v_n(z_1,z_2,\ldots)=z_n.
\]
Then $ \alpha_t(v_n)=e^{i\lambda_nt}v_n,\;t\in\mathbb R $
and hence $D^2(v_n\tau^{1/2})
  =\lambda_n^2v_n\tau^{1/2}.$
Clearly  $(v_n)^\omega\in \mathcal{Z}(\mathsf A^\omega)\subseteq\mathsf A'\cap\mathsf A^\omega$ and $v_n$ satisfies the hypothesis of Lemma \ref{lem: a criteria for existence of certain derivation}.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{thm:existence of derivation for McDuff type algebras}
    Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebra either of the form $\mathsf{M}_1\oplus(\mathsf{M}_2\otimes\mathcal{R})$ or of the form $\mathsf{M}_1\oplus(\mathsf{M}_2\otimes\mathsf A)$ for some von Neumann algebras $\mathsf{M}_1,\mathsf{M}_2$ such that $\mathsf{M}_2\neq0$,
                                                                               
    where $\mathsf A$ is the unique separable diffuse abelian von Neumann algebra. There exists a densely defined closable modular derivation $\delta:\operatorname{dom}\delta\subseteq L^2(\mathsf{M})\to L^2(\mathsf{M})$ such that $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ does not converge strongly on $L^2(\mathsf{M}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega)$ for any $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$.
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Assume that $\mathsf{M}=\mathsf{M}_1\oplus(\mathsf{M}_2\otimes\mathcal{R}))$ for $\mathsf{M}_2\neq0$.     Let $\delta$  be the closable densely defined modular derivations on $L^2(\mathcal{R})$
     as constructed in Lemma \ref{lem: a derivation on the hyperfinite} and denote by  $(\theta_{\alpha})_{\alpha>0}$ the associated deformation. Define the unique modular derivation $\partial$ on $L^2(M)\cong L^2(\mathsf{M}_1)\oplus \left.(L^2(\mathsf{M}_2)\otimes L^2(\mathcal{R})\right)$
     such that the associated deformation of $\partial$ is
\[\eta_\alpha:=\operatorname{id}_{\mathsf{M}_1}\oplus(\operatorname{id}_{\mathsf{M}_2}\otimes\theta_{\alpha}),\quad \alpha>0.\] 
Clearly, then $(\eta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ does not converge strongly on $L^2(\mathsf{M}'\cap \mathsf{M}^\omega)$ for any $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$,  because $(1_{\mathsf{M}_2}\otimes\mathcal{R})'\cap (1_{\mathsf{M}_2}\otimes\mathcal{R})^\omega\subseteq\mathsf{M}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega$ and $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ does not converge strongly on $\mathcal{R}'\cap\mathcal{R}^\omega$. A similar argument yields the assertion if $\mathsf{M}$ is of the form $\mathsf{M}_1\oplus(\mathsf{M}_2\otimes\mathsf A)$ for $\mathsf{M}_2\neq0$ in view of Lemma \ref{lem: a derivation on diffuse abelian}.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{lem:hyperfinite factor absorption}
    If $\mathsf{N}$ is a diffuse amenable von Neumann algebra with separable predual of either type II or type III, then $\mathsf{N}\cong\mathsf{N}\overline{\otimes}\mathcal{R}$.
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
By disintegration theory of  separable von Neumann algebras, it suffices to prove the result when  $\mathsf{N}$ is a factor. If $\mathsf{N}$ is an amenable factor of type II or type III$_{\lambda}$, $0<\lambda\leq 1$, then $\mathsf{N}\overline{\otimes}\mathcal{R}$ is also an amenable factor of the same type (see \cite[Proposition 28.4]{Str20}), so   by the uniqueness of separable amenable factors of these types (\cite{Con76, Haa87}), we have $\mathsf{N}\cong\mathsf{N}\overline{\otimes}\mathcal{R}$.
    Finally type III$_0$ amenable factors are classified by their flow of weight (\cite[Corollary 7.6]{Con76}). If $\mathsf{N}$ is a type III$_0$ factor, then  Flow$(\mathsf{N}\overline{\otimes}\mathcal{R})$=Flow$(\mathcal{R})$. 
    Indeed, let $\varphi$ be a faithful normal state on $\mathsf{N}$, and let $\tau$ be the normalized trace on $\mathcal{R}$. Since
$\sigma_t^{\varphi\otimes\tau}
=\sigma_t^\varphi\otimes\mathrm{id}_\mathcal{R},$ there is a canonical identification
\[(\mathsf{N}\bar\otimes \mathcal{R})\rtimes_{\sigma^{\varphi\otimes\tau}}\mathbb R
\cong (\mathsf{N}\rtimes_{\sigma^\varphi}\mathbb R)\bar\otimes \mathcal{R}
\]under which the dual action becomes $\theta^{\mathsf{N}}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{R}}$. Thus $z\mapsto z\otimes1$ intertwines the actions on the centers, proving that the flows of weights are conjugate. Hence we have  $\mathsf{N}\cong \mathsf{N}\overline{\otimes}\mathcal{R}$.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{cor:a derivation on diffuse amenable von Neumann algebras}
If $\mathsf{M}$ is a diffuse amenable von Neumann algebra with separable predual, then
there is a densely defined closable modular derivation $ \delta:\operatorname{dom}(\delta)\subseteq L^2(\mathsf{M})\to L^2(\mathsf{M})$ such that  $ (\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$
does not converge strongly to the identity on $L^2(\mathsf{M}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega)$ as $\alpha\to\infty$,  for every free ultrafilter $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$.
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
If $\mathsf{M}$ has no amenable summand,   the statement $(2)$ follows from Corollary \ref{cor:dichotomy result in amenable case}.

Otherwise, assume that there is a non-zero central  projection $z\in\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{M})$ such that $z\mathsf{M}$ is amenable. By Corollary  \ref{cor:a derivation on diffuse amenable von Neumann algebras},  choose $\delta:\operatorname{dom}(\delta)\subseteq L^2(z\mathsf{M})\to L^2(z\mathsf{M})$ to be a modular derivation such that the associated deformation $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ does not converge strongly on $L^2((z\mathsf{M})'\cap(z\mathsf{M})^\omega)$.  Consider the zero derivation from $L^2((1-z)\mathsf{M})$ to $ L^2((1-z)\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2((1-z)\mathsf{M})$, and let $\partial=\delta\oplus 0$ be the derivation from $L^2(\mathsf{M})\cong L^2(z\mathsf{M})\oplus L^2((1-z)\mathsf{M})$ to $L^2(z\mathsf{M})\oplus \left(L^2((1-z)\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2((1-z)\mathsf{M})\right)$.  Clearly $(z\mathsf{M})'\cap(z\mathsf{M})^\omega\subseteq\mathsf{M}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega$, so the associated deformation of $\partial$, which is $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)}\oplus \operatorname{id}_{L^2((1-z)\mathsf{M})})^\omega$, does not converge strongly to the identity on $L^2(\mathsf{M}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega)$ as $\alpha\to\infty$, for any $\omega\in \beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$.

Since $z\mathsf{M}$ is amenable, we have $L^2(z\mathsf{M})\prec L^2(z\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2(z\mathsf{M})$ as $z\mathsf{M}$-correspondence. It follows from Lemma \ref{lem:direct sum of bimodule and their weak containment} below that as $\mathsf{M}\cong z\mathsf{M}\oplus(1-z)\mathsf{M}$-correspondence, we have
\begin{align*}
    L^2(z\mathsf{M})\oplus&  \left(L^2((1-z)\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2((1-z)\mathsf{M})\right)\\
    &\prec  \left(L^2(z\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2(z\mathsf{M})\right)\oplus\left(L^2((1-z)\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2(1-z)\mathsf{M})\right).
\end{align*}
However, the correspondence on the right hand side is an $\mathsf{M}$-sub-correspondence of $L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2(\mathsf{M})$, which means that as $\mathsf{M}$-correspondence we have
\begin{align*}
     L^2(z\mathsf{M})\oplus  \left(L^2((1-z)\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2((1-z)\mathsf{M})\right)\prec L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2(\mathsf{M}).
\end{align*}
Thus we have produced  a derivation $\partial$ which satisfies the required conditions.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{lem:direct sum of bimodule and their weak containment}
    Let $\mathsf{H}_i,\mathsf{K}_i$ be Hilbert correspondences over a von Neumann algebra $\mathsf{M}_i$ for $i=1,2$. If $\mathsf{H}_i\prec\mathsf{K}_i$ as $\mathsf{M}_i$-correspondence, we have $\mathsf{H}_1\oplus\mathsf{H}_2\prec \mathsf{K}_1\oplus\mathsf{K}_2$ as $\mathsf{M}_1\oplus\mathsf{M}_2$-correspondence.
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
Put $\mathsf{M}=\mathsf{M}_1\oplus\mathsf{M}_2$, $\mathsf{H}=\mathsf{H}_1\oplus\mathsf{H}_2$ and $\mathsf{K}=\mathsf{K}_1\oplus\mathsf{K}_2$, and denote by $\pi_\mathsf{H},\pi_\mathsf{K}$ the bimodule action of $\mathsf{M}$ on $\mathsf{H},\mathsf{K}$ respectively. If $T\in \mathsf{M}\otimes_{\operatorname{alg}}\mathsf{M}^{\mathrm{op}}$, then $T=\sum_{i,j=1}^2T_{ij}$ for some $T_{ij}\in \mathsf{M}_i\otimes_{\operatorname{alg}}\mathsf{M}_j^{\mathrm{op}},$ $1\leq i,j\leq 2$. Note that $T_{12}$ and $T_{21}$ act as $0$ on $\mathsf{H}$ and $\mathsf{K}$, that is, $\pi_\mathsf{H}(T_{12})=0=\pi_\mathsf{H}(T_{21})$ and same for $\pi_\mathsf{K}$. Therefore, we have
 \begin{align*}
   \|\pi_\mathsf{H}(T)\|=\lVert\pi_{\mathsf{H}_1}(T_{11})\oplus\pi_{\mathsf{H}_2}(T_{22})\rVert=\max_{i=1,2}\lVert\pi_{\mathsf{H}_i}(T_{ii})\rVert\leq \max_{i=1,2}\lVert\pi_{\mathsf{K}_i}(T_{ii})\rVert=\lVert\pi_\mathsf{K}(T)\rVert
 \end{align*}
which proves that $\mathsf{H}\prec\mathsf{K}$ as $\mathsf{M}$-correspondence.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
An inclusion $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ of von Neumann algebras with expectation is said to have {\em $w$-spectral gap} if $\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega=\mathbb (\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M})^\omega$ for some free ultrafilter $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$.
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ be an  inclusion of irreducible factors  such that $\mathsf{Q}$ has separable predual and $\mathsf{Q}$ is nonamenable. Let $\varphi$ be a normal faithful state on $\mathsf{M}$ such that $\mathsf{Q}$ is globally invariant under $\sigma^\varphi$. Fix $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$. If the inclusion $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ does not have $w$-spectral gap, then for every $\varphi$-modular derivation $\delta:\operatorname{dom}\delta\subseteq L^2(\mathsf{M})\to\mathsf{H}$ with $\mathsf{H}\prec L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2(\mathsf{M})$ and $\mathsf{H}$ mixing,
  $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ converges uniformly to the identity on $(\mathsf{Q}^\omega)_1$  as $\alpha\to\infty$.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
Let $\delta:\operatorname{dom}(\delta)\subseteq L^2(\mathsf{M})\to\mathsf{H}$ be a $\varphi$-modular derivation with  $\mathsf{H}\prec L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2(\mathsf{M})$. In view of Proposition \ref{prop: uniform convergence of GNS-symmetric maps}, the result follows once we show
\[\lim_{\alpha\to\infty}\sup_{x\in \mathsf{Q}, \|x\|\leq 1}\|\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\|=0.\]
 For simplicity, write $\psi$ for the state $\varphi^\omega$ on $\mathsf{M}^\omega$.  
   It follows from  Theorem \ref{main_theorem}  that $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ converges strongly  to the identity on $L^2(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega)$ as $\alpha\to\infty$. In other words, 
   \[\tilde\delta_\alpha^\omega(z\psi^{1/2})\to 0 \;\;\mbox{ for all }\;z\in \mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega.\] 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
   Since $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ does not have $w$-spectral gap, we  have $\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega\neq\mathbb C$; hence by \cite[Lemma 2.5]{HR15}, $\mathsf{Q}'\cap(\mathsf{M}^\omega)^\psi$ is diffuse and there is a unitary $u\in \mathsf{Q}'\cap(\mathsf{M}^\omega)^\psi$ such that $E_\mathsf{M}(u)=0$.
                                                                                                                                 
 In particular, for all $\alpha>0$, we have $\zeta_\alpha(u_n)\to 0$ weakly as $n\to\omega$.
Fix $x\in \mathsf{Q}$ with $\|x\|_\infty\leq 1$. Since $\mathsf{H}$ is mixing, 
we have for all $\alpha>0$
\begin{align*}
    \lim_{n\to\omega}\langle\zeta_\alpha(u_n)\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\zeta_\alpha(u_n^\ast),\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\rangle=0
\end{align*}
which further yields
\begin{align*}
     \lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert&\leq \lim_{n\to\omega}\lVert\zeta_\alpha(u_n^\ast )\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\zeta_\alpha(u_n)-\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert
        
                                                                                                                                             
\end{align*}
By the technical  Lemma \ref{lem: the main technical lemma}, it follows for all $\alpha>0$ that
 \begin{align*}
        \lVert\zeta_\alpha(u_n^\ast )\tilde\delta_\alpha&(x\varphi^{1/2})\zeta_\alpha(u_n)-\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert\\
     &\leq \lVert\zeta_\alpha(u_n^\ast )\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\zeta_\alpha(u_n)-\zeta_\alpha(u_n^\ast )\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2}u_n)\rVert\\
     &\quad+\lVert\zeta_\alpha(u_n^\ast )\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2}u_n)-\tilde\delta_\alpha(u_n^*x\varphi^{1/2}u_n)\rVert+\lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(u_n^*x\varphi^{1/2}u_n)-\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert\\
     &\leq 10\|\tilde\delta_\alpha(\varphi^{1/2}u_n)\|^{1/2}+10\|\tilde\delta_\alpha(u_n^\ast\varphi^{1/2})\|^{1/2}+\lVert\tilde\delta_\alpha(u_n^*x\varphi^{1/2}u_n)-\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert
    \end{align*}
 Thus using $xu^\ast=u^\ast x$ and  $u\psi^{1/2}=\psi^{1/2}u$, we obtain
 \begin{align*}
  \|\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\|&=  \lim_{n\to\omega}\lVert\zeta_\alpha(u_n^\ast )\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\zeta_\alpha(u_n)-\tilde\delta_\alpha(x\varphi^{1/2})\rVert\\
  &\leq 20\|\tilde\delta_\alpha^\omega(u\psi^{1/2})\|^{1/2}.
 \end{align*}
 Since the right hand side is independent of $x$ and converges to $0$ as $\alpha\to\infty$, we obtain the required result.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- corollary-7: body_md -->
\label{cor:fullness and rigidity}
   If $\mathsf{M}$ is  a nonamenable  factor with separable predual which is not full, in particular when $\mathsf{M}$ is of type III$_0$,  then $\mathsf{M}$ is rigid with respect to modular derivations taking values in mixing weakly coarse correspondences, that is, for every modular derivation $\delta:\operatorname{dom}\delta\subseteq L^2(\mathsf{M})\to\mathsf{H}$ with $\mathsf{H}\prec L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2(\mathsf{M})$ and $\mathsf{H}$ mixing,
  $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ converges uniformly to the identity on $(\mathsf{M}^\omega)_1$  as $\alpha\to\infty$.
<!-- end corollary-7 -->
<!-- corollary-8: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a tracial von Neumann algebra, and let $\mathsf{Q}$ be a nonamenable irreducible subalgebra of $\mathsf{M}$ with separable predual. If $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ does not have $w$-spectral gap, then $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ is  rigid with respect to modular derivation taking values in weakly coarse mixing correspondences.
<!-- end corollary-8 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
\label{cor: tensor product of nonamenable factors are coarse rigid}
    Let $\mathsf{M}_1$ and $\mathsf{M}_2$ be two nonamenable II$_1$ factors. Then $\mathsf{M}_1\bar\otimes\mathsf{M}_2$ is coarsely rigid.
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
Write $\mathsf{M}=\mathsf{M}_1\bar\otimes\mathsf{M}_2$, and   let $\delta:\operatorname{dom}\delta\subseteq L^2(\mathsf{M})\to \mathsf{H}$ be a modular derivation in a weakly coarse $\mathsf{M}$-$\mathsf{M}$ correspondence $\mathsf{H}$ with the associated deformation $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})_{\alpha>0}$. Let $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$. By Theorem \ref{main_theorem}, $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ converges strongly to the identity on $L^2(\mathsf{M}_1^\omega\bar\otimes1)$ and on $L^2(1\otimes\mathsf{M}_2^\omega)$ as $\alpha\to\infty$. By Lemma \ref{lem:rigidity on commuting subalgebras} below and Proposition \ref{prop:equivalent conditions for L2-rigidity}, it follows that $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ converges strongly to the identity on $L^2(\mathsf{M}^\omega)$ as $\alpha\to\infty$.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{lem:rigidity on commuting subalgebras}
 Let $(\mathsf{M},\tau)$ be a finite von Neumann algebra, and   let $\mathsf A_1,\mathsf A_2\subseteq M$ be inclusion of commuting subalgebras generating $\mathsf{M}$. If $T_i$ is a net of $\tau$-preserving completely positive maps such that $T_i$ converges uniformly to the identity on the unit ball of both $\mathsf A_i$ in the $L^2$-norm, then $T_i$ converges uniformly on the unit ball of $\mathsf{M}$ in the $L^2$-norm.
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
Because we are in the tracial setting, by usual convexity argument (see \cite{Pop86}, \cite[Theorem 4.5]{Pet09}),    it suffices to prove that $\sup_{u\in \mathcal{U}(\mathsf{M})}\|T_i(u)-u\|_{2,\tau}\to 0$ along $i$. Let $(\mathsf{H}_i, \xi_i)$ be the minimal Stinespring dilation for $T_i$, that is, $\mathsf{H}_i$ is an $\mathsf{M}$-$\mathsf{M}$ correspondence and $\xi_i\in \mathsf{H}_i$ is left bounded such that $T_i(x)=L_\tau(\xi)^\ast xL_\tau(\xi)$. For all $x\in \mathsf{M}$, we have
\begin{align*}
\|T(x)-x\|_{2,\tau}\leq     \|x\xi_i-\xi_ix\|\leq \|x\|_{2,\tau}\|T_i(x)-x\|_{2,\tau}
\end{align*}
In particular, the pointwise convergence of $T_i$ implies that 
   $ \|x\xi_i-\xi_ix\|\to 0,\;\forall x\in \mathsf{M}.$
Consider the $\mathsf A_1$ and $\mathsf A_2$ central vectors of $\mathsf{H}_i$ given  by 
\[\mathsf{K}_{i,1}:=\{\xi\in \mathsf{H}_i; a_1\xi=\xi a_1\;\forall a_1\in \mathsf A_1\},\;\;\;\;\mathsf \mathsf{K}_{i,2}:=\{\xi\in \mathsf{H}_i; a_2\xi=\xi a_2\;\forall a_2\in \mathsf A_2\}\]
and denote by $P_{i,1}, P_{i,2}$ the respective projections. Then $P_{i,1}$ and $P_{i,2}$ commute because $\mathsf A_1$ and $\mathsf A_2$ commute. Indeed,  for any $v\in \mathcal{U}(\mathsf{M})$, if we define the unitaries $U_v$ on $\mathsf{H}$ by $\eta\mapsto v\eta v^\ast$, then $\mathsf{K}_{i,1}$ (resp. $\mathsf K_{i,2}$) is precisely the subspace fixed by the unitaries $U_u$ for $u\in \mathcal{\mathsf A_1}$ (resp. $u\in \mathcal{U}(\mathsf A_2)$). However $U_u$ and $U_v$ commute whenever $u\in \mathcal{U}(\mathsf A_1)$ and $\mathcal{U}(\mathsf A_2)$ and hence so does the projection onto their respective fixed point space. Set
\[\eta_i=P_{i,1}P_{i,2}\xi\in \mathsf{K}_{i,1}\cap\mathsf K_{i,2}.\]
Then $a\eta_i=\eta_i a$ for all $a\in \mathsf A_1$ or $a\in\mathsf A_2$, and since $\mathsf{M}=\mathsf A_1\vee\mathsf A_2$, it follows that $x\eta_i=\eta_ix$ for all $x\in \mathsf{M}$. Moreover, we have
\begin{align*}
    \|\xi_i-\eta_i\|&\leq \|(1-P_{i,1})\xi_i\|+\|(1-P_{i,2})\xi_i\|\\
    &=\sup_{u\in \mathcal{U}(\mathsf A_1)}\|T_i(u)-u\|_{2,\tau}+\sup_{u\in \mathcal{U}(\mathsf A_2)}\|T_i(u)-u\|_{2,\tau}
\end{align*}
which converges to $0$ by assumption.  Thus we arrive at the following:
\begin{align*}
    \sup_{u\in \mathcal{U}(\mathsf{M})}\|T_i(u)-u\|_{2,\tau}&\leq \sup_{u\in \mathcal{U}(\mathsf{M})}\|u\xi_i-\xi_i u\|\\
    &\leq \sup_{u\in \mathcal{U}(\mathsf{M})}\|u(\xi_i-\eta_i)+(\eta_i-\xi_i)u\|\\
    &\leq 2\|\xi_i-\eta_i\|
\end{align*}
and the right hand goes to $0$ along i.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
Contrary to what is claimed in \cite{CKSVW23}, the space $\mathbb K(\mathsf B\subset\mathsf{M},\varphi)$ is not necessarily an ideal in the basic construction $\langle \mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$ (regardless of whether $\mathsf B$ is finite or not).

    For example, let $\mathsf{M}=\ell^\infty(\mathbb N)\oplus \ell^\infty(\mathbb N)$, $\mathsf B=\{(x_n,x_n)\mid x_n\in \ell^\infty(\mathbb N)\}$, $\varphi((x_n,y_n))=\sum_{n\geq 1}2^{-n}((1-2^{-n})x_n+2^{-n}y_n)$. We have a natural identification $L^2(\mathsf{M})\cong \ell^2(\mathbb N)\oplus \ell^2(\mathbb N)$ and $\langle \mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle=M_2(\ell^\infty(\mathbb N))$, $\mathbb K(\mathsf B\subset \mathsf{M},\varphi)=\begin{pmatrix}\ell^\infty(\mathbb N)&c_0(\mathbb N)\\c_0(\mathbb N)&c_0(\mathbb N)\end{pmatrix}$ under this identification. Clearly, $\mathbb K(\mathsf B\subset \mathsf{M},\varphi)$ is not an ideal in $\langle \mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- lemma-26: body_md -->
There exists a unique $\ast$-isomorphism from $\mathbb K(\mathcal X_\mathsf B)$ onto $\mathbb K(\mathsf B\subset \mathsf{M},\varphi)$ that maps $\theta_{x,y}$ to $xe_\mathsf B y^\ast $ for $x,y\in \mathsf{M}$.
<!-- end lemma-26 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
We have a unitary $U\colon\mathcal X\mathbin{\overline\odot_\mathsf B} L^2(\mathsf B)\to L^2(\mathsf{M})$ that sends $x\otimes_\mathsf B b\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}$ to $xb\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}$ for $x\in \mathsf{M}$ and $b\in \mathsf B$. Indeed,
    \begin{align*}
        \langle x_1\otimes_\mathsf B b_1\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2},x_2\otimes_\mathsf B b_2\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}\rangle
        &=\langle b_1\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2},E_\mathsf B(x_1^\ast x_2)b_2\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}\rangle\\
        &=\varphi_\mathsf B(b_1^\ast E_\mathsf B(x_1^\ast x_2)b_2)\\
        &=\varphi(b_1^\ast x_1^\ast x_2 b_2)\\
        &=\langle x_1 b_1\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2},x_2 b_2\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}\rangle
    \end{align*}
    for $x_1,x_2\in \mathsf{M}$ and $b_1,b_2\in \mathsf B$.

    Since $\mathbb K(\mathcal X_\mathsf B)$ consists of adjointable operators, we get a $\ast$-homomorphism
    \begin{equation*}
        \sigma\colon \mathbb K(\mathcal X_\mathsf B)\to \mathbb B(L^2(\mathsf{M})),\,S\mapsto U(S\otimes_\mathsf B 1)U^\ast.
    \end{equation*}
    The map $\sigma$ is injective: If $\sigma(S)=0$, then
    \begin{equation*}
        0=\lVert\sigma(S)x\varphi^{1/2}\rVert^2=\lVertSx\otimes_\mathsf B \varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}\rVert^2=\varphi_\mathsf B(\langle Sx\vert Sx\rangle_\mathsf B),
    \end{equation*}
    hence $Sx=0$ for all $x\in \mathsf{M}$ since $\varphi_\mathsf B$ is faithful. Thus $S=0$.

    Moreover, if $x,y,z\in \mathsf{M}$, then
    \begin{align*}
        \sigma(\theta_{x,y})z\varphi^{1/2}=U(\theta_{x,y}(z)\otimes_\mathsf B \varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2})=xE_\mathsf B(y^\ast z)\varphi^{1/2}=xe_B y^\ast z\varphi^{1/2}.
    \end{align*}
    Therefore, $\sigma(\theta_{x,y})=x e_\mathsf B y^\ast $.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
Let $A$, $B$ be $C^\ast$-algebras, let $\mathcal X$ be a Hilbert $C^\ast$-module over $A$, $\mathcal Y$ a Hilbert $C^\ast$-module over $B$ and $\pi\colon A\to \mathcal L(\mathcal Y_B)$ a non-degenerate representation by adjointable operators. If $S\in \mathbb K(\mathcal X_A)$, $T\in \mathbb K(\mathcal Y_B)\cap \pi(A)^\prime$, then $S\otimes_A T\in \mathbb K(\mathcal X\overline\odot_A \mathcal Y_B)$.
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
For $\xi\in\mathcal X$ we define
    \begin{equation*}
        a^\ast(\xi)\colon \mathcal Y\to \mathcal X\overline\odot_A \mathcal Y,\,\eta\mapsto \xi\otimes_A \eta.
    \end{equation*}
    A direct computation shows that $a^\ast(\xi)$ is adjointable with adjoint
    \begin{equation*}
        a(\xi)\colon \mathcal X\overline\odot_A \mathcal Y\to \mathcal Y,\,\zeta\otimes_A\eta \mapsto \pi(\langle \xi\vert \zeta\rangle_A)\eta.
    \end{equation*}
    If $(S_n)$ is a sequence in $\mathbb F(\mathcal X_A)$ such that $S_n\to S$ in norm, then
    \begin{equation*}
        \lVertS\otimes_A T-S_n \otimes_A T\rVert\leq \lVertS-S_n\rVert\lVertT\rVert\to 0,
    \end{equation*}
    hence we may assume that $S=\theta_{\xi,\eta}$ for some $\xi,\eta\in \mathcal X$. We claim that $S\otimes_A T=a^\ast(\xi)T a(\eta)$. Indeed, if $\zeta_1\in \mathcal X$ and $\zeta_2\in \mathcal Y$, then
    \begin{equation*}
        (S\otimes_A T)(\zeta_1\otimes_ A \zeta_2)=\xi\langle \eta,\zeta_1\rangle_A\otimes_A T\zeta_2=\xi\otimes_A T\pi(\langle \eta\vert\zeta_1\rangle_A)\zeta_2=a^\ast(\xi)Ta(\eta)(\zeta_1\otimes_A \zeta_2).
    \end{equation*}
    It remains to show that if $\xi^\prime\in \mathcal X$ and $\eta^\prime\in \mathcal Y$, then $a^\ast(\xi)\theta_{\xi^\prime,\eta^\prime}a(\eta)\in \mathbb F(\mathcal X\overline\odot_A \mathcal Y_B)$. Indeed, if $\xi\in \mathcal X$ and $\xi^\prime\in \mathcal Y$, then
    \begin{align*}
        a^\ast(\xi)\theta_{\xi^\prime,\eta^\prime}a(\eta)(\zeta\otimes_A \zeta^\prime)&=a^\ast(\xi)(\xi^\prime\langle \eta^\prime\vert \pi(\langle \eta\vert \zeta\rangle_A)\zeta^\prime\rangle_B)\\
        &=\xi\otimes_A \xi^\prime\langle \eta\otimes_A \eta^\prime\vert\zeta\otimes_A \zeta^\prime\rangle_B\\
