        &=\theta_{\xi\otimes_A \xi^\prime,\eta\otimes_A \eta^\prime}(\zeta\otimes_A \zeta^\prime).\qedhere
    \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
\label{def:intertwining-by-bimodule}
    Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebra, and let $\mathsf A\subseteq1_\mathsf A\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf A,\mathsf B\subseteq 1_\mathsf B \mathsf{M}1_\mathsf B$  subalgebras with expectations. We say that $\mathsf A$ {\em embeds with expectation into $\mathsf B$ inside $M$} and write $\mathsf A\preceq_\mathsf{M} \mathsf B$ if there exist non-zero projections $p
    \in \mathsf A,q\in \mathsf B$, a unital faithful  normal $\ast$-homomorphism $\pi:p\mathsf A p\to q\mathsf B q$ and a partial isometry $w\in p\mathsf{M} q$ such that $\pi(p\mathsf A p)\subseteq q\mathsf B q$ is with expectation and $w\pi(a)=a w, \forall a\in p\mathsf A p.$
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
\label{def: new definition of diffussness}
    Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebra, let $\omega$ be a free ultrafilter on a directed set, and let $\mathsf A\subseteq 1_\mathsf A\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf A$ and $\mathsf B\subseteq1_\mathsf B\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf B$ be inclusions of von Neumann algebras with expectation.  We say that $\mathsf A$ is {\em diffuse relative to $\mathsf B$ inside $\mathsf{M}$ along the ultrafilter $\omega$}, and write $\mathsf A\npreceq_{\mathsf{M}}^\omega\mathsf B$,  if there is a unitary $u\in \mathsf A^\omega$ such that $E_{\mathsf B^\omega}(x^\ast uy)=0$ for all $x,y\in 1_\mathsf A\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf B$.
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{prop: comparion of two inytertwining notion}
    Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a  von Neumann algebra with separable predual, and let $\mathsf A\subseteq1_\mathsf A\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf A, \mathsf B\subseteq1_\mathsf B\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf B$ be inclusion of von Neumann algebras with expectation. Fix $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$. Consider the following statements:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\mathsf A\preceq_\mathsf{M}\mathsf B$ in the sense of Definition \ref{def:intertwining-by-bimodule}.
        \item $\mathsf A\preceq_{\mathsf{M}}^\omega\mathsf B$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then $(1)$ implies $(2)$. If $\mathsf A$ is finite, then $(2)$ implies $(1)$.
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
Let $\varphi$ be a normal faithful state on $1_\mathsf B\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf B$ such that $\mathsf B$ is globally invariant under $\sigma^\varphi$.
    
    (1)$\implies(2)$ Assume that $\mathsf A\npreceq_{\mathsf{M}}^\omega\mathsf B$. Let $u\in \mathsf A^\omega$ be a unitary such that $E_{\mathsf B^\omega}(x^\ast uy)=0$ for $x,y\in 1_\mathsf A\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf B$. Let $(u_n)$ be a sequence of unitaries in $\mathsf A$ such that $(u_n)\in \mathcal{M}^\omega(\mathsf A)$ and $u=(u_n)^\omega$. Let $(x_n)$ be a countable set which spans a  $\sigma$-weakly  dense space in $1_\mathsf A\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf B$. By a recursive argument, there is a subsequence $(n_k)_{k\in\mathbb N}$ of $\mathbb N$ such that $\|E_\mathsf B(x_i^\ast u_{n_k}x_j)\|_{\varphi}\leq 1/k$ for $1\leq i,j\leq k$. Clearly, then $E_\mathsf B(x^\ast u_{n_k}y)\to 0$ $\ast$-strongly as $k\to\infty$ for all $x,y\in \mathsf{M}$. Hence $\mathsf A\npreceq_\mathsf{M}\mathsf B$ by \cite[Theorem 4.3]{HI17}.
    
    Assume that $\mathsf A$ is finite and we prove  (2)$\implies(1)$. So assume that $\mathsf A\npreceq_\mathsf{M}\mathsf B$.   Since $\mathsf A$ has separable predual, there is a sequence $(u_n)$ of unitaries in $\mathsf A$ such that $E_\mathsf B(x^\ast u_ny)\to 0$ $\ast$-strongly as $n\to\infty$ for all $x,y\in 1_\mathsf A\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf B$. Since $\mathsf A$ is finite, $u:=(u_n)^\omega$ is a well-defined element of $\mathsf A^\omega$. Clearly, then for all $x,y\in \mathsf{M}$, we have 
        \begin{align*}
            \|E_{\mathsf B^\omega}(x^\ast u y)\|_{\varphi^\omega}=\lim_{n\to\omega}\|E_\mathsf B(x^\ast u_ny)\|_\varphi=0
        \end{align*}
      This finishes the proof.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- proposition-10: body_md -->
\label{prop; diffusenss in the scalar case}
    Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a  von Neumann algebra with separable predual, and let $\mathsf A\subseteq1_\mathsf A\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf A$ be an inclusion of von Neumann algebras with expectation. Let $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$. Then $\mathsf A$ is diffuse (that is, $\mathsf A\npreceq_\mathsf{M}\mathbb C$) if and only if $\mathsf A\npreceq_{\mathsf{M}}^\omega\mathbb C$.
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- example-4: body_md -->
\label{ex:the notions of intertwining are not equivalent}
 When $\mathsf A$ is not finite, $(2)\implies(1)$  in Proposition \ref{prop: comparion of two inytertwining notion} fails as the following example shows:

 Let ${\mathcal{R}_\lambda}$ be the Power's III$_\lambda$ injective factor for $0<\lambda<1$. Let $\mathsf{N}$ denote the separable hyperfinite II$_\infty$ factor and let $\tau$ denote the tracial normal faithful semifinite weight on $\mathsf{N}$.  By discrete decomposition (see \cite[Theorem 30.1]{Str20}) and the uniqueness of the hyperfinite II$_\infty$ factor, there is an automorphism $\theta$ on $\mathsf{N}$ such that
 \[{\mathcal{R}_\lambda}=\mathsf{N}\rtimes_\theta\mathbb Z,\quad \tau\circ\theta=\lambda\tau.\]
  Denote by $v\in {\mathcal{R}_\lambda}$ the implementing unitary.  Set
 \begin{align*}
     \mathsf{M}={\mathcal{R}_\lambda}\bar\otimes{\mathcal{R}_\lambda},\,\,\mathsf A={\mathcal{R}_\lambda}\bar\otimes\mathbb C,\,\,\mathsf B=\mathsf{N}\bar\otimes{\mathcal{R}_\lambda}.
 \end{align*}
 The inclusions $\mathsf A,\mathsf B\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ admit normal faithful expectations $\operatorname{id}_{{\mathcal{R}_\lambda}}\otimes\psi$ and $E_\mathsf{N}\otimes\operatorname{id}_{{\mathcal{R}_\lambda}}$ respectively, where $E_\mathsf{N}$ is the canonical normal faithful expectation of ${\mathcal{R}_\lambda}$ onto $\mathsf{N}$ and $\psi$ is a normal faithful state on ${\mathcal{R}_\lambda}$ such that $\psi\circ E_\mathsf{N}=\psi$. We claim that $\mathsf A\npreceq_{\mathsf{M}}\mathsf B$ but $\mathsf A\preceq_\mathsf{M}^\omega\mathsf B$ for any $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$.
 
 \textit{To show} $\mathsf A\preceq_\mathsf{M}^\omega\mathsf B$: By \cite[Proposition 6.23, Remark 6.24]{AH14}, discrete decomposition is preserved under the
Ocneanu ultrapower: 
 \[\mathsf{M}^\omega\cong \mathsf{N}^\omega\rtimes_{\theta^\omega}\mathbb Z.\]
  Assume to the contrary that there is a unitary $u\in \mathsf A^\omega\cong \mathcal{R}_{\lambda}^\omega\bar\otimes\mathbb C$ such that $E_{\mathsf B^\omega}(x^\ast uy)=0$ for all $x,y\in \mathsf{M}$.  Fix $k\in\mathbb Z$ and set $y=v^k\otimes1\in \mathsf{M}$. Then $ 0=E_{\mathsf B^\omega}(u(v^k\otimes1))=E_{\mathsf{N}^\omega}(uv^k).$
  This implies
  \[u=\sum_{k\in \mathbb Z}E_{\mathsf{N}^\omega}(uv^{-k})v^k=0,\]
  an obvious contradiction.

  \textit{To show $\mathsf A\npreceq_\mathsf{M}\mathsf B$:} Set $\mathsf C=\langle {\mathcal{R}_\lambda},\mathsf{N}\rangle=J_\psi\mathsf{N}' J_\psi.$ Since  $\mathsf{N}'\cap\mathcal{R}_\lambda=\mathbb C$, we have
${{\mathcal{R}_\lambda}}'\cap \mathsf C=\mathbb C.$
Furthermore, we have
\[
\langle \mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle=\mathsf C\bar\otimes {\mathcal{R}_\lambda},
\quad e_\mathsf B=e_\mathsf{N}\otimes1,\quad
\mathsf A'\cap\langle \mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle=\mathbb C\bar\otimes {\mathcal{R}_\lambda}.
\tag{2}
\]
Let $\widehat E_\mathsf B:\langle \mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle\longrightarrow \mathsf{M}$ be the canonical operator-valued weight, characterized by  $\widehat E_\mathsf B(xe_Bx^*)=xx^*,$ $x\in \mathsf{M}$. We claim that no nonzero positive element of the algebra in $\langle\mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$ has bounded image under $\widehat E_\mathsf B$.
To see this, let $0\ne d=1\otimes z$, where $z\in {\mathcal{R}_\lambda}_+$. For a finite subset $F\subset\mathbb Z$, put
\[
x_F=\sum_{k\in F}v^ke_\mathsf{N} v^{-k}.
\]
Then  $x_F\le1$, so that $0\le x_F\otimes z\le d.$ But,
\begin{align*}
\widehat E_\mathsf B(x_F\otimes z) =\sum_{k\in F}
\widehat E_\mathsf B\!\left(
(v^k\otimes z^{1/2})e_B(v^{-k}\otimes z^{1/2})
\right)=|F|\,(1\otimes z).
\end{align*}
which implies that $\|z\|\leq \frac{1}{|F|}\|\widehat E_\mathsf B(d)\|$. Since $z\neq0$, this proves that  $\widehat E_\mathsf B(d)$ is not bounded. Since $\mathsf A$ is properly infinite, by \cite[Theorem 4.2]{Iso25}, we have thus proved that $\mathsf A\npreceq_\mathsf{M}\mathsf B$.
<!-- end example-4 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
\label{prop:reduction of intertwining to compresssions}
 Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a von Neumann algebra with separable predual, and   let $\mathsf A\subseteq 1_\mathsf A\mathsf{M} 1_\mathsf A, \mathsf B\subseteq1_\mathsf B\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf B$ be inclusions of von Neumann algebras with expectation, and let $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$. If $p\in \mathsf A$ is a non-zero projection such that $p\mathsf A p\preceq_{\mathsf{M}}^\omega\mathsf B$, then $\mathsf A\preceq_{\mathsf{M}}^\omega\mathsf B$.
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Assume  that $\mathsf A\npreceq_{\mathsf{M}}^\omega\mathsf B$.  Let $u\in \mathsf A ^\omega$ be a unitary such that $E_{\mathsf B^\omega}(x^\ast uy)=0$ for all $x,y\in 1_\mathsf A\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf B$. Let $z$ be the central support of $p$ in $\mathsf A$. Let $z_1$ be the maximal central subprojection of $z$ in $\mathsf A$  such that $z_1p$ is a finite projection. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     Set $z_2=z-z_1$ and $p_i=pz_i$ for $i=1,2$, so that $z_2p$ is a properly infinite projection.
     Moreover,  $p_1\mathsf A p_1$ is a finite von Neumann algebra while $p_2\mathsf A p_2$ is a properly infinite von Neumann algebra. 

Firstly we have $p_2\mathsf A p_2\npreceq_{\mathsf{M}}^\omega\mathsf B$; Indeed, since $p_2$ is a properly infinite projection in $z_2\mathsf A$, there is a partial isometry $v\in z_2\mathsf A$ such that $v^\ast v=p_2$ and $vv^\ast =z_2$. Set $u_2=v^\ast u v\in (p_2\mathsf A p_2)^\omega$. Clearly, $u_2$ is a unitary since $z_2$ commutes with $u$ and  we have $E_{\mathsf B^\omega}(x^\ast u_2 y)=0$ for all $x,y\in p_2\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf B$.

We next claim that $p_1\mathsf A p_1\npreceq_{\mathsf{M}}^\omega\mathsf B$. If not, then $p_\mathsf A p_1\preceq_\mathsf{M}^\omega\mathsf B$, and since $p_1\mathsf A p_1$ is finite, we have $p_1\mathsf A p_1\preceq_\mathsf{M}\mathsf B$ by Proposition \ref{prop: comparion of two inytertwining notion}. It then follows from \cite[Remark 4.2]{HI17} that $\mathsf A\preceq_{\mathsf{M}}\mathsf B$, and another use of Proposition \ref{prop: comparion of two inytertwining notion} says that $\mathsf A\preceq_{\mathsf{M}}^\omega\mathsf B$. This contradicts our assumption. Thus we have $p_1\mathsf A p_1\npreceq_{\mathsf{M}}^\omega\mathsf B$, so one gets a unitary $u_1\in (p_1\mathsf A p_1)^\omega$   such that $E_{\mathsf B^\omega}(x^\ast u_1 y)=0$ for all $x,y\in p_1\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf B$.

 Set $u=u_1+u_2\in \mathcal{U}((p\mathsf A p)^\omega)$. Clearly then we have $E_{\mathsf B^\omega}(x^\ast u y)=0$ for all $x,y\in p\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf B$. This proves that $p\mathsf A p\npreceq_{\mathsf{M}}^\omega\mathsf B$.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- proposition-12: body_md -->
\label{prop:convergence of deformation with compact resolvent gives intertwining}
Let $\mathsf B,\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ be inclusion of von Neumann algebras with expectation, and let $\omega$ be a cofinal ultrafilter on a directed set. Let $T_i$ be a net of operators in $C^\ast(\mathsf{M} e_\mathsf B \mathsf{M})$ such that $T_i^\omega$ strongly converges to identity on $L^2(\mathsf{Q}^\omega)$ along $i$. We have $p\mathsf{Q} p\preceq_{\mathsf{M}}^\omega\mathsf B$ for each projection $p\in \mathsf{Q}$.
<!-- end proposition-12 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
Let $\varphi$ be a normal faithful state such that $\varphi\circ E_\mathsf B=\varphi$. Set $\psi=\varphi^\omega$.
Assume to the contrary that there is a non-zero projection in $p\in \mathsf{Q}$  such that $p\mathsf{Q} p\npreceq_{\mathsf{M}}^\omega\mathsf B$. Then there is a non-zero element $u\in (p\mathsf{Q} p)^\omega$ such that $E_{\mathsf B^\omega}(x^\ast u y)=0$ for all $x,y\in \mathsf{M}$. This implies that for all $z\in \mathsf{M}$, we have \[\|(ye_\mathsf B x)^\omega
(uz\psi^{1/2})\|=\|ye_{B^\omega}x(uz\psi^{1/2})\|\leq \|y\| \|E_{B^\omega}(xuz)\|_\psi=0\]
and hence
\[T^\omega u(z\varphi^{1/2})^\omega=T^\omega (uz\psi^{1/2})=0\] for each $T\in C^\ast(\mathsf{M} e_{\mathsf B}\mathsf{M})$ and $z\in \mathsf{M}$, which further implies that    $T^\omega u(\eta)^\omega=0$ for all $\eta\in L^2(\mathsf{M})$, since $\mathsf{M}\varphi^{1/2}$ is dense in $L^2(\mathsf{M})$. Let $\varphi_1$ be a normal faithful state on $\mathsf{M}$ such that $\mathsf{Q}$ is globally invariant under $\sigma^{\varphi_1}$. Set $\psi_1=\varphi_1^\omega$. Thus what we have proved implies in particular that 
\[T^\omega(u\psi_1^{1/2})=T^\omega u(\varphi_1^{1/2})^\omega=0.\] In particular, we have $T_i^\omega(u\psi_1^{1/2})=0$ for each $i$. But then $u\psi_1^{1/2}\in L^2(\mathsf{Q}^\omega)$; so the hypothesis implies that $T_i^\omega(u\psi_1^{1/2})\to u\psi_1^{1/2}$ along $i$. Consequently, we obtain $u\psi_{1}^{1/2}=0$, an obvious contradiction.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- proposition-13: body_md -->
\label{prop:convergence of deformation with compact resolvent for tracial Q}
Let $\mathsf B,\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ be inclusion of von Neumann algebras with expectation, and let $\omega$ be a cofinal ultrafilter on a directed set.  Let $T_i$ be a net of operators in $C^\ast(\mathsf{M} e_\mathsf B \mathsf{M})$. If $\mathsf{Q}$ is finite and such that $T_i$ uniformly converges along $i$ to identity on the unit ball of $\mathsf{Q}$, then  for each projection $p\in \mathsf{Q}$ we have $p\mathsf{Q} p\preceq_{\mathsf{M}}\mathsf B$ in the sense of Definition \ref{def:intertwining-by-bimodule}.
<!-- end proposition-13 -->
<!-- proposition-14: body_md -->
\label{prop:convergence of deformation with compact resolvent gives intertwining on relative commutatant}
Let $\mathsf B,\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ be inclusion of von Neumann algebras with expectation, and let $\omega$ be a cofinal ultrafilter on a directed set.  Let $T_i$ be a net of operators in $C^\ast(\mathsf{M} e_\mathsf B \mathsf{M})$ such that $T_i^\omega$ strongly converges to identity on $L^2(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega)$ along $i$. Then for every projection $p\in \mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega$ and a unitary $u\in p(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega)p$, there is $x\in \mathsf{M}$ such that   $E_{\mathsf B^\omega}(x^\ast u x)\neq 0$.
<!-- end proposition-14 -->
<!-- proposition-15: body_md -->
\label{prop:convergence of deformation with compact resolvent gives atomicity}
Let $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ be inclusion of von Neumann algebras with expectation, and let $\omega\in \beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$.  Let $T_i$ be a net of compact operators  such that $T_i^\omega\xi\to\xi$  for all $\xi\in L^2(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega)$ (resp. $\mathsf{Q}^\omega$) along $i$. Then $\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega$ and hence $\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}$ (resp. $\mathsf{Q}^\omega$ and hence $\mathsf{Q}$) are completely atomic.
<!-- end proposition-15 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
We prove the result only for $\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega$. For every compact operator $T$ on $L^2(\mathsf{M})$, we have
$T^\omega(L^2(\mathsf{M})^\omega)\subset L^2(\mathsf{M}).$ Indeed, this holds for finite-rank operators, and then follows for compact operators by norm approximation. Thus for all $\xi\in L^2(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega)$, each $T_i\xi\in L^2(\mathsf{M})$ which, by hypothesis, implies that $\xi\in L^2(\mathsf{M})$. This proves 
$L^2(Q'\cap M^\omega)\subseteq L^2(\mathsf{M})
$ which further implies $\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega\subseteq\mathsf{M}$, and hence $\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}=(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M})^\omega$. By \cite[Theorem 2.3]{HR15}, it follows that $\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}$ is atomic.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- proposition-16: body_md -->
If a von Neumann algebra $\mathsf{M}$ admits a modular derivation $\delta\colon \text{dom}(\delta)\subset L^2(\mathsf{M})\to \mathsf{H} $ with $\mathsf{H} \prec L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2(\mathsf{M})$ such that $\delta^\ast\bar\delta$ has compact resolvent then $\mathsf{M}$ is $\omega$-solid for every cofinal ultrafilter $\omega$ on a directed set  and hence $\mathsf{M}$ is solid.
<!-- end proposition-16 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
Fix a cofinal ultrafilter $\omega$ on a directed set.
Let $\mathsf{Q}$ be a subalgebra of $\mathsf{M}$ with expectation such that $\mathsf{Q}$ is not amenable. Let $p\in \mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{Q})$ be a non-zero projection such that $p\mathsf{Q}$ has no amenable summand.  By  Theorem \ref{main_theorem}, $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ converges strongly  on $L^2(p(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega))$. Since $\theta_\alpha^{(2)}$ is compact for each $\alpha>0$, $p(\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega)$ is atomic  by Proposition \ref{prop:convergence of deformation with compact resolvent gives intertwining}; hence $\mathsf{Q}'\cap\mathsf{M}^\omega$ is not diffuse.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
\label{thm:omega-solidity}
 Let $\mathsf B\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ be an inclusion of  von Neumann algebras  with expectation  such that $\mathsf{M}$ has separable predual, and   let $\delta:\operatorname{dom}\delta\subseteq L^2(\mathsf{M})\to\mathsf{H}$ be a densely defined closable modular derivation such that $\mathsf B\subseteq\operatorname{Null}(\bar\delta)$. Assume that there exist $\mathsf B$-$\mathsf B$ correspondences $\mathsf{K}$ and $\mathsf{K}_t$ for $t\geq 0$ such that $_\mathsf{M}\mathsf{H}_\mathsf{M}\prec {_\mathsf{M} L^2(\mathsf{M})}\otimes_\mathsf B\mathsf{K}\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M})_\mathsf{M}$ and $_\mathsf{M}(\mathsf{H}_{\Phi_t})_\mathsf B\prec {_\mathsf{M} L^2(\mathsf{M})}\otimes_\mathsf B (\mathsf{K}_t)_\mathsf B$ for $t\geq 0$. If  $\delta^\ast\bar\delta$ has compact resolvent relative to $\mathsf B$, then $\mathsf{M}$ is $\omega$-solid relative to $\mathsf B$ for any cofinal ultrafilter $\omega$.
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
Let $\omega$ be a cofinal ultrafilter on a directed set $I$.    Let $\mathsf{Q}$ be a subalgebra of $1_\mathsf{Q}\mathsf{M}1_\mathsf{Q}$ with expectation $\mathsf{Q}$ is completely nonamenable relative to $\mathsf B$. 
 By Theorem \ref{main_theorem}, $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)})^\omega$ converges strongly to the identity on $L^2(\mathsf{Q}'\cap1_\mathsf{Q}\mathsf{M}^\omega1_\mathsf{Q})$ as $\alpha\to\infty$. By Proposition \ref{prop:convergence of deformation with compact resolvent gives intertwining on relative commutatant}, we have the result.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- theorem-13: body_md -->
\label{thm:stable solidity}
    Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a   von Neumann algebra with separable predual and with a densely defined closable modular  derivation $\delta:\operatorname{dom}(\delta)\subseteq L^2(\mathsf{M})\to\mathsf{H}$, let $\mathsf B\subseteq\operatorname{Null}(\bar\delta)$. Assume that there exist $\mathsf B$-$\mathsf B$ correspondences $\mathsf{K}$ and $\mathsf{K}_t$ for $t\geq 0$ such that $_\mathsf{M}\mathsf{H}_\mathsf{M}\prec {_\mathsf{M} L^2(\mathsf{M})}\otimes_\mathsf B\mathsf{K}\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M})_\mathsf{M}$, $_\mathsf{M}(\mathsf{H}_{\Phi_t})_\mathsf B\prec{_\mathsf{M} L^2(\mathsf{M})}\otimes_\mathsf B(\mathsf{K}_t)_\mathsf B$ and that $\delta^\ast\bar\delta$ has a compact resolvent relative to $\mathsf B$. Then $\mathsf{M}$ is stably solid relative to $\mathsf B$ along $\omega$, for any $\omega\in \beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$.
<!-- end theorem-13 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf{N}$ be a $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebra with faithful normal state $\psi$ and $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq \mathsf{M}\bar\otimes\mathsf{N}$  be a subalgebra with expectation such that $\mathsf{Q}'\cap(\mathsf{M}\overline{\otimes\mathsf{N}})\npreceq^\omega_{\mathsf{M}\overline{\otimes}\mathsf{N}} \mathsf B\otimes\mathsf{N}.$ Consider the tensor product derivation $\delta_1:=\delta\otimes \mathrm{id}$ on $\operatorname{dom}(\delta)\odot\mathsf{N}_\infty \psi^{1/2}$ taking values in $\mathsf{H}_1:=\mathsf{H}\otimes L^2(\mathsf{N})$ whose semigroup is given by $e^{-t\delta^\ast\bar\delta}\otimes 1.$ Then $\delta_1$ is a modular derivation and $\mathsf B\overline\otimes\mathsf{N}=\operatorname{Null}(\bar\delta_1).$ Moreover, $\delta_1^\ast\bar\delta_1$ has compact resolvent relative to $\mathsf B\bar\otimes\mathsf{N}$. Give $\mathsf{K}\otimes L^2(\mathsf{N})$ the obvious $\mathsf B\overline{\otimes}\mathsf{N}$-bimodule structure. Then  as an $\mathsf{M}\bar\otimes\mathsf{N}$ correspondence, we have 
  \begin{align*}
       \mathsf{H}_1&\prec (L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes_\mathsf B \mathsf{K}\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M}))\otimes L^2(\mathsf{N})\\
       &\cong (L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2(\mathsf{N}))\otimes_{\mathsf B\overline{\otimes}\mathsf{N}}(\mathsf{K}\otimes L^2(\mathsf{N}))\otimes_{\mathsf B\overline{\otimes}\mathsf{N}} (L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes L^2(\mathsf{N})).
  \end{align*}
  Now if $\mathsf{Q}$ is not amenable relative to $\mathsf B\bar\otimes\mathsf{N}$, there is a projection $q\in \mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{Q}'\cap (\mathsf{M}\bar\otimes\mathsf{N}))$ such that $q\mathsf{Q}$ has no amenable summand relative to $\mathsf B\bar\otimes\mathsf{N}$. This means by Theorem \ref{main_theorem} that $(\theta_\alpha^{(2)}\otimes 1_\mathsf{N})^\omega$ converge uniformly on $q\mathsf{Q}'\cap (\mathsf{M}\overline{\otimes}\mathsf{N})^\omega$ for every cofinal ultrafilter on a directed set.  By Proposition \ref{prop:convergence of deformation with compact resolvent gives intertwining}, it follows that $\mathsf{Q}'\cap(\mathsf{M}\overline{\otimes\mathsf{N}})\preceq_{\mathsf{M}\overline{\otimes}\mathsf{N}}^\omega\mathsf B\bar\otimes\mathsf{N}$, a contradiction.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- corollary-9: body_md -->
\label{thm:stable solidity_finite case}
    Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a tracial  von Neumann algebra with   a densely defined closable modular  derivation $\delta:\operatorname{dom}(\delta)\subseteq L^2(\mathsf{M})\to\mathsf{H}$, let $\mathsf B=\operatorname{Null}(\bar\delta)$. Assume that there exist $\mathsf B$-$\mathsf B$ correspondences $\mathsf{K}$ and $\mathsf{K}_t$ for $t\geq 0$ such that $_\mathsf{M}\mathsf{H}_\mathsf{M}\prec {_\mathsf{M} L^2(\mathsf{M})}\otimes_\mathsf B\mathsf{K}\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M})_\mathsf{M}$, $_\mathsf{M}(\mathsf{H}_{\Phi_t})_\mathsf B\prec{_\mathsf{M} L^2(\mathsf{M})}\otimes_\mathsf B(\mathsf{K}_t)_\mathsf B$ and that $\delta^\ast\bar\delta$ has a compact resolvent relative to $\mathsf B$. Then for every finite von Neumann subalgebra $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq (\mathsf{M}\overline{\otimes}\mathsf{N})$  such that $\mathsf{Q}'\cap (\mathsf{M}\overline{\otimes}\mathsf{N})\npreceq_{\mathsf{M}\overline{\otimes}\mathsf{N}}\mathsf B\otimes\mathsf{N}$, we have that $\mathsf{Q}$ is amenable relative to $\mathsf B\otimes\mathsf{N}.$
<!-- end corollary-9 -->
<!-- corollary-10: body_md -->
\label{thm:stable solidity_amenable_case}
    Let $\mathsf B\subseteq\mathsf{M}$ be an inclusion of   von Neumann algebras with separable predual and with expectation such that $\mathsf B$ is amenable. If  $\delta:\operatorname{dom}\delta\subseteq L^2(\mathsf{M})\to\mathsf{H}$ is a densely defined closable modular  derivation  such that $\mathsf{H}\prec L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M})$ and $\delta^\ast\bar\delta$ has a compact resolvent relative to $\mathsf B$, then $\mathsf{M}$ is stably solid relative to $\mathsf B$ along $\omega$ for $\omega\in \beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$.
<!-- end corollary-10 -->
<!-- proposition-17: body_md -->
If $\Phi_j\colon \mathsf{M}_j\to \mathsf{M}_j$ is a $\varphi$-preserving ucp map with $\Phi_j^{(2)}\in \mathbb K(\mathsf B\subset \mathsf{M}_j,\varphi_j)$ for $j\in \{1,2\}$ and $\lVert\Phi_1^{(2)}|_{L^2_0(\mathsf{M}_1)}\rVert<1$, then $(\Phi_1\ast_\mathsf B \Phi_2)^{(2)}\in\mathbb K(\mathsf B\subset \mathsf{M}_1\ast_\mathsf B \mathsf{M}_2,\varphi))$.
<!-- end proposition-17 -->
<!-- lemma-27: body_md -->
If $\mathcal E$ is the quantum Dirichlet form associated with $(\Phi_t)_{t\geq 0}$, then $\mathfrak A$ is a Tomita subalgebra of the maximal Tomita algebra associated with $\varphi$, it satisfies $\mathfrak A\subset \mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}$ and it is a form core for $\mathcal E$.
<!-- end lemma-27 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
From the description of the modular conjugation and modular operator, it is not hard to see that $\mathfrak A$ is a Tomita subalgebra of the maximal Tomita algebra associated with $\varphi$.
    
    Since $\Phi_t(b)=b$ for $b\in \mathsf B$, we have $\mathsf B_\infty \varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}\subset \mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}$.
    
    To show that 
    \begin{equation*}
        \bigcup_{(j_1,\dots,j_n)\in\mathbf J_n}\{a_1\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B} a_n\mid a_k\in \mathfrak A_{j_k}\cap L^2_0(\mathsf{M}_{j_k})\text{ for }1\leq k\leq n\}\subset \mathfrak A_{\mathcal E},
    \end{equation*}
    we proceed by induction over $n\in\mathbb N$. Since 
    \begin{equation*}
        \Phi_t^{(2)}=\operatorname{id}_{L^2(\mathsf B)}\oplus\bigoplus_{n\geq 1}\bigoplus_{(j_1,\dots,j_n)\in\mathbf J_n}\Phi_{j_1,t}^{(2)}|_{L^2_0(\mathsf{M}_{j_1})}\otimes_\mathsf B\dots\otimes_\mathsf B \Phi_{j_n,t}^{(2)}|_{L^2_0(\mathsf{M}_{j_n})}
    \end{equation*}
    and
    \begin{equation*}
        \Delta_\varphi^{it}=\Delta_{\varphi_\mathsf B}^{it}\oplus\bigoplus_{n\geq 1}\bigoplus_{(j_1,\dots,j_n)\in \mathbf J_n}\Delta_{\varphi_{j_1}}^{it}\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\Delta_{\varphi_{j_n}}^{it},
    \end{equation*}
    the case $n=1$ is immediate.
    
    Assume that we have proven the claim for $n\in\mathbb N$. If $(j_1,\dots,j_{n+1})\in\mathbf J_{n+1}$ and $a_k\in \mathfrak A_{j_k}\cap L^2_0(\mathsf{M}_{j_k})$ for $1\leq k\leq n+1$, then 
    \begin{equation*}
        a_1\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\otimes \dots \otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_{n+1}=\pi_l(a_1)a_2\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\otimes \dots \otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_{n+1}.
    \end{equation*}
    Since $\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}$ is a left Hilbert algebra and $a_1,a_2\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\otimes \dots \otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_{n+1}\in \mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}$, we conclude that $a_1\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\otimes \dots \otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_{n+1}\in\mathfrak A_{\mathcal E}$.

    To show that $\mathfrak A$ is a form core for $\mathcal E$, we first show that it is dense in $\mathsf{H}$. For this purpose, we prove by induction over $n\in\mathbb N$ that for every $(j_1,\dots,j_n)\in\mathbf J_n$ the set
    \begin{equation*}
        \operatorname{span} \{a_1\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B} a_n\mid a_k\in \mathfrak A_{j_k}\cap L^2_0(\mathsf{M}_{j_k})\text{ for }1\leq k\leq n\}
    \end{equation*}
    is dense in $L^2_0(\mathsf{M}_{j_1})\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\otimes\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}L^2_0(\mathsf{M}_{j_n})$.

    For the case $n=1$, let $P_j\colon L^2(\mathsf{M}_j)\to L^2_0(\mathsf{M}_j)$ be the orthogonal projection. Since $\Phi_{j,t}$ commutes with $E_j$, it follows easily that $P_j(\mathfrak A_j)\subset \mathfrak A_j$. Combined with the fact that $\mathfrak A_j$ is dense in $L^2(\mathsf{M}_j)$, we obtain the claim for $n=1$.

    Now suppose that the claim is true for $n$ and let $(j_1,\dots,j_{n+1})\in \mathbf J_{n+1}$, $\xi\in \mathcal D(L^2_0(\mathsf{M}_{j_1})_\mathsf B,\varphi_\mathsf B)$, $\eta\in L^2_0(\mathsf{M}_{j_2})\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\otimes\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}L^2_0(\mathsf{M}_{j_{n+1}})$. Note that $L_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(\xi)\in \mathcal L(L^2(\mathsf B)_\mathsf B,L^2(\mathsf{M}_{j_1})_\mathsf B)=\mathcal L(L^2(\mathsf{M}_{j_1})_\mathsf B)\iota_{j_1}$. Since $\mathcal L(L^2(\mathsf{M}_{j_1})_\mathsf B)$ is the weak$^\ast$ closed linear span of $\{ye_\mathsf B z\mid y,z\in \mathsf{M}_{j_1}\}$ and $y e_\mathsf B z\iota_{j_1}=yE_{j_1}(z)\iota_{j_1}\in \mathsf{M}_{j_1}\iota_{j_1}$, there exists $x\in \mathsf{M}_{j_1}$ such that $L_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(\xi)\iota_{j_1}=x\iota_{j_1}$.
    
    By the induction hypothesis, there exists a sequence $(\eta_k)$ in $\operatorname{span}\{a_2\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B} a_{n+1}\mid a_k\in \mathfrak A_{j_k}\cap L^2_0(\mathsf{M}_{j_k})\text{ for }2\leq k\leq n+1\}$ that converges to $\eta$. Moreover, by \cite[Theorem 6.3]{Wir22} there exists a sequence $(a_k)$ in $\mathfrak A_1$ such that $\lVert\pi_l(a_k)\rVert\leq \lVertx\rVert$ and $\pi_l(a_k)\to x$ in strong operator topology. Therefore,
    \begin{align*}
        \lVert\xi\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\eta-a_k\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\eta_k\rVert&\leq \lVert(\xi-a_k)\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\eta\rVert+\lVerta_k\otimes_{\varphi_{\mathsf B}}(\eta-\eta_k)\rVert\\
        &\leq\langle \eta,\pi_l^\mathsf{K}(\lvert (x-\pi_l(a_k))\iota_{j_1}\rvert^2)\eta\rangle^{1/2}+\lVertx\rVert\lVert\eta-\eta_k\rVert,
    \end{align*}
    where $\mathsf{K}=L^2_0(\mathsf{M}_{j_2})\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\otimes\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\varphi}L^2_0(\mathsf{M}_{j_{n+1}})$. By assumption, the right side converges to zero.

    Thus we have proven that $\mathfrak A$ is dense in $\mathsf{H}$. Moreover, it is evidently invariant under $\Phi_t^{(2)}$ for all $t\geq 0$. Hence it is a form core by \cite[Lemma 3.4]{Wir22}.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- lemma-28: body_md -->
If $\delta_j\colon \mathfrak A_{\mathcal E_j}\to L^2(\mathsf{N}_j)\ominus L^2(\mathsf{M}_j)$ is the $\varphi_j$-modular derivation associated with $(\Phi_t^{(j)})_{t\geq 0}$ and
    \begin{equation*}
        \delta\colon \mathfrak A\to L^2(\mathsf{N}_1\ast_\mathsf B \mathsf{N}_2)\ominus L^2(\mathsf{M}_1\ast_\mathsf B \mathsf{M}_2)
    \end{equation*}
    is given by $\delta|_{\mathsf B_\infty\varphi^{1/2}}=0$ and
    \begin{equation*}
        \delta(a_1\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_n)=\sum_{k=1}^n a_1\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_{k-1}\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\delta_{j_k}(a_k)\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_{k+1}\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_n
    \end{equation*}
    for $a_k\in \mathfrak A_{j_k}\cap L^2_0(\mathsf{M}_{j_k})$ and $(j_1,\dots,j_n)\in\mathbf J_n$, then $\delta$ is a $\varphi$-modular derivation and
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathcal E(a)=\lVert\delta(a)\rVert^2
    \end{equation*}
    for $a\in\mathfrak A$.
<!-- end lemma-28 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
From the description of the modular data for $\varphi$, it is not hard to see that $\delta$ is a $\varphi$-modular derivation. Moreover, if $a_k\in \mathfrak A_{j_k}\cap L^2_0(\mathsf{M}_{j_k})$ for $1\leq k\leq n$ and $(j_1,\dots,j_n)\in\mathbf J_n$ and $a_k^\prime\in \mathfrak A_{_k}\cap L^2_0(\mathsf{M}_{i_k})$ for $1\leq k\leq m$ and $(i_1,\dots,i_m)\in\mathbf J_n$, then 
    \begin{equation*}
        \langle\delta(a_1\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B} \dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_n),\delta(a_1^\prime\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_m^\prime)\rangle=0
    \end{equation*}
    unless $m=n$ and $j_1=i_1$.

    In this case, write $a_{<k}$ for $a_1\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_{k-1}$ and $a_{>k}$ for $a_{k+1}\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_n$. We have
    \begin{align*}
        &\quad\langle\delta(a_1\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B} \dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_n),\delta(a_1^\prime\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_n^\prime)\rangle\\
        &=\sum_{k=1}^n \langle a_{<k}\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\delta_{j_k}(a_k)\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_{>k}, a_{<k}^\prime\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\delta_{j_k}(a_k^\prime)\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_{>k}^\prime\rangle\\
        &=\sum_{k=1}^n \langle \delta_{j_k}(a_k),\delta_{j_k}(L_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(a_{<k})^\ast L_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(a_{<k}^\prime)\cdot a_k^\prime\cdot J_{\varphi_\mathsf B}R_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(a_{>k}^\prime)^\ast R_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(a_{>k})J_{\varphi_\mathsf B})\rangle\\
        &=-\frac{d}{dt}\bigg|_{t=0}\sum_{k=1}^n \langle a_k,\Phi_{t,j_k}^{(2)}(L_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(a_{<k})^\ast L_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(a_{<k}^\prime)\cdot a_k^\prime\cdot J_{\varphi_\mathsf B}R_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(a_{>k}^\prime)^\ast R_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(a_{>k})J_{\varphi_\mathsf B})\rangle\\
        &=-\frac{d}{dt}\bigg|_{t=0}\sum_{k=1}^n \langle a_k,L_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(a_{<k})^\ast L_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(a_{<k}^\prime)\cdot(\Phi_{t,j_k}^{(2)} a_k^\prime)\cdot J_{\varphi_\mathsf B}R_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(a_{>k}^\prime)^\ast R_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(a_{>k})J_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\rangle\\
        &=-\frac{d}{dt}\bigg|_{t=0}\sum_{k=1}^n \langle a_{<k}\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_k\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_{>k},a_{<k}^\prime\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\Phi_{t,j_k}^{(2)}(a_k^\prime)\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_{>k}^\prime\rangle\\
        &=-\frac{d}{dt}\bigg|_{t=0}\langle a_1\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_n,\Phi_t^{(2)}(a_1\prime\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_n^\prime)\rangle\\
        &=\mathcal E(a_1\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_n,a_1\prime\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}a_n^\prime),
    \end{align*}
    where we used that $\Phi_{t,j_k}^{(2)}$ and $\delta_{j_k}$ are $\mathsf B$-bimodule maps.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- remark-8: body_md -->
As discussed in Subsection \ref{subsec:bimodules}, it is not restrictive to assume that $\delta_j$ takes values in $L^2(\mathsf{N}_j)\ominus L^2(\mathsf{M}_j)$. In the special case when $\delta_j\colon \mathfrak A_{\mathcal E_j}\to L^2(\mathsf{M}_j)\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M}_j)$, the formula from the previous lemma shows that $\operatorname{ran}\delta\subset (L^2(\mathsf{M}_1\bar\ast_\mathsf B M_2)\otimes_\mathsf B L^2(\mathsf{M}_1\bar\ast_\mathsf B \mathsf{M}_2))^{\oplus 2}$. In particular, this is the case for the derivation $\delta_j$ associated with the dephasing semigroup $(\Phi_{j,t}=e^{-t}\mathrm{id}_{\mathsf{M}_j}+(1-e^{-t})E_\mathsf B$ discussed in the beginning of the section. Thus, if $\mathrm{id}_{L^2(\mathsf{M}_j)}\in\mathbb K(\mathsf B\subset \mathsf{M}_j,\varphi_j)$, then the solidity results from Section~\ref{sec:solidity} apply to $\mathsf{M}_1\bar\ast_\mathsf B \mathsf{M}_2$.
<!-- end remark-8 -->
<!-- theorem-14: body_md -->
\label{thm:solidity for amalgamated free products}
    Let $\mathsf{M}_1,\mathsf{M}_2$ be $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebras with a common von Neumann subalgebra $\mathsf B$ with expectations such that $\mathrm{id}_{L^2(\mathsf{M}_j)}\in\mathbb K(\mathsf B\subset \mathsf{M}_j,\varphi_j)$ for $j=1,2$. Then $\mathsf{M}_1\bar\ast_\mathsf B\mathsf{M}_2$ is $\omega$-solid relative to $\mathsf B$ and stable solid relative to $\mathsf B$ along $\omega$ for any $\omega\in \beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$.
<!-- end theorem-14 -->
<!-- lemma-29: body_md -->
\label{lem:rel_compact_Fock_space}
    Assume that there exists a finite family $(\xi_\lambda,p_\lambda)_{\lambda\in \Lambda}$ with $\xi_\lambda\in \mathcal D(\mathsf{H},\varphi_\mathsf B)\cap \operatorname{dom}(\mathcal U_{-i/2})$, $\mathcal J\mathcal U_{-i/2}\xi_\lambda\in \mathcal D(\mathsf{H},\varphi_\mathsf B)$ and $p_\lambda\in \mathsf B$ a projection for $\lambda \in \Lambda$ such that $L_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(\xi_\lambda)^\ast L_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(\xi_\mu)=\delta_{\lambda,\mu}p_\lambda$ for all $\lambda,\mu\in \Lambda$ and
    \begin{equation*}
        \sum_{\lambda\in \Lambda}L_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(\xi_\lambda) L_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(\xi_\lambda)^\ast=1_\mathsf{H}.
    \end{equation*}
    The operator $\mathcal F(e^{-t})$ belongs to $\mathbb K(\mathsf B\subset \mathsf{M},\varphi)$ for all $t>0$.
<!-- end lemma-29 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
Let $P_n$ be the orthogonal projection from $\mathcal F(_\mathsf{M} \mathsf{H} _M)$ onto $\mathsf{H}^{\otimes_\mathsf B n}$. Since $\mathcal F(e^{-t})=\sum_{n=0}^\infty e^{-nt}P_n$, it suffices to prove that $P_n\in \mathbb K(\mathsf B\subset M,\varphi)$ for all $n\in\mathbb N$.

    For $(i_1,\dots,i_n)\in \Lambda^n$ let $\xi_{(i_1,\dots,i_n)}=\xi_{i_1}\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\xi_{i_n}$and define inductively $x_{\emptyset}=1$, $x_i=a^\ast(\xi_i)+a(\mathcal J\mathcal U_{-i/2})$ and $x_{(i_1,\dots,i_n)}=x_{i_1} x_{(i_2,\dots,i_n)}-(L_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(\xi_{i_1})^\ast L_{\varphi_\mathsf B}(\xi_{i_2}))\cdot x_{(i_3,\dots,i_n)}$ for $n\geq 2$. By definition, $x_{(i_1,\dots,i_n)}\in \mathsf{M}$ and one checks recursively that $x_{(i_1,\dots,i_n)}\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}=\xi_{(i_1,\dots,i_n)}$ for all $(i_1,\dots,i_n)\in \Lambda^n$ and $n\in\mathbb N$.
    
    The set $(\xi_{(i_1,\dots,i_n)},p_{(i_1,\dots,i_n)})_{(i_1,\dots,i_n)\in \Lambda^n}$ forms a quasi-orthonormal basis of $\Lambda^n$, which implies 
    \begin{equation*}
        P_n=\sum_{(i_1,\dots,i_n)\in \Lambda^n}x_{(i_1,\dots,i_n)} e_\mathsf B x_{(i_1,\dots,i_n)}^\ast\in C^\ast(\mathsf{M} e_\mathsf B \mathsf{M})
    \end{equation*}
    for all $n\in\mathbb N$.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- proposition-18: body_md -->
\label{prop:construction of QMS on Free-Araki Woods}
    Let $T\colon \mathsf{H}\to \mathsf{H}$ be a bounded self-adjoint $\mathsf B$-bimodule map with $\lVertT\rVert\leq 1$ such that $\mathcal J T=T\mathcal J$ and $\mathcal U_t T=T\mathcal U_t$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$. There exists a unique GNS-symmetric ucp map $\Phi$ on $\Gamma(_\mathsf B\mathsf{H}_\mathsf B,\mathcal J,(\mathcal U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R})$ such that $\mathcal F(T)=\Phi^{(2)}$.

    Moreover, if $\mathsf{H}_\Phi$ denotes the minimal Stinespring correspondence for $\Phi$, then there exists a $\mathsf B$-$\mathsf B$ correspondence $\mathsf{K}$ such that $_\mathsf{M}(\mathsf{H}_\Phi)_\mathsf B\subset {_\mathsf{M} \mathcal F(\mathsf{H})}\otimes_\mathsf B \mathsf{K}_\mathsf B$.
<!-- end proposition-18 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
The proof of the first part is a simple modification of \cite[Theorem 2.11]{BKS97}. Let $_\mathsf B\tilde \mathsf{H}_\mathsf B={_\mathsf B\mathsf{H}_\mathsf B}\oplus {_\mathsf B\mathsf{H}_\mathsf B}$, $\tilde{\mathcal J}=\mathcal J\oplus \mathcal J$, $\tilde{\mathcal U_t}=\mathcal U_t\oplus\mathcal U_t$, $\tilde\mathsf{M}=\Gamma(_\mathsf B\tilde \mathsf{H}_\mathsf B,\tilde{\mathcal J},(\tilde{\mathcal U}_t)_{t\in\mathbb R})$ and
    \begin{equation*}
        \tilde T=\begin{pmatrix}T&(1-T^2)^{1/2}\\1-T^2)^{1/2}&-T\end{pmatrix}\in \mathbb B(\tilde\mathsf{H}).
    \end{equation*}
    Clearly, $\tilde T$ is a $\mathsf B$-bimodule map that commutes with $\tilde{\mathcal J}$ and $\tilde{\mathcal U_t}$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$. Moreover, $\tilde T$ is unitary.

    Let $\iota\colon \mathsf{M}\to\tilde \mathsf{M}$ be the $\ast$-homomorphism that maps $s(\xi)$ to $s(\xi,0)$ for $\xi\in \mathcal D(\mathsf{H},\varphi_\mathsf B)\cap \operatorname{dom}(\mathcal U_{-i/2})$ with $\mathcal J\mathcal U_{-i/2}\xi=\xi$ and $\pi_l^{\mathcal F(_\mathsf B\mathsf{H}_\mathsf B)}(b)$ to $\pi_l^{\mathcal F(_\mathsf B\tilde \mathsf{H}_\mathsf B)}(b)$ for $b\in \mathsf B$.
    
    Let $\tilde\varphi$ be the vector state induced by $\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}$ on $\tilde\mathsf{M}$. By the description of the modular theory of $\varphi$ in \cite[Section 5.2]{KW25}, the image $\iota(\mathsf{M})$ is globally invariant under $\sigma^{\tilde\varphi}$. Let $E\colon \tilde\mathsf{M}\to\iota(\mathsf{M})$ be the $\tilde\varphi$-preserving conditional expectation.
    
    Finally, let $\alpha=\mathrm{ad}(\mathcal F(\tilde T))$. We have $\alpha(s(\xi))=s(\tilde T \xi)$ for $\xi\in \mathcal D(\tilde\mathsf{H},\varphi_\mathsf B)\cap\operatorname{dom}(\tilde{\mathcal U}_{-i/2})$ with $\tilde{\mathcal J}\tilde{\mathcal U}_{-i/2}\xi=\xi$ and $\alpha(b)=b$ for $b\in \mathsf B$ so that $\alpha$ leaves $\mathsf{M}$ globally invariant. We define $\Phi=\iota^{-1}E\alpha \iota$. Note that $\Phi$ commutes with $\sigma^\varphi$. The fact that $\Phi^{(2)}=\mathcal F(T)$ follows by a direct calculation.

    Let $W\colon \mathsf{H}\to \tilde\mathsf{H}$, $\xi\mapsto (\xi,0)$. For $x,y\in \mathsf{M}$ we have
    \begin{align*}
        \langle \varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2},\alpha(\iota(x))\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}\iota(y)\rangle&=\langle \mathcal F(W)(\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}y^\ast),\mathcal F(\tilde T) \mathcal F(W)x\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}\rangle\\
        &=\langle \varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}\iota(y^\ast),\iota(\Phi(x))\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}\rangle\\
        &=\langle \varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2},\Phi(x)\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}y\rangle.
    \end{align*}
    Hence a minimal Stinespring dilation of $\Phi$ is given by $\mathsf{H}_\Phi=\overline{\mathrm{span}}\{\alpha(\iota(x))\varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}\iota(y)\mid x,y\in \mathsf{M}\}$, $V=\mathcal F(W)$ and $\pi=\alpha\iota$. Since $\alpha|_\mathsf B=\operatorname{id}_\mathsf B$, $\mathcal F(\tilde T)^\ast\colon \mathsf{H}_\Phi\to \mathcal F(_\mathsf B\tilde \mathsf{H}_\mathsf B)$ is a right $\mathsf B$-module map such that $\mathcal F(\tilde T)^\ast \alpha(\iota(x))=\iota(x)\mathcal F(\tilde T)^\ast$. Hence ${_\mathsf{M}(\mathsf{H}_\Phi)_\mathsf B}\subset {_\mathsf{M}\mathcal F(_\mathsf B\tilde \mathsf{H}_\mathsf B)_\mathsf B}$, where the left action of $\mathsf{M}$ on $\mathcal F(_\mathsf B\tilde \mathsf{H}_\mathsf B)$ is given by $\iota$. Finally,
    \begin{equation*}
        _\mathsf{M}\mathcal F(_\mathsf B\tilde \mathsf{H}_\mathsf B)_\mathsf B\cong {_\mathsf{M}}\mathcal F(_\mathsf B\mathsf{H}_\mathsf B)\otimes_\mathsf B(L^2(\mathsf B)_\mathsf B\oplus \mathsf{H}\otimes_\mathsf B\mathcal F(_\mathsf B\mathsf{H}_\mathsf B)_\mathsf B).\qedhere
    \end{equation*}
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- corollary-11: body_md -->
\label{cor:solidity of free Araki-Woods with finitely generated bimodule}
    If $(\mathsf{H},\mathcal J,(\mathcal U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R})$ is a Tomita correspondence over $\mathsf B$ that satisfies the condition from Lemma~\ref{lem:rel_compact_Fock_space}, then $\Gamma(_\mathsf B\mathsf{H}_\mathsf B,\mathcal J,(\mathcal U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R})$ is stably solid relative to $\mathsf B$ along $\omega$ and is $\omega$-solid relative to $\mathsf B$ for any $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$.
<!-- end corollary-11 -->
<!-- corollary-12: body_md -->
\label{cor:solidity of free Araki-Woods}
    If $(\mathsf{H},\mathcal J,(\mathcal U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R})$ is a Tomita correspondence over $\mathsf B$ such that $\mathsf{H}=\oplus_{j\in \Lambda}\mathsf{H}_j$ for some countable set $\Lambda$, where each $\mathsf{H}_j$
is invariant under the left and right actions, the
Tomita conjugation, and the modular group, and satisfies the condition from Lemma~\ref{lem:rel_compact_Fock_space},
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
    then $\Gamma(_\mathsf B\mathsf{H}_\mathsf B,\mathcal J,(\mathcal U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R})$ is stably solid relative to $\mathsf B$ along $\omega$ and is $\omega$-solid relative to $\mathsf B$ for any $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$.
<!-- end corollary-12 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
We assume that $\Lambda$ is infinite. Choose positive real numbers $\lambda_j\geq 1$ such that $\lambda_j\to\infty$ as $j\to\infty$, and define the operator $S:\mathsf{H}\to \mathsf{H}$ and $(T_t:\mathsf{H}\to\mathsf{H})_{t\geq 0}$ by 
\[
S_{|_{H_j}}=\lambda_j,\qquad T_t=e^{-tS}.
\]
For $t>0$, each  ${T_t}_{|_{\mathsf{H}_j}}$ is a relatively compact $\mathsf B$-bimodule map because $\mathsf{H}_j$ is finitely generated as right $\mathsf B$-module, and since $e^{-t\lambda_j}\to 0$, it follows that  $T_t$ is compact relative to $\mathsf B$.  Moreover, it is clear that $T_t$ commutes with the Tomita data, and $\|T_t\|\leq \sup_{j\in \Lambda}e^{-t\lambda_j}<1$.

On the Fock module,
\[
\mathcal F(T_t)=1_{L^2(B)}\oplus\bigoplus_{n\geq1}T_t^{\otimes_B n}
\]
is relatively compact by Lemma~\ref{lem:rel_compact_Fock_space}. Second quantization gives a GNS-symmetric QMS by the construction of Proposition \ref{prop:construction of QMS on Free-Araki Woods}. As above, consider the subspace $\mathfrak A$ spanned by  $\mathsf B_\infty {\varphi_\mathsf B}^{1/2}$ and $\bigcup_{n\geq 1}\{\xi_1\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\xi_n\mid $ where
\[\xi_k\in \bigcap_{z\in \mathbb C}\operatorname{dom}(\mathcal U_z)\cap\operatorname{dom}(S^{1/2}),\,\,\,\mathcal U_z\xi_k\in\mathcal D(\mathsf{H},{\varphi_\mathsf B})\cap \mathcal D^\prime(\mathsf{H},{\varphi_\mathsf B})\]
for all $z\in\mathbb{C},1\leq k\leq n$ and define the linear map $ \delta_S\colon \mathfrak A\to \mathcal F(_\mathsf B\mathsf{H}_\mathsf B)\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\mathsf{H}\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\mathcal F(_\mathsf B\mathsf{H}_\mathsf B),$
by $\delta|_{B_\infty \varphi_\mathsf B^{1/2}}=0$ and
\begin{equation*}
    \delta_S(\xi_1\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\xi_n)=\sum_{k=1}^n \underbrace{\xi_1\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B \dots}\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\xi_{k-1}}_{\in \mathcal F(_\mathsf B\mathsf{H}_\mathsf B)}\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\underbrace{S^{1/2}\xi_k}_{\in \mathsf{H}}\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\underbrace{\xi_{k+1}\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\dots\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\xi_n}_{\in\mathcal F(_\mathsf B\mathsf{H}_\mathsf B)}.
\end{equation*}
Again as above, one shows that $\delta_S$ is a $\varphi$-modular derivation such that $\mathcal{F}(T_t)=e^{-t{\delta_S}^\ast\bar\delta_S}$. Note that the codomain $\mathcal F(_\mathsf B\mathsf{H}_\mathsf B)\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\mathsf{H}\otimes_{\varphi_\mathsf B}\mathcal F(_\mathsf B\mathsf{H}_\mathsf B)$ of $\delta_S$ carries a natural structure of an $\langle \mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$-$\langle \mathsf{M},\mathsf B\rangle$ correspondence.
The results now follow from the general results of Section \ref{sec:solidity}.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- corollary-13: body_md -->
If $(U_t)_{t\in \mathbb R}$ is a one-parameter group of orthogonal transformations on a separable Hilbert space $\mathsf{H}_{\mathbb R}$ such that $U_t$ is almost-periodic, then $\Gamma(U_t,\mathsf{H}_{\mathbb R})$ is stably solid along $\omega$ and is $\omega$-solid for any $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$
<!-- end corollary-13 -->
<!-- example-5: body_md -->
Let $G$ be a discrete group and let $\pi\colon G\to O(H)$ be a strongly continuous orthogonal representation. If $(U_t)_{t\in \mathbb R}$ is a strongly continuous almost periodic orthogonal group on $H$ that commutes with $\pi(g)$ for all $g\in G$, then we obtain a Gaussian action $g\mapsto \Gamma(\pi(g))$ on the free Araki--Woods factor $\Gamma(H^\mathbb C,J,(U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R})$, where $H^\mathbb C$ is the complexification of $H$ and $J$ is the induced complex conjugation.

    Let $\mathsf B=L(G)$ and $\mathsf{H}=H^\mathbb C\otimes \ell^2(G)$ with left and right actions given by $\pi_l^\mathsf{H}(\lambda(g))=\pi(g)\otimes \lambda(g)$ and $\pi_r^\mathsf{H}(\lambda(g)^\mathrm{op})=1\otimes\rho(g^{-1})$. One can turn $\mathsf{H}$ into a Tomita correspondence over $(\mathsf B,\tau_G)$ by defining $\mathcal J(\eta\otimes 1_g)=J\eta\otimes 1_{g^{-1}}$ and $\mathcal U_t=U_t\otimes 1$. As shown in \cite[Proposition 6.7]{KW25}, there exists an isomorphism $\alpha\colon \Gamma(H,J,(U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R})\rtimes_{\Gamma(\pi)} G\to \Gamma(_\mathsf B\mathsf{H}_\mathsf B,\mathcal J,(\mathcal U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R})$ that preserves the canonical copies of $\mathsf B$.
    
    Since $(U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R}$ is almost periodic, we have $H^{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{i\in I}H_i^{\mathbb C}$ with $H_i^{\mathbb C}$ a finite-dimensional eigenspace of $(U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R}$. If $(\xi_k^{(i)})_{1\leq k\leq n_i}$ is an orthonormal basis of $H_i^\mathbb C$, then $(\xi_k^{(i)}\otimes 1_e,1_\mathsf B)_{1\leq k\leq n_i}$ is a finite quasi-orthonormal basis of $\mathcal D(H_i^\mathbb C\otimes \ell^2(G),\tau_G)$. Thus $\Gamma(\mathsf{H},J,(U_t))\rtimes_{\Gamma(\pi)}G$ is stably solid relative to $L(G)$.
<!-- end example-5 -->
<!-- lemma-30: body_md -->
\label{lem:automorphisms}
For $g,h,k\in\Gamma$,
\begin{align}
&\alpha_{gh}^{-1}\circ\alpha_g
 =\mathrm{Ad}(\kappa_{g,h})\circ\alpha_h^{-1},\label{eq:intertwiner}\\
&\alpha_h^{-1}\circ\alpha_g^{-1}
 =\mathrm{Ad}(\kappa_{g,h}^*)\circ\alpha_{gh}^{-1}.\label{eq:inverseaction}\\
 &\kappa_{g,hk}\kappa_{h,k}
 =\alpha_{ghk}^{-1}(\nu_{g,h})\kappa_{gh,k}.\label{eq:blockcocycle}
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-30 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
Compose \eqref{eq:action}  on the left with $\alpha_{gh}^{-1}$.
Since any automorphism $\theta$ on $\mathsf B$ and $v\in\mathcal{U}(\mathsf B)$ satisfies
$\theta\circ\mathrm{Ad}(v)=\mathrm{Ad}(\theta(v))\circ\theta$, this gives
\[
\alpha_{gh}^{-1}\circ\alpha_g\circ\alpha_h
 =\alpha_{gh}^{-1}\circ\mathrm{Ad}(\nu_{g,h})\circ\alpha_{gh}
 =\mathrm{Ad}(\alpha_{gh}^{-1}(\nu_{g,h}))
 =\mathrm{Ad}(\kappa_{g,h}).
\]
Compose on the right with $\alpha_h^{-1}$ to obtain
\eqref{eq:intertwiner}. The second identity easily follows from the first by composing by $\alpha_g^{-1}$ from the right.

Finally we  prove \eqref{eq:blockcocycle} by applying the 
automorphism $\alpha_{ghk}$ to both sides.
On one hand,
the twisted action identity \eqref{eq:action} for the pair $(g,hk)$  yields
\begin{equation*}
\alpha_{ghk}\circ\alpha_{hk}^{-1}
 =\mathrm{Ad}(\nu_{g,hk}^*)\circ\alpha_g
\end{equation*}
which further yields
\begin{align*}
\alpha_{ghk}\bigl(\kappa_{g,hk}\kappa_{h,k}\bigr)
 &=\nu_{g,hk}\,
       \alpha_{ghk}\bigl(\alpha_{hk}^{-1}(\nu_{h,k})\bigr)\\
 &=\nu_{g,hk}\,
       \nu_{g,hk}^*\alpha_g(\nu_{h,k})\nu_{g,hk}\\
 &=\alpha_g(\nu_{h,k})\nu_{g,hk}.
\end{align*}
On the other hand, apply \eqref{eq:inverseaction} with $(g,h)$ replaced by $(gh,k)$ to obtain:
\[
\alpha_k^{-1}\circ\alpha_{gh}^{-1}
 =\mathrm{Ad}(\kappa_{gh,k}^*)\circ\alpha_{ghk}^{-1}.
\]
Composing on the left with $\alpha_{ghk}$  gives
\begin{equation*}
\alpha_{ghk}\circ\alpha_k^{-1}\circ\alpha_{gh}^{-1}
=\mathrm{Ad}(\alpha_{ghk}(\kappa_{gh, k}^\ast)) =\mathrm{Ad}(\nu_{gh,k}^*).
\end{equation*}
Consequently,
\begin{align*}
\alpha_{ghk}\bigl(\kappa_{gh,k}\alpha_k^{-1}(\kappa_{g,h})\bigr)
&=\nu_{gh,k}\,
  (\alpha_{ghk}\circ\alpha_k^{-1}\circ\alpha_{gh}^{-1})(\nu_{g,h})\\
&=\nu_{gh,k}\,\nu_{gh,k}^*\nu_{g,h}\nu_{gh,k}\\
&=\nu_{g,h}\nu_{gh,k}\\
&=\nu_{g,h}\alpha_{ghk}(\kappa_{gh,k}).
\end{align*}
Thus we obtain
\eqref{eq:blockcocycle}.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- proposition-19: body_md -->
If we set $d_g(t)=\left(\frac{D(\varphi\circ\alpha_g)}{D\varphi}\right)_t $ for $g\in \Gamma, t\in\mathbb R$ to be the Connes cocycle derivative, then the modular objects of $\tilde\varphi$ satisfy
\begin{align}
\Delta_{\tilde\varphi}^{i t}(\delta_g\otimes\xi)
 &=\delta_g\otimes d_g(t)\Delta_\varphi^{i t}\xi,
       \label{eq:Delta}\\
J_{\tilde\varphi}(\delta_g\otimes\xi)
 &=\delta_{g^{-1}}\otimes
       \nu_{g,g^{-1}}^*V_gJ_{\mathsf B}\xi,
       \label{eq:J}
\end{align}
for $\xi\in L^2(\mathsf B)$. Moreover,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sigma}
\sigma_t^{\tilde\varphi}(a)=\sigma_t^\varphi(a),\quad
\sigma_t^{\tilde\varphi}(u_g)=u_gd_g(t),\quad a\in\mathsf B.
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-19 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
We have $\tilde\varphi^{1/2}=\delta_e\otimes\varphi^{1/2}$ and $u_ga\tilde\varphi^{1/2}=\delta_g\otimes a\varphi^{1/2}$ for $g\in \Gamma, a\in \mathsf B$, so the set
    \[\mathcal{D}_0:=\text{span}\{\delta_g\otimes a\varphi^{1/2}; g\in \Gamma, a\in \mathsf B\}\] lies in the domain of the Tomita operator $S_{\tilde\varphi}$ such that
\begin{align*}
S_{\tilde\varphi}(\delta_g\otimes a\varphi^{1/2})
 =S(u_ga\tilde\varphi^{1/2})
 =(u_ga)^*\tilde\varphi^{1/2}
 =\delta_{g^{-1}}\otimes
       \nu_{g,g^{-1}}^*\alpha_g(a^*)\varphi^{1/2}.
\end{align*}
By Kaplansky's density theorem, the algebraic crossed product is strongly-$\ast$ dense in $\mathsf{M}$ with
bounded approximants. Hence for every $x\in\mathsf{M}$, finite Fourier
sums $x_i$ can be chosen so that both
$x_i\tilde\varphi^{1/2}\to x\tilde\varphi^{1/2}$ and $x_i^*\tilde\varphi^{1/2}\to x^*\tilde\varphi^{1/2}$.
It follows that $\mathcal D_0$ is a core for $S_{\tilde\varphi}$.

For each $g\in \Gamma$, write $H_g=\delta_g\otimes L^2(\mathsf B)$ so that we have $\ell^2(\Gamma)\otimes L^2(\mathsf B)=\oplus_{g\in \Gamma}H_g$. Put
\[
\psi_g=\varphi\circ\alpha_g,\quad
D_g=\Delta_{\psi_g,\varphi},\quad
C_g=\nu_{g,g^{-1}}^*V_gJ_{\mathsf B}.
\]
where $D_g$ is the operator $S_{\psi_g,\varphi}^\ast S_{\psi_g,\varphi}$. Here the relative Tomita operator $S_{\psi_g,\varphi}$ is the closure of the map 
$a\varphi^{1/2}\mapsto a^*\psi_g^{1/2}, a\in\mathsf B,$
and has polar decomposition
$S_{\psi_g,\varphi}=J_{\mathsf B} D_g^{1/2}$ (see \cite[Proposition 10.3]{Hia21}).
The operator $C_g$ is antiunitary on $L^2(\mathsf B)$ and $\mathsf B\varphi^{1/2}$ is a core for each $D_g^{1/2}$, by the
definition of the relative Tomita operator.
Since $V_g$ is the standard implementation of $\alpha_g$,
$V_g\psi_g^{1/2}=\varphi^{1/2}.$
Thus
\begin{align*}
\nu_{g,g^{-1}}^*\alpha_g(a^*)\varphi^{1/2}
 =\nu_{g,g^{-1}}^*V_g(a^*\psi_g^{1/2})=\nu_{g,g^{-1}}^*V_gS_{\psi_g,\varphi}(a\varphi^{1/2})
 =C_gD_g^{1/2}(a\varphi^{1/2}).
\end{align*} 
Thus we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Sclosed}
S_{\tilde\varphi}(\oplus_{g\in \Gamma}\delta_g\otimes \xi_g)=\oplus_{g\in \Gamma}\delta_{g^{-1}}\otimes C_gD_g^{1/2}\xi_g
\end{equation}
with domain
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{dom}(S_{\tilde\varphi})=\left\{\oplus_{g\in \Gamma}\delta_g\otimes\xi_g\in \ell^2(\Gamma)\otimes L^2(\mathsf B): \xi_g\in \operatorname{dom}(D_g^{1/2}), \sum_{g\in \Gamma}\|D_g^{1/2}\xi_g\|^2<\infty\right\}
\end{equation*}
We now compute the formula for the adjoint $S_{\tilde\varphi}^\ast$.
Because $C_g$ is antiunitary and $D_g^{1/2}$ is self-adjoint,
$
(C_gD_g^{1/2})^*=D_g^{1/2}C_g^{-1}.
$
The adjoint reverses the direction of the original block:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Sstarblock}
S^*(\delta_{g^{-1}}\otimes\eta)
 =\delta_g\otimes D_g^{1/2}C_g^{-1}\eta,
\quad C_g^{-1}\eta\in\operatorname{dom}(D_g^{1/2}).
\end{equation}
More explicitly, $\oplus_{g\in \Gamma}\delta_g\otimes\eta_g\in\operatorname{dom}(S^*)$ precisely when
\[
C_g^{-1}\eta_{g^{-1}}\in\operatorname{dom}(D_g^{1/2})\quad\text{for every }g,
\quad
\sum_g\|D_g^{1/2}C_g^{-1}\eta_{g^{-1}}\|^2<\infty.
\]
For $\xi\in\operatorname{dom}(D_g)$, formulas \eqref{eq:Sclosed} and
\eqref{eq:Sstarblock} now give
\begin{align}\label{eq:directsum}
S_{\tilde\varphi}^*S_{\tilde\varphi}(\delta_g\otimes\xi)
 =S_{\tilde\varphi}^*(\delta_{g^{-1}}\otimes C_gD_g^{1/2}\xi)
 =\delta_g\otimes D_g^{1/2}C_g^{-1}C_gD_g^{1/2}\xi
 =\delta_g\otimes D_g\xi.
\end{align}
This shows that
\[\Delta_{\tilde\varphi}=\oplus_{g\in \Gamma}{1\otimes D_g}\]
with
\[
\operatorname{dom}(\Delta_{\tilde\varphi})=\left\{\oplus_{g\in \Gamma}\delta_g\otimes\xi_g\in \ell^2(\Gamma)\otimes L^2(\mathsf B):
\xi_g\in\operatorname{dom}(D_g)\;\forall g,\;\sum_g\|D_g\xi_g\|^2<\infty\right\}.
\]
Define the antiunitary $C$ on $\ell^2(\Gamma)\otimes L^2(\mathsf B)$ by
\[
C(\delta_g\otimes\xi)=\delta_{g^{-1}}\otimes C_g\xi.
\]
Equations \eqref{eq:Sclosed} and \eqref{eq:directsum} say that
$S_{\tilde\varphi}=C\Delta_{\tilde\varphi}^{1/2}$. Since $\Delta_{\tilde\varphi}$ is nonsingular,
uniqueness of the polar decomposition yields $C=J_{\tilde\varphi}$,
proving \eqref{eq:J}. In particular $C^2=1$.
Functional calculus in \eqref{eq:directsum} gives
\[
\Delta_{\tilde\varphi}^{i  t}(\delta_g\otimes\xi)
 =\delta_g\otimes D_g^{i  t}\xi.
\]
The Connes derivative identity
$d_g(t)=D_g^{i  t}\Delta_\varphi^{-i  t}
$
implies $D_g^{i  t}=d_g(t)\Delta_{\varphi}^{i  t}$ (see \cite[Proposition 10.11]{Hia21}),
which proves \eqref{eq:Delta}.
Finally, we have
\begin{align*}
\sigma_t^{\tilde\varphi}(u_ga)\tilde\varphi^{1/2}
 &=\Delta_{\tilde\varphi}^{i  t}(u_ga\tilde\varphi^{1/2})\\
 &=\delta_g\otimes d_g(t)\Delta_\varphi^{i  t}(a\varphi^{1/2})\\
 &=\delta_g\otimes d_g(t)\sigma_t^\varphi(a)\varphi^{1/2}\\
 &=u_gd_g(t)\sigma_t^\varphi(a)\tilde\varphi^{1/2}.
\end{align*}
and the separating property of $\tilde\varphi^{1/2}$ yields \eqref{eq:sigma}.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- remark-9: body_md -->
If $\varphi\circ\alpha_g=\varphi$ for every $g$, then $d_g(t)=1$
and $\Delta_{\tilde\varphi}^{i t}=1\otimes\Delta_\varphi^{i t}$.
The cocycle factors in the formulas for the modular operators are still present.
<!-- end remark-9 -->
<!-- lemma-31: body_md -->
The operator  $\partial_{|_{\mathfrak{A}}}$ is a $\tilde\varphi$-modular derivation.
<!-- end lemma-31 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
For any $g\in\Gamma, \xi\in L^2(\mathsf B),\eta\in \mathsf{K}$, one verifies that $\delta_g\otimes\xi\otimes\eta\in \operatorname{dom}(\partial^\ast)$ such that 
\[\partial^\ast(\delta_g\otimes\xi\otimes\eta)=-i\langle c(g),\eta\rangle \delta_g\otimes\xi\]
This shows that $\operatorname{dom}(\partial^\ast)$ is dense in $L^2(\mathsf{M})\otimes\mathsf{K}$; hence $\partial$ is closable and so is $\partial_{|_\mathfrak{A}}$. This also shows that
\[\partial^\ast\bar\partial(\delta_g\otimes\xi)=\|c(g)\|^2\delta_g\otimes\xi,\;\;g\in \Gamma,\xi\in L^2(\mathsf B).\]
Since $\partial\subseteq \overline{\partial_{|_\mathfrak{A}}}$, it suffices to show the required derivation formulas  for $\partial$ restricted to the set $\text{span}\{\delta_g\otimes b\varphi^{1/2}; g\in \Gamma, b\in \mathsf B\}$. The following identities are straightforward to verify:
\begin{align*}
    \partial\circ\Delta_{\tilde\varphi}^{it}=\mathcal{U}_t\circ\partial,\;\;\partial\circ J_{\tilde\varphi}=\mathcal{J}\circ\partial,\;\;t\in\mathbb R.
\end{align*}
To show the derivation rule, we first write the following formula for $g,h\in \Gamma$ and $a,b\in \mathsf B$: 
\begin{align*}
   u_g a\tilde\varphi^{1/2}u_hb&=u_ga(\delta_h\otimes J_{\mathsf B} b^\ast J_{\mathsf B} V_h^\ast\varphi^{1/2})=\delta_{gh}\otimes\kappa_{g,h}\alpha_h^{-1}(a)J_{\mathsf B} b^\ast J_{\mathsf B} V_h^\ast\varphi^{1/2}\\
   &=(\delta_g\otimes a\varphi^{1/2})u_h b=\delta_{gh}\otimes \kappa_{g,h} J_{\mathsf B} b^\ast J_{\mathsf B} V_h^\ast a\varphi^{1/2}
\end{align*}
On the one hand, we have 
\begin{align*}
    \partial(u_g a\tilde\varphi^{1/2}u_hb)=i\delta_{gh}\otimes\kappa_{g,h}\alpha_h^{-1}(a)J_{\mathsf B} b^\ast J_{\mathsf B} V_h^\ast\varphi^{1/2}\otimes c(gh).
\end{align*}
On the other hand, a similar calculation of the left-right action on $\mathsf{H}$ yields  
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{J}&(u_h b)^\ast\mathcal{J}
\partial(u_ga\tilde\varphi^{1/2})+u_ga\partial(\tilde\varphi^{1/2}u_hb)
    \\
    &= \mathcal{J}(u_h b)^\ast\mathcal{J}(i\delta_g\otimes a\varphi^{1/2}\otimes c(g))+iu_ga(\delta_h\otimes J_{\mathsf B} b^\ast J_{\mathsf B} V_h^\ast\varphi^{1/2}\otimes c(h))\\
    &=i\delta_{gh}\otimes \kappa_{g,h} J_{\mathsf B} b^\ast J_{\mathsf B} V_h^\ast a\varphi^{1/2}\otimes c(g)+i\delta_{gh}\otimes \kappa_{g,h}\alpha_h^{-1}(a)J_{\mathsf B} b^\ast J_{\mathsf B} V_h^\ast\varphi^{1/2}\otimes\pi_g c(h)\\
    &=i\delta_{gh}\otimes\kappa_{g,h}\alpha_h^{-1}(a)J_{\mathsf B} b^\ast J_{\mathsf B} V_h^\ast\varphi^{1/2}\otimes c(gh).
\end{align*}
So we get $ \partial(u_g a\tilde\varphi^{1/2}u_hb)=\mathcal{J}(u_h b)^\ast\mathcal{J}
\partial(u_ga\tilde\varphi^{1/2})+u_ga\partial(\tilde\varphi^{1/2}u_hb)$ which is precisely the required derivation condition.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- lemma-32: body_md -->
\label{lem:multiplies of positive definite functiona}
    Let $f:\Gamma\to\mathbb C$ be a normalized positive definite function. Then  the assignment $\Phi:u_ga\mapsto f(g)u_ga$ for $g\in \Gamma, a\in \mathsf B$ extends to a normal $\tilde\varphi$-preserving unital completely positive map on $\mathsf B\rtimes\Gamma$. If $f$ is real-valued, then $\Phi$ is $\tilde\varphi$-GNS symmetric.
<!-- end lemma-32 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
Define the bounded operator $\Phi$ on $\mathbb B(\ell^2(\Gamma)\otimes L^2(\mathsf B))$ by 
    the assignment 
    \[\langle\delta_h\otimes\eta,\Phi(T)(\delta_g\otimes\xi)\rangle=f(hg^{-1})\langle\delta_h\otimes\eta,T(\delta_g\otimes\xi)\rangle,\] 
    $g,h\in \Gamma, \eta,\xi\in L^2(\mathsf B), T\in \mathbb B(\ell^2(\Gamma)\otimes L^2(\mathsf B))$
 One easily verifies that $\Phi$ is a normal completely positive map using the positive-definiteness of $f$.  A simple calculation shows that $\Phi$ maps $\mathsf{M}$ to itself and we have $\Phi(u_ga)=f(g)u_ga$ for $g\in \Gamma, a\in \mathsf B$. The condition $f(e)=1$ implies that $\Phi$ is $\tilde\varphi$-preserving. When $f$ is real-valued,  the $L^2$-implementation of $\Phi$ on $L^2(\mathsf B\rtimes\Gamma)$ is self-adjoint implying that $\Phi$ is GNS symmetric.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- theorem-15: body_md -->
\label{prop:omega solidity in crossed products}
    Let $\Gamma$ be a countable discrete group admitting a cocycle $c$ into a representation weakly contained in the left regular representation, and let $(\alpha,\nu)$ be a cocycle  action on a von Neumann algebra $\mathsf B$ with separable predual. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                        
    If $c$ is proper, then $\mathsf B\rtimes\Gamma$ is stably solid and $\omega$-solid relative to $\mathsf B$ for $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$.
<!-- end theorem-15 -->
<!-- corollary-14: body_md -->
Let $\Gamma$ be a countable discrete group admitting a proper 1-cocycle $c$ into a representation weakly contained in the left regular representation, let $\nu:\Gamma\times\Gamma\to \mathbb T$ be a 2-cocycle, and let $\omega\in\beta\mathbb N\setminus\mathbb N$. Then $L_\nu(\Gamma)$ is $\omega$-solid and stably solid in the sense of \cite{DV25}.
<!-- end corollary-14 -->
